News.title: Glam nurse-turned-drug mule who was caught smuggling £160k of cannabis into UK KEEPS medical licence
News.content:
BLUNT DECISION Glam nurse-turned-drug mule who was caught smuggling £160k of cannabis into UK KEEPS medical licence

A GLAM nurse who was caught smuggling £160,000 worth of cannabis into the UK has been allowed to keep her medical licence.

Levi Whalley – an Instagram influencer – faced being struck off from her day job as a nurse after she was caught with friend Sophie Bannister trying to enter the country with 32kg of the drug.



The pair claimed they were on their way back from a “shopping trip” in New York when Border Force officials found the huge stashes in their luggage at Birmingham Airport.

Whalley’s suitcase alone contained 38 packages of the class B drug, weighing 19kg.



The 32-year-old, who has almost 45,000 followers on Instagram and posts photos of her jet-setting across the world, escaped a jail sentence but was told by the nursing regulator that it would be pushing for her to be struck off.

But now, Whalley has avoided losing her nursing licence at a Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) tribunal.



The single mum, from Blackburn, Lancashire, has instead escaped with a 12 month suspension.

The NMC ruled stripping her of her licence would be “unduly punitive” and said she was experiencing a “very difficult” time when she tried to smuggle the drugs.



She has been working as a botox and filler injector – running her own beauty business – since she was suspended and has not been able to practise as a nurse since then.

The NMC heard that Whalley had “always wanted to be a nurse from a very young age”.

She has worked in healthcare since she was 18, qualifying as a nurse in 2019 – she then got a job at an eye clinic and was promoted to a management role.

Whalley later started running her own clinics as a “nurse injector” before working in an ophthalmology department in the private sector until she was suspended in December 2023.

That month, it was heard she was arrested at Birmingham Airport after what she claimed was a “three-day shopping trip to New York” with Bannister.



Her phone and passport were seized after her arrest, and she was referred to the NMC by West Midlands Police.

Whalley was convicted of drug smuggling at Blackburn Magistrates Court, Lancashire, in February 2025, and in April 2025 she was given a 16 month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, at Preston Crown Court.

The NMC tribunal heard she was facing “very difficult circumstances” in her personal life at the time, which have “now positively resolved”.



The NMC panel, summarising Whalley’s evidence at the tribunal said Whalley’s friend had “offered for you to go to New York for the weekend for free and that you and your friend would have to bring back some watches to the UK.”

“You explained that you just wanted escapism after everything you had been through, and you thought it would be good for your wellbeing,” the panel continued.

“You did not think about the consequences, you made a very irrational decision in the moment.

“You explained that it suddenly hit you an hour before your flight home and after you received the suitcase; you panicked and did not want to go ahead but received messages threatening your home and family.

“It was then at Birmingham airport you were arrested. You explained that when you got sentenced, you felt you had lost everything.



“All the hard work you had done for your nursing career had been thrown away over this very stupid decision. You have so much regret for what you have done.

“You have not worked as a nurse for two and a half years and you would like to return to nursing in a medical ward as this would give you the chance to build up your nursing skills and work alongside a team.

“You accepted that the conviction was as a result of poor decision making and you can understand how the public would see this.”

She said that as part of her sentence she did 80 hours of unpaid work, which she completed at a charity shop.

Whalley added that she was in a “very different stage of life now” as she is a mother and looks at the world “differently”.



The NMC panel decided against striking her off the register and cited her engagement with authorities and “willingness to learn and grow as a person and strengthen your character”.

“In the specific and unusual circumstances surrounding your offending, the panel concluded that your conviction was not fundamentally incompatible with remaining on the register,” the panel concluded.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It therefore concluded that a striking-off order would be disproportionate and unduly punitive in the circumstances.”

The added a 12 month suspension was “appropriate in this case to mark the seriousness of her conviction”.

DOG ATTACK Dogwalker injured after being attacked by ‘out of control’ XL Bully-type hound as CCTV released in hunt for man & woman

A DOGWALKER has been injured in a suspected XL-bully attack, as cops hunt a man and a woman in their 60s.

Police were called to Normanton Park, Derby, on Thursday, July 16, after receiving reports that a dog had attacked a woman.

It was reported that a large, XL-bully type hound had lunged towards the woman as she walked her own dog in the park.

She was knocked over – causing an injury to her back, before a couple came and pulled the attacking mutt away.





The couple are described as being in their 60s, the man was wearing a black turban, a white shirt and grey trousers and had a beard.

The woman had long dark hair worn in a plait, and wore a white t-shirt and grey trousers.

Derbyshire Police is now appealing for information that may assist them with their investigation into the attack.

News.title: Please don’t bomb us, beg Russians in plea to Ukraine drone pilots on warehouse roofs amid blitz on ‘Russia’s Amazon’
News.content:
RUSSIANS have painted a desperate plea to Ukrainian drone pilots to spare their warehouse as Volodymyr Zelensky’s troops continue to blitz Russia’s Amazon equivalent.

It comes after Ukraine targeted Russian online seller Wildberries with a devastating series of strikes, dubbed “long-range sanctions”.



The huge online marketplace has had a fifth of its warehouses attacked since July 18.

Now Ozon, another huge online seller, fears it could be the next target.



The e-commerce giant painted an enormous message on the roof of one of its largest logistics centres, begging Ukrainians to leave it intact.

It read: “This is not Wildberries. Fly past.”



The warehouse is in Nizhny Novgorod, around 800miles deep into Russia.

Head of defence company Fire Point Denys Shtilerman said the retailer would not be spared, telling Ukrainian media: “First we will finish off Wildberries, and then we will destroy Ozon too.”

Ukraine has been putting its foot on Moscow’s neck with a series of strikes crippling the regime’s biggest e-commerce platform.

The devastating strikes on warehouses owned by Wildberries – the country’s biggest online marketplace – have shattered Russian morale.



A huge hub in Penza was set ablaze after an overnight strike as another key logistics centre in Sarapul was hit last night.



And the drone onslaught has thrown Russian daily life into chaos – wiping out local businesses overnight and suffocating small-scale trade.

Ukraine also blitzed an oil facility in Perm last night.

It comes as Nato scrambled fighter jets after a suspected Russian missile crossed into Polish airspace.

The incident came during a deadly overnight assault from Vladimir Putin – which saw two girls, aged five and 12, among eight killed in Ukraine.

Smoke was seen rising from Poland‘s Lublin region where a 33ft-wide crater was reportedly found after air raid sirens sounded across the area.



Polish operational command said an “unidentified object” crashed in its territory after multiple missiles were spotted flying close to the border.

One, feared to be a Kh-101 missile launched from a Russian bomber, entered Polish airspace at around 3.30am.

How Ukraine’s cunning tactic to blitz ‘Russia’s Amazon’ could deal fatal blow to Putin’s regime BY Harvey Geh AFTER weeks of blitzing Vladimir Putin’s oil depots with state-of-the-art drones, Ukraine has now shifted its crosshairs to Russia’s Amazon. In another bid to bring the tyrant to the negotiating table, Kyiv is putting its foot on Moscow’s neck with a series of strikes crippling the regime’s biggest e-commerce platform. The despot could be staring down the barrel of a mutiny by the time key elections come round in September if Ukraine keeps its foot on the gas and Moscow continues to struggle against aerial assaults, experts say. Russia expert Mark Galeotti told The Sun: “The Ukrainians have been extraordinarily and unexpectedly successful, and this is slowly grinding away… at support for the regime bit by bit.” And John Foreman CBE, former UK Defence Attaché to Russia, said: “The strategy… is to inflict pain inside Russia, inside the occupied territories, inside Crimea, to bring home the cost of war back to Russians.” Russia analyst Natia Seskuria told us: “It’s a very smart strategy from the Ukrainian side… it will have a significant impact on Russian households.” She added: “This is something new and something that we haven’t seen before, but I think the message is still the same in terms of making the war extremely costly for Russia.” READ MORE HERE

Residents of Targowisko reported a loud explosion as the missile crashed and burned in a field.

Poland’s operational command said in a statement: “At 3.29am, the closest approach was made by one of the objects.



“At 3.40am, an unidentified object was detected in Polish airspace moving westward. An F-16 fighter jet was dispatched to the area to identify and intercept it.

“At 3.46am, before a clear identification could be made, the object disappeared from radar detection.

“To verify and ultimately confirm the radar’s technical indications, an Mi-24 helicopter was dispatched to the area of the last detection.

“The helicopter crew located the probable crash site of the object in an undeveloped area near the town of Tarnawa-Kolonia in the Lublin Voivodeship.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The crash site sits four miles from Otrocz, which is around 56 miles from the Ukrainian border.



Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said: “Clarification is now underway as to what kind of object fell near the locality of Tarnawa-Kolonia.”

News.title: Hilarious moment impatient dog jumps in driver’s seat and beeps horn to hurry its owner up
News.content:
A FUNNY video shows an impatient dog honking a car’s horn as it waits for its owner who has gone shopping.

The fluffy white pet is seen with its paws on the wheel of the red Fiat 500 blasting out the sound.



Business owners and passers by gathered in the street to see who was behind the angry commotion.

But their concern turned to laughter when they realised it was a dog at the wheel.



The funny moment was captured in Bovey Tracey in Devon on Wednesday morning.

The mutt’s owner had left the car on a single yellow line while she carried out errands.

The pet then jumped in the drivers’ seat and started beeping before it was filmed jumping back onto the passenger seat.

Video showed the middle aged female owner return to the motor before driving off.

James Stafford, 36, a painter and decorator, said: “At first I thought it was an angry driver, then I turned and saw this dog leaning on the horn with its tongue lolling out.

“I think it was a cockerpoo or something.

“It was hilarious. It obviously got bored of waiting and rather than bark for attention it was clever enough to start beeping the horn.”

News.title: Brit’s final movements in Athens before body found in suitcase – as haunting texts to family AFTER she died are revealed
News.content:
INVESTIGATORS are desperately piecing together the final movements of a Brit found dead inside a suitcase in an abandoned building in Athens.

Haunting text messages were reportedly sent to the family of victim Elisabeth Ross, 38, for two weeks after her mysterious death as cops try to track down who was using her phone.



The Scottish woman’s mobile was only turned off on Wednesday morning after reports of the body being found made global headlines, local media claim.

The suitcase was first discovered on July 18 by a homeless man who noticed a foul smell coming from inside 7 Evelpidon Street.



But experts believe the woman was likely dumped in the neighbourhood of Kypseli and was not found for around seven days.

After speaking to the victim’s dad, Greek officials then learned that the woman’s phone had been active for two weeks.



Do you know more about the case? Please contact georgie.english@the-sun.co.uk or Whatsapp 07353 096414

From July 15 to 29, several messages had been sent to Elisabeth’s relatives pretending to be the Brit, according to news site Flash.

They reportedly said that she needed some time by herself and wanted to be left alone for a while.

​The last trace of the phone was found in the capital of Athens before it was switched off.



Police have managed to piece together several key dates regarding Elisabeth’s disappearance and tragic end.

She arrived in Greece on June 29 after flying out from Edinburgh, according to the Hellenic Police.

Officers from Greece’s main federal law enforcement agency say they are looking into the possibility of whether she was accompanied by another person or if someone was waiting for her at the airport.



Elisabeth is believed to have stayed at a friend’s house in Attica before leaving on July 15.

Phone records show she called a friend shortly after heading off.

Three days later, her body was found at 7 Evelpidon Street in the neighbourhood of Kypseli shortly after 1pm.



There were no visible wounds on the body or any clear signs of a struggle, police confirmed.

Police are urgently looking into those crucial three days to try and uncover where Elisabeth went and who she encountered.

The friends who hosted her during her stay have been questioned and confirmed she left under her own power and appeared to be in good spirits.

She said she was going to visit some American friends in Kypseli.

Autopsy results are yet to be confirmed to determine an exact time and cause of death.



Cops suspect Elisabeth may have been lured to the abandoned location by a homeless person who “left her in the state she was found,” an official told The Times.

A homeless man reportedly first found the victim inside the building which had been deserted for at least two years.

He entered a room inside and found the suitcase on the ground.

The suitcase did not belong to the victim, police have confirmed.

Officers initially couldn’t identify the woman as she reportedly had no identification on her, sparking Interpol to help with DNA testing.



The body was identified as Elisabeth on July 27 as Greek police launched a murder probe two days later.

Police spokesperson Konstantina Dimoglidou told Skai TV that authorities were treating the incident “as a criminal act, given how the body was found”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another Greek officer told The Sun: “To find a foreign national dead in a suitcase here in the heart of Athens is a first.

“In the history of Greek British relations, it is unprecedented.”

News.title: Hundreds evacuated from UK holiday park in dead of night and major incident declared as fire crews tackle wildfire
News.content:
HUNDREDS of holidaymakers were evacuated in the middle of the night as a wildfire raced towards a popular seaside resort.

Around 200 caravans were evacuated as a major incident was declared at National Trust site Dunwich Heath in Suffolk.



The fire broke out just after 5.30pm yesterday evening and has been spreading rapidly overnight, with 90 firefighters scrambling to the scene.

Crews successfully evacuated Coastguard Cottages, Mount Pleasant Farm and Cliff House Holiday Park and around 200 caravans at the holiday park in the dead of night.



It comes as families flock to the area to enjoy the summer holidays on the Suffolk coast.

There is currently an “exceptional” wildfire risk covering the UK, as 14 crews in Suffolk work to protect the buildings and control the blaze.



Locals have been urged to avoid the area and keep their windows and doors closed as the wind sends billows of smoke into the sky.

Have you been affected by this? Contact araminta.plumptre@thesun.co.uk

Suffolk Fire and Rescue said the inferno, which has burnt through around 14 football pitches of heathland, is now a major incident “due to the size and complexity”.



The fire is around 2.5miles from Sizewell B nuclear power station and is not thought to be a threat to the station currently, but the service said it is a “live and dynamic situation.”

Station manager Dan Davis added that the blaze was a “large-scale, wind-driven forestry fire” and that 70 firefighters are still tackling it this morning.

The wildfire is close to the RSPB Minsmere nature reserve and heading towards St James’ Church.

Anyone displaced has been told to attend Westleton Village Hall at 08:00am for further updates.

Speaking to the BBC, Justin North – one of around 60 displaced people at the hall – said he was woken to hammering on the door of his holiday cottage.



He was told to “go immediately” with no time to pack and had to sleep in his car with his wife before the evacuation centre opened.



Other holiday-goers, including families, pensioners and people with disabilities, were housed with villagers overnight and instructed not to return to their homes.

Just hours before the fire broke out, Suffolk joined half the country by officially declaring a drought.

The areas are East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the whole of London, Thames Valley, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight, Devon and Cornwall, the West Midlands, and Wessex – covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire and Gloucestershire.

The record for the longest drought in 1976 is on the brink of being broken.

Some areas of the UK have had no rain for 43 days, closing in on the 1976 record of 48 days.



The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) had issued an amber heat-health alert for the East Midlands, the East, South East and London which is in place until 9am this morning.

The mercury is forecast to hit 28C today as several major wildfires continue to burn across the UK.

Fire services responded to 706 wildfires this year across England and Wales, 200 of those were recorded in the last fortnight, the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) said.



A grass fire devoured 30 acres in Romford, east London, yesterday.

Also in London, 100 firefighters rushed to tackle another blaze in Rainham, covering four acres.

In Scotland, crews said they were making “significant progress” tackling a wildfire in the Cairngorms that broke out two weeks ago.

Across Europe holiday hotspots have been set ablaze by wildfires.

More than 360,000 people in France and Spain have been forced to flee their homes as fires stoked by arid, tinderbox conditions and strong winds continue to rage.



The Met Office said a cooler change was on the way, with temperatures expected to fall much closer to average across much of the UK

Deputy Chief Forecaster Mark Sidaway said: “The forecast is showing potential for more rain than much of the UK has experienced over the last few weeks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“However, it looks as though amounts of rain for many will be fairly modest, and won’t balance out the shortfall that we have recorded this summer.

“It’s still possible that some areas of the south will miss out and see little or no rainfall.”

News.title: Nato scrambles fighter jets after ‘Russian missile hits Poland’ as children among 8 dead in Ukraine strikes
News.content:
NATO scrambled fighter jets after a suspected Russian missile crossed into Polish airspace.

The incident came during a deadly overnight assault from Vladimir Putin – which saw two girls, aged five and 12, among eight killed in Ukraine.



Smoke was seen rising from Poland‘s Lublin region where a 33ft-wide crater was reportedly found after air raid sirens sounded across the area.

Polish operational command said an “unidentified object” crashed in its territory after multiple missiles were spotted flying close to the border.



One, feared to be a Kh-101 missile launched from a Russian bomber, entered Polish airspace at around 3.30am.

Residents of Targowisko reported a loud explosion as the missile crashed and burned in a field.



Poland’s operational command said in a statement: “At 3.29am, the closest approach was made by one of the objects.

“At 3.40am, an unidentified object was detected in Polish airspace moving westward. An F-16 fighter jet was dispatched to the area to identify and intercept it.

“At 3.46am, before a clear identification could be made, the object disappeared from radar detection.

“To verify and ultimately confirm the radar’s technical indications, an Mi-24 helicopter was dispatched to the area of the last detection.

“The helicopter crew located the probable crash site of the object in an undeveloped area near the town of Tarnawa-Kolonia in the Lublin Voivodeship.”



The crash site sits four miles from Otrocz, which is around 56 miles from the Ukrainian border.

Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said: “Clarification is now underway as to what kind of object fell near the locality of Tarnawa-Kolonia.”

Prime Minister Donald Tusk added: “It looks like it was a Russian missile, but we don’t have 100 per cent certainty exactly what kind of missile.”



It comes as Ukraine faced another night of drone and missile attacks at the hands of Russia.

President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned Russia was preparing for a “massive attack”.

Two girls, aged five and 12, were among six killed in a village near the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih.

A ballistic missile is said to have hit a home and sparked a fire, a local official said.

Eight others were injured, including two children.



Zelensky said: “A Russian missile strike in Radushne, Dnipropetrovsk region, killed parents and three children.

“Two more children were rescued alive from the rubble. A regular residential building was completely destroyed by a ballistic missile.

“Dozens of ordinary homes, civilian businesses, and infrastructure facilities have been destroyed and damaged.



“This attack involved more than 70 missiles, and a significant number of them were ballistic. More than 280 attack drones were also used.”

In the capital Kyiv, one person died as multiple blazes broke out in three buildings, according to mayor Vitali Klitschko.

The mayor of Poltava also said one person has died after a Nova Poshta postal terminal had been attacked.

Several other cities were also reported as being under attack by relentless Russian bombing.

It comes as Putin is reportedly set to mobilise half a million men for his war in Ukraine – as the tyrant vows to be “bolder” despite suffering huge losses.



Zelensky said Putin is planning to mobilise the 500,000 troops after legislative elections scheduled for September.

The move is said to be in response to Kyiv’s recent attacks on Russia’s economy.

Ukraine has been putting its foot on Moscow’s neck with a series of strikes crippling the regime’s biggest e-commerce platform.

The devastating strikes on warehouses owned by Wildberries – the country’s biggest online marketplace – have shattered Russian morale.

Over the last few days, Ukraine has destroyed or damaged a series of complexes belonging to the largest e-commerce site in Russia.



A huge hub in Penza was set a ablaze after an overnight strike as another key logistics centre in Sarapul was hit last night.

And the drone onslaught has thrown Russian daily life into chaos – wiping out local businesses overnight and suffocating small-scale trade.

Ukraine also blitzed an oil facility in Perm last night.

News.title: 19 countries have pulled out of World Cup as UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino boycott
News.content:
19 countries have pulled out of World Cup as UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino boycott

A potential World Cup boycott is being considered following revelations this week

View 5 Images Gianni Infantino is under major fire for his FIFA sale plans (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

UEFA are threatening to boycott the World Cup if Gianni Infantino goes forward with his plans to sell off part of FIFA. The governing body's president is considering selling shares to private investors to create a £15billion ($20bn) subsidiary.

‌



UEFA will hold an emergency meeting at 2pm today to ward off FIFA's attempt to launch a new commercial company with outside investment. Infantino wants to sell off more than 20% of the FIFA Forward Enterprise and raise £3.16bn ($4.2bn).

‌



It is reported that these plans were not raised during meetings with football associations in New York the night before the World Cup final. UEFA said in a statement: "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously.

‌



"So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott READ MORE :

UEFA holding emergency meeting over World Cup boycott to stop FIFA villain Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

‌



In the wake of this, Mirror Football examines previous occasions when nations have withdrawn from the World Cup.

Uruguay - 1934

The reigning world champions were due to head to the second edition of the tournament in 1934, having triumphed four years earlier. However, they withdrew in protest after several European sides refused to travel to South America for the 1930 World Cup in Uruguay.

The 1934 World Cup remains the only edition where the defending champions failed to take part.

‌



Austria - 1938

View 5 Images Austria were unable to compete at the 1938 World Cup (Image: RDB/ullstein bild via Getty Images)

Among the favourites heading into the 1938 tournament, Austria were unable to compete after Nazi forces annexed the nation at the time. Several Austrian stars joined up with the German squad, though standout player Matthias Sindelar refused to represent the Nazi-led side.

India - 1950

On the sole occasion India reached the World Cup, they chose not to attend. In 1950, the Asian nation progressed to the finals by default following withdrawals during qualifying.

‌



Their absence was attributed to travel costs, training time and squad selection difficulties.

15 African teams - 1966

View 5 Images The 1966 World Cup was actually boycotted by 15 nations (Image: Rolls Press/Popperfoto via Getty Images)

The 1966 tournament holds fond memories for England, but one often-overlooked element is the absence of African nations. The continent's teams boycotted the qualifying stages in protest against FIFA's decision to grant just one place for the African, Asian and Oceania confederations combined.

‌



These nations include: Algeria, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Gabon, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Libya, Mali, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, Sudan, Tunisia and the United Arab Republic (now called Egypt).

Chile - 1974

In 1974, the world watched as a qualified nation came close to boycotting the World Cup on political grounds. During the intercontinental play-off between Chile and the Soviet Union, the latter refused to participate in the fixture in protest against Augusto Pinochet's dictatorship.

Pinochet had overthrown the socialist government, turning Chile from a former Soviet ally into an enemy. As a result, the Chilean players took to the pitch alone, with captain Francisco Valdes scoring into an empty net before the match was abandoned.

‌



World Cup protests and issues

View 5 Images There have been more recent protests (Image: ANP via Getty Images)

In more recent times, outright boycott threats have been few and far between, though tensions did surface during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. All 32 qualified nations took part in the tournament, yet some players staged demonstrations concerning alleged human rights abuses and the host nation's controversial stance on LGBT rights.

Captains from seven European nations - England, Wales, the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Germany and Switzerland - had planned to wear "OneLove" armbands promoting inclusivity.

‌



View 5 Images Seven European nations planned a protest in 2022 (Image: Alain Pitton/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

They abandoned the plan just hours before their matches after FIFA threatened to issue automatic yellow cards to any player wearing the unauthorised armband.

Meanwhile, in March this year – ahead of the 2026 World Cup – following escalating regional conflict and U.S./Israeli airstrikes, Iranian sports minister Ahmad Donyamali publicly declared that the national team would not participate in the tournament "under any circumstances."

Article continues below

However, Iran did not officially withdraw and instead petitioned FIFA to have their matches relocated to co-host nation Mexico. This request was rejected and Iran ultimately played in the tournament, although they were subject to travel restrictions and were forced to travel in and out of the USA on the day of each match.

News.title: George Cottrell 'transferred $2m to his mum' days before her Reform UK donations
News.content:
George Cottrell 'transferred $2m to his mum' days before her Reform UK donations

The party’s finances have come under intense scrutiny over recent weeks, and the Metropolitan Police are looking at whether donors might have got around restrictions on political funding

View 2 Images George Cottrell is a close ally of Nigel Farage (Image: Getty Images)

A convicted fraudster is said to have transferred more than two million dollars to his mother before she donated to Reform UK in 2024.

‌



George Cottrell is reported to have sent the massive sum to his mum Fiona Cottrell, with part of it then going to Nigel Farage’s party.

‌



Mr Cottrell is a convicted criminal who provided funding for Nigel Farage’s security and staffing in the year before he was elected.

‌



The party’s finances have come under intense scrutiny over recent weeks, and the Metropolitan Police are looking at whether donors might have got around restrictions on political funding.

Public thinks Nigel Farage battling with Count Binface to avoid scrutiny, poll finds READ MORE :

View 2 Images Nigel Farage pictured with George Cottrell in 2020 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ms Cottrell is thought to have received one deposit of 1.4 million dollars and then two further installments of more than 300,000 dollars each.

‌



She allegedly told bankers the money came from her son, when she was asked about the deposits.

Ms Cottrell received the money around 24-72 hours before she made a donation either to Reform UK directly or to the company Britain Means Business, according to The Guardian.

The Met Police is understood to be probing two donations totaling £500,000 from Britain Means Business, a company directed by Reform’s Deputy Leader Richard Tice, in 2024.

‌



Electoral Commission records show the two donations of £250,000 were given to Reform by the company two days apart.

The money was paid to his company by Reform donor Ms Cottrell, Mr Tice has previously outlined.

Reports suggest she gave £1 million to Britain Means Business in June 2024, and half of that money was then given to Reform.

Article continues below

Bridget Phillipson, the Labour Party chairwoman, urged Reform UK leaders to “stop ducking questions and come clean about who’s bankrolling the party”.

She said: “This is incredibly serious for Nigel Farage and Reform. If these reports, which George Cottrell is yet to deny, are true, then the ultimate source of these donations to Reform was Cottrell himself."

A Reform UK spokesman said: “Reform takes pride in its stringent vetting of donations and always ensures that the Electoral Commission guidelines on donations, as set out in the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, are strictly followed, as has been the case with all donations.”

News.title: Suffolk wildfire live: Massive blaze at Dunwich Heath as hundreds evacuated
News.content:
Holidaymakers evacuated overnight from a caravan site in the path of the flames in Dunwich Heath, Suffolk, as people living nearby are warned to keep windows closed

A major incident has been declared as a wildfire rages at a National Trust site, with hundreds of people evacuated from a caravan site.

Firefighters rushed to the scene of the blaze in Dunwich Heath, near Sizewell B nuclear plant, on Wednesday evening. The forest has been managed by the National Trust since 1968 and is a well known local beauty spot.

The fire broke out at roughly 5:30pm with the cause unclear. Crews successfully evacuated 200 approximately caravans at the holiday park in the dead of night as the fire showed no signs of stopping. Emergency services remain at the scene.

Fire crews have advised the public should avoid the area, keep roads clear for emergency vehicles, and keep windows and doors closed if smoke is nearby.

The heath is about three miles from Sizewell B nuclear plant and 30 miles north-east of Ipswich.

News.title: Europe wildfires live: Crete inferno amid warning 'all of continent' could burn
News.content:
Europe's emergency response chief has warned that wildfires could engulf the whole continent as fires ravage parts of the Greek island of Crete

A new wildfire is ravaging the Greek island of Crete as Europe's emergency response chief warned the entire continent could be engulfed.

Wildfires on the south of the island are currently burning "out of control on all fronts", with firefighting aircraft unable to be deployed due to strong winds. Three firefighters in Greece have been killed while tackling flames in Crete and Mani.

Maria Zuber, head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre, said wildfires could engulf "all of Europe" within days. Her warning comes as intense blazes also rage in France, Spain, and Portugal.

"Italy will face risk at the beginning of August, and we will need to see what will happen with the Iberian Peninsula, because if (it is) there as well, we will have all Europe on fire," she said.

News.title: 'Significant danger' warning as UKHSA confirms 2,877 UK deaths
News.content:
'Significant danger' warning as UKHSA confirms 2,877 UK deaths

An update was released on Thursday morning

View 3 Images Heatwaves cause what are known as 'excess deaths' (Image: Pexels)

A new update has confirmed that 2,877 people have died from a 'significant danger' in the UK this summer.

‌



The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said on Thursday morning that it estimates there were 2,877 heat-associated deaths during two notable periods of hot weather in May and June 2026, almost double the figure reported annually for 2025. An estimated 753 deaths were associated with the May heat episode between May 24 and 27 and a further 2,124 with the June heatwave between June 21 and 28. While these figures remain interim, they are already approaching the annual record reported by UKHSA in 2022, it confirmed.

‌



The June heatwave lasted for eight days and triggered a red heat-health alert. This was only the second time the highest level of alert has been issued in England, reflecting the exceptional temperatures recorded, the UKHSA said.

‌



Both May and June also broke Met Office monthly temperature records for England, with 31.5C recorded at Kew Gardens on May 26 and 37.7C recorded at Lingwood, Norfolk on June 26. The UKHSA said "these findings demonstrate the importance of the heat-health alerting system, delivered in partnership with the Met Office, which provides early warning when temperatures are likely to have significant impacts on health and wellbeing".

View 3 Images Extreme heat has put pressure on health services (Image: PA)

It added that heatwaves occurring earlier in the season could have a greater impact due to people, communities and services having less time to adapt to the warmer conditions. To support partners in preparing and responding to these events, UKHSA recently published the updated Adverse Weather and Health Plan for England for 2026 to 2027.

‌



It added: "Based on the interim data, it is likely that 2026 could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record, surpassing the 2,985 recorded in 2022. While the figures are indicative of the public health impact of the heatwaves, these numbers should be regarded as interim. UKHSA will publish finalised figures in the annual report in early 2027."

Dr Ross Thompson, principal environmental public health scientist at UKHSA and author of the report, said: “These figures highlight the significant danger that very hot weather can pose to people’s health. This is particularly true for those who are more vulnerable including older adults and people with underlying medical conditions.

“While the figures are interim, they suggest that, if we experience more periods of hot weather this summer, we could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record. As the climate becomes warmer, we can expect periods of hot weather to become longer, more frequent and more extreme. That’s why it’s vital that individuals, communities and systems are prepared to deal with higher temperatures, and to ensure those most vulnerable to the heat are protected.”

‌



View 3 Images The NHS has been experiencing winter-like pressure, the health secretary said (Image: PA Wire/PA Images)

Health and Social Care Secretary, Yvette Cooper, said: “The sweltering heat has had a serious impact this summer on people’s health and on our NHS. For many years, we have been used to winter pressures in our NHS and the need to support those who are vulnerable in the coldest weather. But now we are seeing the summer heat have an increasingly serious impact on the health of thousands of people, and on the pressures facing our NHS too.

"My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves in recent months. And my heartfelt thanks go to the NHS staff, care workers and emergency responders who have worked tirelessly through these exceptionally busy and challenging months to protect and care for people affected by the heat.

Article continues below

“As we move through the summer, it is so important for people to be able to look out for their health and help those who are more vulnerable to the hot conditions. Please don't hesitate to seek help if you're worried about your own wellbeing, or anyone else's. A little care could make a lifesaving difference.”

News.title: Tragedy as boy, 12, dies after plunge through barn roof in front of horrified pals
News.content:
Tragedy as boy, 12, dies after plunge through barn roof in front of horrified pals

Jaxon Robert Hubery, from Bishop Auckland in County Durham, was rushed to Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle but passed away from his injuries

View Image The boy was rushed to Royal Victoria Infirmary but tragically died from his injuries (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

A boy has plunged to his death after falling through the roof of a barn, with his parents pleading for children to be kept away from the area.

‌



The tragedy happened at a barn at Woodhouses near Bishop Auckland in County Durham in front of the boy's horrified friends. He has been named as 12-year-old Jaxon Robert Hubery, of Bishop Auckland.

‌



Durham Constabulary said the fall took place shortly before 2.45pm on Friday, July 24, as the boy was with a group of friends. Jaxon sustained serious injuries and was taken to Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle but died on Tuesday afternoon.

‌



The boy's family have pleaded with other parents to keep their children away from the area, as an investigation was launched by the police alongside the Health and Safety Executive (HSE).

In a statement, the force said: "A boy has sadly died after falling through the roof of a barn. Shortly before 2.45pm on Friday (July 24) police were alerted to an incident in which a child had fallen through the roof of a barn at Woodhouses, near Bishop Auckland.

‌



"The boy, who was with a group of friends at the time, sustained serious injuries and was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary, in Newcastle, for treatment. Tragically, he died [on Tuesday] afternoon (July 28) as a result of his injuries.

"He has been named as 12-year-old Jaxon Robert Hubery, of Bishop Auckland. His family would like to thank those who have given them love and support throughout the last few days.

"They are also urging other parents to keep their children away from the area. Police are working alongside the Health and Safety Executive to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident."

Article continues below

Among other aspects, the HSE investigates potential risks of incidents against the public and workers which could "harm many people".

News.title: Mum-of-three thought she was just tired from dream holiday - but it was something far worse
News.content:
Mum-of-three thought she was just tired from dream holiday - but it was something far worse

Laura Ann Fitt had to wait more than a year before she was handed a devastating diagnosis by doctors - who explored many possible conditions she could have been suffering from

View 6 Images Laura Ann Fitt spent mnts waiting for a diagnosis before she learned she had a terminal illness (Image: Laura Ann Fitt / SWNS)

A Brit mum who believed she'd pulled a muscle after walking 20,000 steps on holiday was devastated to discover she was actually suffering from a terminal disease.

‌



Laura Ann Fitt, 40, a mum-of-four from Ashfield in Nottinghamshire, believed her active holiday in New York City caused her frequent stumbles and falls. She was convinced she had overexerted herself during the dream trip with her husband in July 2025, and had been caught out by the city's uneven pavements.

‌



But her troubles only continued when she returned home, and she continued catching her left foot, while also developing persistent muscle twitches above her left knee.

‌



Jesy Nelson’s secret heartache behind victory in getting all babies tested for SMA READ MORE :

View 6 Images Mum Laura put her difficulties down to an active dream holiday (Image: Laura Ann Fitt / SWNS)

Colleagues believed the symptoms were caused by a magnesium deficiency, but it continued after taking supplements - leading her to see her GP on August 19 last year. As she underwent months of testing, she progressed from using a walking stick to requiring a wheelchair to cover longer distances.

She didn't discover what was truly wrong with her until she completed a full year of tests, with doctors exploring possible causes including multiple sclerosis, brain tumours, strokes, and functional neurological disorders.

‌



The mum finally received a devastating diagnosis of motor neurone disease (MND) on July 4, less than a month after her 40th birthday.

View 6 Images Laura said the waiting and not knowing was worse than the diagnosis (Image: Laura Ann Fitt / SWNS)

Laura said she struggled hardest with the "limbo period" leading up to her diagnosis, having clung to hope that her condition wasn't life-limiting in some way. She said: "I had a couple of falls, tripping and things, but I thought maybe I had just overexerted myself or that I was walking on un-even ground.

‌



"I'd been waiting for a diagnosis so long that I really knew what it was going to be. That limbo period of not knowing was harder than actually knowing.

"Once you know, you can get your ducks in a row. All the 'what ifs' and 'maybes' are so stressful because you cling to hope that it isn't something life-limiting." MND is a life-limiting and sadly terminal disease that damages the brain's nerves and spinal chord. It has an average life expectancy of between two to three years.

View 6 Images Laura said her son has struggled to understand she is dying (Image: Laura Ann Fitt / SWNS)

‌



Laura, who has worked in healthcare since she was 18, wasn't overly concerned by her initial symptoms. It was at her neurology appointment in January that she became suspicious, and asked the neurologist if it could be MND.

She said: "They said 'No, we don't think so' but we need to rule it out. The electromyography (EMG) [a nerve test] couldn't confirm it, but it couldn't rule it out either." Her symptoms continued to get worse, and by May this year she needed a wheelchair to attend appointments, and doctors explained that with MND, it often takes time before a clearer picture develops.

A lumbar puncture ruled out autoimmune conditions shortly before her 40th birthday in June. A repeat EMG on July 2 confirmed all of her fears, with Laura receiving her diagnosis 48 hours later.

‌



View 6 Images Laura was devastated to discover she was suffering from MND (Image: Laura Ann Fitt / SWNS)

Her first thoughts went to her husband and children. Her 15-year-old son Alex is blind and autistic. She said: "I thought, how are they going to cope without me? I don't want to leave them, but I don't have a choice. The thought of not seeing them grow up, get married, have children, and being there to support them is just really difficult.

"My son Alex has developmental issue so he doesn't really understand what's happening, or death as a concept. When you ask him 'what's wrong with mummy?' he says 'mummy's got spaghetti legs."

‌



Now, she wants to spend as much quality time as possible with her husband and children, with Alex being one of four siblings alongside Harmonie, 14, Gabriella, 16, and Ellis, 19.

View 6 Images Active mum Laura now hopes to raise money to enjoy her last days with her family (Image: Laura Ann Fitt / SWNS)

She also hopes to raise awareness of the early symptoms that people may overlook and tell people to advocate for themselves when they experience persistent symptoms. As both a nurse, and now a patient, Laura hopes sharing her story will help others. She said: "The nurse in me wants to get the message out there. If sharing my story helps even one person get answers sooner, then it's worth it."

Article continues below

She has set up a GoFundMe campaign so she can put together £3,000, money she needs to enjoy the remaining years of her life with her family.

News.title: Morrisons' freebie that anyone in the UK can claim until September
News.content:
Morrisons' freebie that anyone in the UK can claim until September

The offer is running in every Morrisons store across the country with a cafe

View 2 Images Morrisons is offering something to all customers for free - no questions asked (Image: Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)

According to research by Morrisons, almost half (48%) of parents have admitted they have been forced to skip meals entirely just to make ends meet and ensure their child does not go without during the summer holidays. Most often, breakfast is the number one thing cut from the menu.

‌



In an effort to help families make their money go further this summer, Morrisons is offering a free deal to everyone until September, no questions asked. Families visiting their local Morrisons Café can enjoy a free Kellogg’s Breakfast.

‌



The deal was recently highlighted by ITV's This Morning regular and money specialist Jordon Cox. In an Instagram post to remind families of the deal, he said: "If you’re struggling over the school summer holidays - head down to a Morrisons Cafe.

‌



"Anyone can claim this, although the deal is focused on helping people who may be struggling to afford keeping the kids fed/entertained over the summer. So maybe only use it if you need it!"

To redeem the offer, ask for at the cafe till for a 'Kellogg's Breakfast', and staff will give you the items included in the deal for free. Alternatively, people can use touch-screen ordering kiosks in certain stores with those installed, as there will be a specific option for the free breakfast.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Matt Khan, senior trader for Morrisons Café, said: "We know that when schools close for the summer, family budgets get stretched to the absolute limit. Losing that daily routine makes it a challenging time for parents and grandparents.

"By teaming up with Kellogg’s, we want to take some of that pressure off by offering a welcoming space where families can sit down and enjoy a healthy, proper breakfast together, completely free of charge." Andrew Ridge, social impact manager at Kellogg’s, added that the cereal company is " incredibly proud to partner with Morrisons" to support families left feeling the pinch.

On top of the Kellogg’s Breakfast offer, Morrisons popular Kids Eat Free offer will also continue to run in all of its Cafés. This all-day offer allows families to enjoy a free meal and drink for one child aged 16 or under when they purchase an adult main meal costing over £5 from The Breakfasts and The Classics menu.

Article continues below

View 2 Images Morrisons and Kellogg’s have brought back the school holiday ‘Breakfast Clubs’ to all stores with cafes (Image: Morrisons)

What is included in the Kellogg's offer?

Families can take advantage of the offer at Morrisons Cafés nationwide throughout the 2026 school holidays (running from June 29 to September 6). Limited to one per person per day, Morrisons has partnered with Kellogg's to offer a simple yet balanced breakfast option that won't eat into a family budget this summer.

When redeeming the offer, customers receive a complete breakfast, including a portion pack of Cornflakes (24g) or Rice Krispies (22g) with milk or a milk alternative (125ml). On top of this, the offer includes a portion of fruit (usually an apple or banana).

News.title: How the UK's extreme heat is shifting the conversation about air-con
News.content:
Against him stand those who think Britain's hostility to cooling has curdled into a type of masochism.

David Lawrence, of the Centre for British Progress think tank, puts it plainly: we don't tell people to insulate their homes in winter and then skip the radiators. So why insist shade and shutters are enough in summer?

He points out that air conditioning is standard now in offices, hotels and shops, "but we don't expect it for schools and hospitals - which is kind of odd, because those are places where millions of people are every day", and where heat measurably dents concentration, learning and health.

This dispute over the pros and cons of the technology is becoming political.

Some London councils, following a planning "cooling hierarchy", say lowâenergy ways of keeping homes cool should be prioritised over air conditioning and in a small number of cases have ordered property owners to remove them; the Conservative front bench calls it "dark ages" miserabilism; other MPs and political commentators demand an "air-con revolution".

Since April, in England and Wales the Boiler Upgrade Scheme has offered Â£2,500 towards a reversible air-air heat pump: a machine that warms a home in winter and cools it in summer. It is, in all but name, Britain's first air-conditioning subsidy - but it is badged as a heat pump, and only worth a third of the Â£7,500 for a heating-only model.

Such has been the silence around this grant, that in its first month only around 45 households claimed it. By comparison, the numbers claiming a heating-only model ran into the thousands.

In Scotland homeowners can also get a Â£7,500 grant for a heat pump via its Home Energy scheme - but for air-air versions that could offer cooling there is no funding at all. And in Northern Ireland there is no universal heat pump grant offered for households.

Under the terms of the England and Wales scheme, some people cannot apply at all. It is closed to social housing and newbuilds - which many argue shuts out the very people most exposed.

Take Woolwich, in south-east London, where a resident called Keisha says her top-floor flat reaches 43C in a heatwave.

She calls the building "inhumane"; she and around twenty neighbours in Canada Court and Clifton Lodge are taking their landlord, the housing association PA Housing, to court over homes they say are unfit to live in.

News.title: Thousands evacuated in Crete as European wildfires continue to rage
News.content:
Thousands of people have been evacuated on the Greek island of Crete as wildfires fanned by strong winds menace tourist resorts and villages.

Around 8,000 people were evacuated overnight in Rethymno, where gusts have reached 125km per hour.

The evacuations came after two firefighters died on the island on Wednesday after getting trapped near Krya Vrysi, and a third died near the Peloponnese port town of Gytheio.

Greece is among many European countries facing devastating fires and droughts as the continent experiences extreme high temperatures.

Forecasters warn fire-prone conditions will spread towards the centre of Europe this week, with Greece and Turkey among places most affected.

News.title: Israel building new land barriers in Gaza and displacing families
News.content:
"We've been displaced from place to place, and now we have nowhere left to go," says Umm Mohammed al-Shawish.

She is desperately searching for somewhere to live after Israel moved yellow concrete blocks that mark out where it controls in the Gaza Strip.

Families living in al-Tuffah in northern Gaza woke on Monday to find the blocks had been moved westwards into the centre of Salah al-Din road, a key north-south route through Gaza.

Nearby, an Israeli flag was flying on top of an earth barrier around 3m (10ft) tall.

The al-Shawish family home was destroyed during the war. On Sunday, they had to flee again after the Israeli military called to warn of an attack on a nearby building. Their only shelter was a tent, which was torn apart by the strike.

"We are going to die here," Mohammed al-Shawish said. "Death is better than humiliation. No-one is standing with us."

Under the terms of the US-brokered ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas last October, Israel agreed to withdraw its forces from across Gaza to a designated demarcation - the Yellow Line.

The deal was meant to leave Israel in temporary control of the area behind the Yellow Line - equating to 53% of Gaza's territory. However, the Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu recently said the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) controlled more than 60%. In May, he said publicly that his "directive" was to move to 70%.

Hamas accuses Israel of violating the October ceasefire agreement by moving the Yellow Line westwards. A senior Israeli government official said Israel rejected Hamas's claims outright. The BBC was told: "IDF deployments and security lines are operational measures taken to protect Israeli citizens and prevent Hamas from rebuilding its terror army. Israel will continue to act against any ceasefire violations."

The Israeli military initially marked the Yellow Line with concrete blocks, before moving some markers further into Gaza. But Israel has now constructed a network of barriers, having started soon after the ceasefire. The barriers now stretch more than 42km (26 miles) and cover 85% of Israel's Yellow Line, with the longest section already 13.8km (8.5 miles).

Experts have told the BBC that the earthworks suggest Israel is planning for a long occupation of the strip. In some areas the earth barrier effectively moves the de facto "border" - the Yellow Line - deeper into Gaza, further increasing the deadly no-go zone for Gazans.

One section of the embankment near the al-Mawasi camp is more than 1.5km beyond where the Yellow Line was originally mapped. Another section in Khan Younis is positioned more than 500m over it.

News.title: Three children among eight dead in Russian strikes on Ukraine, officials say
News.content:
Eight people, including two boys and a girl, have died during a Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine, according to local officials.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had launched more than 70 missiles and over 280 drones at the country overnight. The worst attack was near Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih.

Dozens of "ordinary homes, civilian businesses and infrastructure facilities" were destroyed or damaged in the attack, he added.

The attack comes after Zelensky met US President Donald Trump in Washington DC this week to urge the US to grant Ukraine a licence to produce Patriot interceptor missiles, which he says are crucial to the country's defence.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said an object that crashed into a field in eastern Poland in the early hours of Thursday was probably a Russian missile.

Ukraine's acting Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha had earlier said a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile had "crossed into Poland as part of Russia's massive strike against Ukraine, violating Nato airspace".

News.title: Virtual job interviews don't let people shine, says Burnham
News.content:
Bosses should not rely so heavily on virtual job interviews when hiring as they don't capture candidates' personality and passion, Andy Burnham has said.

"One thing I really don't like is this culture now of interviewing via Zoom or Teams," the prime minister told a careers podcast, adding: "How does a young person shine in that situation?"

With more than one million 16 to 25-year-olds not in work or education, and vacancies at a five-year low, firms are increasingly turning to AI to sift through applications and choosing online interviews over in-person.

But some young people have told the BBC the experience of applying for hundreds of jobs and never hearing back is "robotic and brutal".

It comes as some 89% of UK recruiters say they are planning to use more AI in the hiring process this year, according to data from Linked In.

Speaking to former political adviser Jimmy McLoughlin on his podcast Jimmy's Jobs of the Future, Burnham said he was concerned that the use of technology was not making recruitment processes "fairer".

"How do you get over some of your personality, your passion?" he asked, referring to virtual interviews. "It seems to me to then work against people who have that side to their character and work for those who are just giving the more formulaic answer.

"I do worry about that and I've seen that in relation to my kids and their situation."

News.title: Beauty Pie founder on how she dropped out of university and built five businesses
News.content:
Kilgore didn't always know she wanted to be an entrepreneur but growing up she saw first-hand the stress that financial insecurity could cause.

"I remember deciding at eight-years-old that when I was my parents' age, I would never want to be stressed about my electric bill," she says.

That desire shaped her approach to work and risk. "I knew that working for other people wouldn't necessarily give me the freedom I wanted and at least when you are an entrepreneur, the risk is your own."

She didn't begin with a grand business plan - she moved from Canada to New York to study at Columbia University and her tuition plan fell through so she had to get a job to support herself.

"You can't sit around thinking: 'What am I going to do? You have to survive. I knew I had to use the skills I had to support myself and then I would figure it out."

She started working as a personal trainer and taking beauty classes in the evening.

"What ended up transpiring was that I was quite good at the beauty industry job," she says and eventually she dropped out of university to pursue a career in it.

News.title: How serial killer James Desborough preyed on vulnerable homeless men
News.content:
"He's really off his head. He doesn't care... he is kamikaze."

Those were Claudio Aquilino's words during a 999 call the day before he disappeared.

He was frightened and told police he wanted nothing to do with a crime he believed was about to be committed by a man called James Desborough.

About 12 hours later on 18 April 2025, CCTV captured Aquilino with Desborough in a Newquay pub.

It was the last time Aquilino was seen alive.

Police found his burnt remains in a stream months later as they searched woodland owned by Desborough near Sticker, a small village in south Cornwall.

By then another man - Daniel Coleman - had also vanished after last being seen in Desborough's company. His remains were found nearby.

Desborough denied murdering either man, claiming they had died separately in a "series of unfortunate circumstances", but yesterday he was convicted of both of their murders after a seven-week trial at Winchester Crown Court.

He was given a whole life prison sentence with no chance of parole.

On the same day police revealed they are looking into four unexplained deaths at the homeless shelter that had housed him.

News.title: The Chinese robot army transforming the UK's retail industry
News.content:
Every time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.

Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.

At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.

Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.

By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.

Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.

Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.

News.title: Cooler conditions on way for parts of UK - but still no rain for drought-hit areas
News.content:
Cooler conditions and some rain are on the way for parts of UK on Thursday into the weekend, as a cold front moves into the UK.

However, with more than half of England and parts of Wales officially in drought, the coming days are unlikely to bring any rain to the driest areas of the country.

The latest UK heatwave peaked on Wednesday with temperatures soaring to 35.2C at Writtle in Essex. It was the hottest day for more than two weeks, when 35.2C was also recorded in Cotton in the Elms, Derbyshire, on 10 July.

It did not reach the highs experienced last month, when a new UK June temperature record of 38C was set at Lingwood in Norfolk on the 26th, which was also the hottest day of the year so far.

Last month's record was provisionally reported as 37.7C but the Met Office announced on Wednesday a new figure of 38.0C following a verification process.

It comes after drought was declared across more than half of England on Wednesday as hot, dry weather takes its toll on the country's water supplies.

The Environment Agency (EA) announcement covered much of central, eastern and southern England, and was a public sign that further restrictions on water use might follow.

It added that the impacts are already being felt, including low river flows, early harvests and high risk of wildfires. More than 20 million people are already under hosepipe bans.

North Wales and the Upper Severn river basin entered drought conditions last week, Natural Resources Wales said.

Scotland does not declare drought but monitors "water scarcity". Some parts of eastern Scotland are in the most extreme category of "significant scarcity", according to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency.

Northern Ireland is not currently in drought.

News.title: Arrest after firearm discharge outside mosque
News.content:
A man has been arrested after a firearm was discharged outside a mosque in York.

North Yorkshire Police said it happened outside York Mosque and Islamic Centre on Bull Lane at about 02:15 BST.

The force said the arrested man was a 44-year-old white UK national from the city. This information has been released by the police consistent with their national guidelines, external.

The suspect left the area in a silver vehicle before he was held, and remains in custody for questioning. The weapon was believed to have been an air rifle and no-one was hurt, police said.

In a statement, North Yorkshire Police said: "It is too early to say what may have been the motivation behind this disturbing incident, but our Muslim community in York can be reassured that we are doing everything we can to establish the full circumstances."

The force said there would be "high-visibility patrols" in the area around the mosque while people attended for prayers and officers would meet with the imam.

Witnesses or anyone with information, CCTV or dashcam footage that could support the investigation are asked to contact police.

News.title: 'End this nightmare': Wife of ailing Briton jailed in Saudi Arabia appeals for release
News.content:
The UK Foreign Office says his case has been raised with the Saudi authorities.

Its current travel advice warns that it is illegal in Saudi Arabia to say anything publicly that the authorities "deem disruptive to public order". And it urges visitors to avoid commenting on the royal family, the Saudi authorities, or "issues that could be perceived as political".

"Speaking publicly about these issues can be defined by the Saudi authorities as posing a threat to national security," the advice states.

It adds: "Statements made on social media many years ago, or those published outside Saudi Arabia, may be taken into account. Punishment can include long custodial sentences."

Al-Doush's legal team in the UK say that neither they, his family, nor the UK government have been allowed to see any of the legal papers related to his case, including the judgment, despite repeated requests. So they don't fully understand the charges against him or the basis of his conviction.

But his London-based lawyer, Haydee Dijkstal, says he appears to have been questioned over several tweets posted in 2018 - and subsequently deleted - about Sudan, where he was born, and over his acquaintance with the son of a UK-based Saudi dissident.

She says Al-Doush was initially held for five months without charge, and interrogated without a lawyer before being sentenced in May 2025 to 10 years in jail by Saudi Arabia's Specialised Criminal Court, which is understood to have convicted him of using social media to spread fake news against the government. Human rights groups say the court has been used as a political tool, relying on vague counterterrorism and cybercrime laws to punish online expression.

This April, Al-Doush's sentence was reduced on appeal to five years. But his physical and mental health are still deteriorating, according to his wife.

Amnesty International says he is being held in a cell built for six to eight people, currently housing around 16 prisoners. His phone calls home have been frequently restricted, the group says. And he's been warned that he will be punished if he discusses his health, or his legal case.

"Ahmed Al-Doush has a family in the United Kingdom who urgently need him. He has been imprisoned for nothing more than social media posts - posts that would raise no eyebrow in any democratic country," says Eilidh Macpherson of Amnesty International UK.

"His health is now in crisis, and every day he remains detained is another day of unconscionable injustice inflicted not just on him, but on four young children who are growing up without their father."

"The Saudi authorities have the power to end this nightmare today," she adds. "We call on them to act without delay: release Ahmed Al-Doush and allow him to return home."

The group has also appealed to governments around the world to update their travel advice to ensure visitors to Saudi Arabia are aware of the risks that their past social media activity could entail, as the country gears up to host the World Cup in 2034 and other major events.

News.title: Stunning photos capture July's Buck Moon over the UK
News.content:
The July full Moon, also known as the Buck Moon, illuminated the sky over the UK on Wednesday night.

Skygazers captured stunning photos of the celestial display - which reached its peak at 15:36 BST - after the skies darkened.

The Buck Moon marks the second of three full Moons this summer.

The next chance to see one will be in the end of August, as the Sturgeon Moon rises as the final full Moon of season.

News.title: Former farmer, aged 99, fulfils wish to lead cow at show one more time
News.content:
A 99-year-old care home resident in south-west Scotland has fulfilled his wish to show a cow at his local agricultural show one more time.

Staff at the Belmont Care Centre in Stranraer put a post on social media about former farmer Jackie Brown's dream in the hope of being able to see it realised.

It came to the attention of the organisers of Stranraer Show who organised for Jackie to come along to the farming event on Wednesday.

He showed one of the Ayrshire cows - just as he had done many times across his pioneering career.

News.title: Inquiry finds MoD Afghan data breach was foreseeable failure
News.content:
The committee also questioned the decision not to provide confidential briefing to parliamentarians, with then-Defence Secretary Grant Shapps pushing back against plans to tell then-shadow defence secretary John Healey of the breach.

Thursday's report also questioned the government's overarching policy to not comment on special forces matters, describing it as "inappropriate" in the context of the breach.

The committee added that special forces involvement "should not prevent Parliament and the public from understanding how administrative failings occurred".

Dhesi said: "Secrecy has been too easily used as a shield against proper accountability in areas far removed from sensitive operations."

The role of UKSF in the resettlement scheme was also questioned by the committee after reports the breach had been due to their involvement in deciding whether to relocate Afghan special forces.

The committee was unable to establish this connection, due to the "neither confirm nor deny" policy of the government, but it did raise concerns over the handling of these cases.

In February 2024, BBC Panorama revealed that British Special Forces had been given a de facto veto over Arap applications from their Afghan counterparts seeking to relocate to safety in the UK.

Afghan special forces served alongside UKSF on some of the conflict's most dangerous missions and are considered among those at the highest risk of reprisal since the Taliban takeover.

Last year, the BBC obtained internal MoD documents - also cited in the report - showing a British Special Forces officer personally rejected 1,585 resettlement applications from Afghans with credible links to special forces in a matter of weeks, in 2023. The UKSF officer did not approve a single application during that period.

The rejections from UKSF left many in fear for their lives and former members of the Afghan special forces told the BBC they were living in hiding.

One said he had been interrogated and beaten by the Taliban before he went on the run, while another said he had escaped first but had heard the Taliban had gone to his home looking for him.

"I'm living in a very bad situation. I am in hiding and mostly my family can't live together and we cannot go out and we cannot work," he said. "I feel I have been left alone in the midst of hell."

The government had to announce a review in 2024 and since then 884 former members of Afghan special forces, who served alongside UKSF, have since had their rejections overturned.

The defence committee report outlined that the "proportion of decisions subsequently overturned demonstrates the seriousness of that failure".

The UK government closed Arap to new applications in 2025, but the report said the government had a "special responsibility" to the Afghan special forces it had wrongly rejected. Many of them had made their applications in 2021, but were still living in fear due to "government delay or error".

The defence secretary currently faces a legal challenge at the Royal Courts of Justice from former Afghan special forces who are unable to escape to the UK.

In a hearing on Wednesday, the court heard one family had "$200 left to survive".

A MoD spokesperson said: "This incident should never have happened and we acknowledge the significant impact it has had on many people.

"Thousands of eligible Afghans have already been safely relocated to the UK, where they can rebuild their lives and we are committed to ensuring that we conclude the Afghan resettlement programme by the end of this Parliament.

"We are learning the lessons from this incident and important reforms are already in place, including improved data protection standards, strengthened case-working processes and better programme governance.

"We welcome the public and parliamentary scrutiny of our actions, so we can learn more and be held to account, and we'll continue to work closely with the committee on this issue."

News.title: 'It was heartbreaking to attend a fertility appointment in a maternity unit'
News.content:
A woman who has been on a 10-year IVF journey is calling for fertility and gynaecology appointments to be separated from maternity services in some hospitals following her "heartbreaking" experience.

Niamh Smyth and her husband Justyn have spent over a decade trying to start a family, undergoing four rounds of IVF (In vitro fertilisation), with three unsuccessful attempts and one pregnancy which ended in miscarriage.

After nearly five years on a gynaecology waiting list, Smyth attended her appointment in May in the Ulster Hospital in Northern Ireland.

However, struggling to find the whereabouts of the gynaecology department in the hospital, she said she was shocked to find out where she had been directed to go.

"I phoned them and asked where the gynaecology department was," she said.

"They told me it was inside the maternity unit. Whenever I heard that, my heart just dropped."

News.title: Salman Rushdie attacker convicted of terror offences
News.content:
A US man who is already serving 25 years in prison for attempting to kill Sir Salman Rushdie has been convicted of additional charges, including providing material support to a terrorist group.

Hadi Matar was convicted in a New York federal court on Wednesday of providing assistance to Hezbollah, the Lebanese armed faction which is designated as a terrorist group by the US, UK and many other countries.

Prosecutors argued that Matar had been motivated by a fatwa, a religious edict, issued by Iran's religious leader in 1989 for Sir Salman's death.

The award-winning author testified during the trial, describing the attack and crediting a firefighter with saving his life by providing medical care.

The jury convicted Matar of engaging in an act of transnational terrorism and providing material support to Hezbollah.

During the trial in the New York city of Buffalo, prosecutors argued that he had been motivated by a 2006 speech by the then-leader of Hezbollah, calling for the fatwa against Sir Salman to be enforced, and that he had plotted the attack for two years.

"The defendant decided no one was going to do it, so he had to do it," Assistant US Attorney Timothy Lynch said in his closing statement, according to The Buffalo News, external.

"The defendant is the one who answered that call."

They also played videos made by Matar, 28, and interviewed Sir Salman on the witness stand about being stabbed 15 times, including to his cheek, chest, eye, neck and thigh.

"I was on the stage, lying down, with an enormous pool of blood all around me," he testified, adding: "It was an enormous and expansive lake of blood."

He also lifted the darkened lens on his glasses to reveal the wound to his eye, which has left him partially blinded, saying the attacker's knife had come "within millimetres from my brain".

Defence attorneys argued that Matar's attack had not been motivated by terrorism, and questioned the author about whether he should have expected a backlash to his controversial 1988 novel The Satanic Verses.

"I don't believe the book is on trial," Sir Salman responded. "Somebody else is on trial."

Matar is already serving a 25-year sentence after being convicted of attempted murder by a state court in 2025. He could now face life in prison in the federal conviction.

World Cup sensation Vozinha is fighting for permission to use his footballing nickname on his shirt when he debuts for new club Colo-Colo, despite regulations in Chile prohibiting it.

The 40-year-old proved a goalkeeping marvel for Cape Verde at the World Cup and after his performances for the small island nation, and his worldwide fame on Instagram, he is set to sign a six-month deal with Colo-Colo.

However, league rules in Chile do not allow players to use nicknames on their jerseys.

For the personal identification of players, the paternal and/or maternal surname must be printed on the upper back of the jersey, between 5 and 5.5 cm high, and the initial of the first name may be added, according to the league’s regulations. They ⁠also expressly prohibit the use of ‌nicknames.

Colo-Colo is trying to get permission for Vozinha to use his nickname on his shirt ( Getty Images )

“Nicknames, appellations, or sobriquets will not be permitted. If there are players with the same surname at a club, the initial of the first name or ‌the second surname, in that order of precedence, must ‌be added to distinguish them,” the rules continue.

But there have been previous exceptions allowed by the Chilean football association (ANFP) and Colo-Colo are hoping they will allow the veteran goalkeeper, whose real name is Josimar José Évora Dias, to use Vozinha, as he did during the World Cup.

"We have this problem. I spoke with the ANFP and they showed good disposition,” Colo-Colo president Aníbal Mosa told reporters on Wednesday.

“There is a Council of Presidents that was already called for Friday. I have spoken with several presidents of (other clubs) and they have shown me their favourable disposition to have the possibility of him playing with the name Vozinha, considering that he did so in the most important event ‌in the world.”

The nickname Vozinha, which means little grandmother in Portuguese, was given by the older kids when he was a boy and would cry after losing games of street football and storm home to his grandparents, with whom he lived.

Vozinha is expected to arrive in Santiago on Thursday, having been offered a six-month deal, Mosa added.

The agreement also includes an option to extend his stay by a further 12 months.

Vozinha was last at Portuguese second-division club ​Chaves but has also played at clubs in Angola, Cyprus, Moldova and Slovakia.
