Higher defence spending amid global conflicts is delivering a boost to Rolls-Royce and BAE Systems as the FTSE 100 stalwarts upgraded their annual outlooks after solid half-year figures.

Engine maker Rolls surged to the top of the FTSE 100 Index as shares jumped 6% in morning trading on Thursday thanks to a solid profit guidance upgrade.

It now expects to post underlying operating profits of £4.7 billion to £4.9 billion for 2026, up from previous guidance for between £4 billion and £4.2 billion.

The upgrade follows results showing underlying earnings surged 46% to £2.53 billion in the six months to June 30 on revenues a fifth higher at £11.28 billion.

open image in gallery BAE Systems CEO Charles Woodburn recently warned over UK defence spending (Andrew Matthews/PA) ( PA Archive )

The group is benefitting from higher global defence spending, adding to greater civil aerospace demand and as rapid AI data centre rollouts bolster its power systems division.

But statutory pre-tax profits more than halved to £1.93 billion from £4.84 billion a year ago due to exchange rate movements and after selling off parts of the business.

Defence contractor BAE Systems hiked its profit outlook, with a 10% to 12% rise in underlying earnings expected for 2026, up from the 9% to 11% previously forecast.

Underlying earnings rose 11% in the half-year on sales 9% higher, while pre-tax profits rose to £1.28 billion from £1.19 billion a year ago.

Listed firms operating in the defence sector have been enjoying stellar gains as countries bolster their defences amid growing global conflict, after the Iran conflict and Russia’s ongoing war with Ukraine.

The appointment of former defence secretary John Healy as Britain’s new Chancellor has given the sector a further fillip.

open image in gallery New Chancellor John Healey (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Wire )

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants to increase defence spending, though he has yet to commit to 3% of national income by 2030.

Last month, Mr Healey resigned as defence secretary from Sir Keir Starmer’s government after accusing the former prime minister and then chancellor Rachel Reeves of putting the country’s security at risk, with its long-awaited defence investment plan.

BAE’s chief executive Charles Woodburn recently warned that defence spending in the UK “falls well short” of what is required.

He described the current climate as “the most threatening time I’ve seen” and warned of the advances made by Russia before and during the war with Ukraine.

Despite extra funding pledged in June, he told the BBC it still “falls well short of what is needed to protect the country”.

News.title: What does fold mean in poker: A beginner’s guide
News.content:
Though it is accepted that poker is a game that entails luck, skill, experience and even psychological factors, the various strategies involved have contributed to it becoming one of the most popular games on poker sites and physical tables the world over.

Online poker may seem complicated to play if you are a beginner, but it is surprisingly simple once you learn the rules, strategies and terms.

And one such key term that is a vital part of each hand is the ‘fold’, or ‘folding’.

Folding is the term used for when a player decides to give up their hand and withdraw from the round, thereby forfeiting their chance of winning the pot – but saving their own remaining chips in the process.

Below, we have provided an in-depth guide, answering the question of what folding means in poker. We’ve also examined how to fold in poker, when to fold in poker and how to use the fold as part of a winning strategy.

What does fold mean in poker?

So, what is folding in poker exactly? And what does it mean to fold in poker?

In simple terms, a fold is when a player decides to give up their hand and withdraw from the current round.

When you fold, you forfeit any chance of winning the pot, but you also avoid having to commit more chips.

How to fold in poker: when and why to fold

Players fold by pushing their cards face-down toward the dealer and verbally declaring “fold.” They will place their cards into the pile of cards that is no longer in play – this is sometimes referred to as the ‘muck’. When playing poker on casino sites, the process simply requires a tap of the relevant button.

Folding is often done when a player believes their hand is too weak to compete against others, based on the community cards and opponents’ betting actions.

But why do players fold in poker?

Essentially, folding is a defensive move, as it protects players from losing chips. Although you have no chance of winning the pot once you fold, it is likely that you would never have won anyway if your hand is that weak.

Common scenarios for folding in poker

There are several key situations where folding is the best option during a poker game. It is vital to learn when to fold in poker, so we have discussed the main situations below.

Weak starting hands: In games like Texas Hold’em, hands like 7-2 offsuit or 9-4 are considered weak and often not worth playing, so folding pre-flop is a smart choice in order to preserve your remaining chips. Be sure to memorise the relevant poker hands to fold before playing.

After a big bet: If an opponent makes a large bet and the player has a marginal or weak hand, folding can prevent unnecessary losses.

When you’re beat: When the community cards suggest your opponent has a much stronger hand (for example, if you hold top pair but the board shows a potential flush or straight), then folding is often the best option.

Bluffing gone wrong: If you’ve been bluffing and your opponent calls or raises aggressively, folding can be a way to cut your losses and move on to the next hand.

When not to fold

Folding too often can be a mistake, and can lead to what’s known as ‘fold remorse’. It’s important to stay aggressive in some situations, particularly if:

You have a strong hand: Players sometimes misread their own hand strength and fold when they actually have a decent chance of winning. Make sure you are prepared by knowing what constitutes a strong hand in certain situations.

Players sometimes misread their own hand strength and fold when they actually have a decent chance of winning. Make sure you are prepared by knowing what constitutes a strong hand in certain situations. Your opponent is bluffing: If you suspect your opponent is bluffing, folding might not be the best option. Think carefully and avoid folding too quickly without considering the full situation.

While folding is a smart move in many cases, players should not fold simply to avoid risk all the time, as a certain level of risk-taking can be beneficial in poker.

Fold vs check

Folding is a similar process to checking, though it helps to understand the important distinction.

In short, folding means withdrawing from the hand entirely, while checking means passing the action to the next player without betting (this can only be done if nobody else at the table has placed a bet).

Essentially, think of it like this: folding ends your hand, whereas checking allows you to stay in the game without committing more chips.

Folding as part of a winning strategy

Though folding may seem like admitting defeat, it is an essential part of any solid poker strategy, as it helps to balance risk and your potential gain.

The ability to fold and save chips for future hands is a worthwhile tactic, and experienced players fold frequently to avoid risky situations and conserve chips for hands that offer better chances of winning.

How to know when to fold

There are a few specific tips that will help players to recognise when it’s the right time to fold – we have provided some detail below.

Understand hand strength: Get familiar with which starting hands are strong and which are weak. In Texas Hold’em, hands like Ace-King, Ace-Queen and pairs are worth playing, while weaker combinations often require a fold.

In short, unless your cards include a pair or a suited ace, you should fold a hand with a card of six or less. If you have sevens, eights, or nines, unless you have a pair, a suited ace or consecutive suited cards, you would also consider the fold.

Read the board: Pay attention to the table cards and how they interact with your hand. If the board is unfavourable (for example, an opponent could have a straight or flush), then folding is often the safest move.

Watch your opponents: Observe betting patterns. If a player who is usually passive starts putting down serious chips, it might be time to fold.

Folding in different poker variants

Folding plays a role in different poker games – we’ve explained the differences in the three main games below.

Texas Hold’em: Folding in Texas Hold’em is fairly common due to the variety of hands that are dealt. Players often fold weak starting hands to avoid getting trapped and losing chips.

Omaha: Since players have more cards to choose from, folding can be more complex in Omaha, but it’s still important to know when to let go of weak hands.

Seven-card stud: Folding happens less frequently in seven-card stud, but knowing when to fold against strong visible cards is still critical. There are various situations when you would fold – for example, if two or more of your suit were to be out and you didn’t have at least a fully live king-high among your first three cards.

Summary: What does fold mean in poker

In summary, a fold in poker is when a player decides to give up their hand and withdraw from a round. They forfeit any chance of winning the pot, but they preserve their remaining chips.

The poker fold is an important tool to manage risk and minimise losses. Remember that folding is not a sign of weakness but a smart, strategic move that can lead to long-term success in poker.

Though there is no set poker fold strategy, it helps to know how, when and why to fold in poker – essentially, when a player believes their hand is too weak to compete against others.

Remember to try and memorise common situations in which you might fold – for example, if you have a weak starting hand, if an opponent has just made a big bet, if your bluffing has backfired, or if you know you’re beat. In addition, try to understand hand strength, how to read the board and how to watch your opponents, and remember when not to fold too.

Finally, remember to gamble responsibly, and take note of the various tools that are available on gambling sites to help you do so. Don’t be afraid to get support if you need it either.

Gambling responsibly

Remember that gambling is only a form of entertainment, not a way to make money. Never wager more than you can afford to lose, never chase any losses, and take steps to remain in control of your budget immediately.

Poker games can be addictive, and the amounts you wager can climb quickly, so remember to always have a budget in mind and stick to it.

If you’re playing online, make use of responsible playing tools offered by gambling sites, such as self-assessment calculators, deposit limits, loss limits, self-exclusion and time-outs.

You’ll find the same tools on regulated slot sites and bingo sites if you find yourself engaging with those departments on gambling apps.

A popular brewery that promised free beer to its patrons upon the death of President Donald Trump is having its alcohol permit revoked.

The Wisconsin Department of Revenue is planning to shut down the Minocqua Brewing Company by August 4, according to a newsletter published Sunday by brewery owner Kirk Bangstad, who described the business as “the state’s most progressive brewery.”

Bangstad, a liberal activist who often posts anti-Trump messages on the company’s social media accounts, said he plans to fight against the decision “tooth and nail” after receiving a letter from state officials dated July 15, and asked readers to donate to the brewery’s legal defense fund.

“We need all the money we can get to sue the Department of Revenue and stay in business,” Bangstad said in an email to The Independent.

“As you can imagine, I’m not taking this lying down,” he wrote in the Substack post. “We’re going to fight the state of Wisconsin tooth and nail, and once again, they’ll have to pry me out of my taprooms before I stop selling beer to thirsty progressives who come to visit us.”

open image in gallery Minocqua Brewing Company has until August 4 to appeal its alcohol permit being revoked ( Minocqua Brewing Company )

He went on to list each of the rules that the DOR’s Division of Alcoholic Beverages has claimed that the company had broken, and explained why he believes the minor violations do not warrant the shutdown.

The company, which has locations in Madison and Minocqua, has until August 4 to appeal the revocation.

Wisconsin’s DOR said in an email to The Independent: “The Division of Alcohol Beverages is dedicated to the fair and consistent enforcement of alcohol beverages regulations in Wisconsin. The division is required to follow and implement state law, including ensuring permit holders and licensees follow all applicable laws and regulations. The division takes appropriate actions when these laws are not followed.

“We can confirm that the Department of Revenue has issued notice of a Brewer's permit revocation for two Minocqua Brewing Company locations and notice of an Alcohol Beverage Warehouse permit revocation for one location. The business has until August 4th to appeal and can operate during the appeal process,” the statement concluded.

As the agency carries out the investigation, Bangstad has shared his concerns that he might be getting pushed out of business due to his vocal political views rather than the reported violations.

“Everyone reading this, Democrat or Republican, should recoil at the thought of a small and thriving business being destroyed by their state government over such small violations—especially a brewery in the state of Wisconsin!” he said.

open image in gallery Donald Trump was at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in April when a shooting broke out, but he was unharmed ( Getty Images )

It comes after the brewery appeared to suggest on social media that it would give out free beer if Trump were to die, although the January 22 post did not include his name, as first reported by Fox News Digital.

“Free beer, all day long the day he dies,” the post said. “Show us this post when it happens in a few months and we’ll make good on that promise.” The post was later updated to clarify, “we meant the Madison Taproom because that’s open all year, if he dies in the summer, then it’s gonna be the Minocqua Taproom.”

After shots were fired while Trump was present at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in April, the brewery’s Facebook said, “Well, we almost got #freebeerday.”

In a new Substack post shared Wednesday, Bangstad shared that he replied to Fox News Digital’s request for comment with a similar joke promising half-off beers in the name of Mitch McConnell, who was recently hospitalized.

Bangstad concluded his letter: “Together, we’ll get to the bottom of who’s trying to put us out of business and silence our voice in Wisconsin—one beer at a time.”

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals Tottenham are closing in on another transfer ‘bomba’ – but four stars considering exits

ROBERTO DE ZERBI has promised Tottenham fans another transfer “bomba” to continue their summer splurge.

Spurs have already spent more than £230million on new faces this summer, but De Zerbi says they are only just over halfway there on new signings – and has some more surprises up his sleeve.



De Zerbi also revealed that England star Djed Spence has spoken to him about leaving the club, along with captain Cristian Romero, midfielder Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario. He also confirmed he has stopped trying to convince Romero to stay in north London.

The Italian, who saved the north Londoners from relegation to tee up a huge summer spend, has overseen six signings already but now wants to add a fierce new forward line.



Talks continue over a deal for Manchester City‘s £60m-rated Savinho, though he may not be the teased “bomba” as the Spurs boss wants to add a striker and perhaps one more winger.

De Zerbi, 47, admitted he becomes like a “shark” when signings are in the offing and relishes working in the transfer market.

He said: “The transfer market, it’s not finished for sure. We completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market. Now we have another bomba.

“Is it close? I hope, but it’s not finished for sure.

“We have to increase the number of goals with the play, with the quality of the play, with the midfielders, with the attackers, but we have to bring players able to score goals.

With such an influx of new faces and the money which comes with that, players will also need to be sold. Luka Vuskovic has already joined Brighton in a £50m deal, while De Zerbi confirmed he has spoken to four stars who are considering a move away this term.

Sports.title: Who is Eddie Howe’s wife Vicki and how many children does the ex-Newcastle boss have?
Sports.content:
EDDIE HOWE has parted ways with Newcastle United with immediate effect after a memorable five-year tenure.

The manager ended the Magpies’ 70-year wait for a major domestic trophy and brought Champions League football back to St James’ Park during his time in charge.



Here’s everything you need to know about Howe’s family who support him on and off the pitch.

Who is Eddie Howe?

Eddie Howe was most recently the manager of Newcastle United, and he was born on November 29, 1977 in Buckinghamshire.



He was raised by a single mother, Anne, who he describes as a hardworking parent who raised him and his siblings.

Anne sadly passed away in 2012.

Howe’s life has always been sport-focused, he was a top cricketer at age 14 and started playing football for Bournemouth in 1994, making his senior debut with the team in 1995.

He was a key defender before injuries led to early retirement at 29 in 2007.

Howe immediately moved into coaching the reserve squad at Bournemouth before managing the first-team in two stints – from December 2008 to January 2011 and from October 2012 to August 2020.

In the second spell, he took the team from League One to the Premier League.



He eventually replaced Steve Bruce as Newcastle manager in November 2021, steering the club out of a relegation battle to a mid-table finish.

Howe transformed the Magpies into top-four contenders, securing Champions League qualification in both 2023 and 2025.

His crowning achievement came in March 2025, when he led Newcastle to a 2–1 Carabao Cup final victory over Liverpool, ending a 70-year wait for a major domestic trophy.

His tenure came to an end in July 2026 following a tough 2025–26 league campaign where the club finished 12th, combined with growing frustration over key player departures during the summer transfer window.

Who is Eddie Howe’s wife Vicki?

Vicki Howe keeps a low public profile, intentionally avoiding the spotlight to focus on family life.



The couple met during Eddie’s playing career at Bournemouth and have three sons: Harry, Rocky, and Theo.

When Eddie was appointed Newcastle manager in late 2021, he initially lived in a hotel while Vicki managed the family home on the south coast before moving the family north to reunite.

Since settling in Northumberland, Vicki and Eddie are regularly seen supporting their eldest two sons at local grassroots youth football matches across the North East.

The family fully embraced life in Tyneside during Eddie’s managerial stint, with the children even picking up local Geordie phrases.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Eddie told the BBC: “I asked my youngest to do something yesterday and his answer was: ‘Howay dad!’ I always have a little second glance and check their language.



“It’s brilliant that they’re fully immersed in the Newcastle way of life, the language, the way of thinking.



“It’s such a great area with such positive, driven and motivated people. I’m very proud that they are going to be adopted Geordies.”

BOURNEMOUTH star Eli Junior Kroupi faces four months out — wrecking his hopes of a big-money move this summer.

Barcelona, Arsenal and Tottenham were among clubs targeting the £100million-rated striker.



Kroupi, 20, has had surgery after breaking a bone in a foot during the Cherries’ pre-season trip to Austria.

The Frenchman netted 13 goals in 33 Premier League matches last season as a teen to help the Cherries finish sixth in the Prem.



That led to a host of major clubs putting him on their wish list after emerging as one of Europe’s most promising forwards.

There were reports that Tottenham were looking to splash out £85m to sign him, while Manchester United and Chelsea were also linked.



However, it’s understood Bournemouth were never planning on selling the highly-rated forward this summer.

And Kroupi will likely have to wait until January at the earliest if he wants an exit from the Vitality.

His injury blow means he is set to miss the start of Bournemouth’s maiden Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth do have enough depth to cover them in attack after Kroupi’s blow.



New boss Marco Rose has strengthened his attack this summer by signing striker Alvaro Rodriguez, 22, from Elche for £21m.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rose also has Evanilson and Enes Unal at his disposal.

Kroupi is not the only Bournemouth player generating interest this summer.

Midfielder Alex Scott is being chased by the likes of Chelsea and Manchester United after his impressive 2025-26 campaign.

And Brazilian winger Rayan, 19, also has his suitors after scoring five and assisting two in the Prem last season.



Those displays were enough to win him a place in Brazil‘s World Cup squad and he made three starts at the tournament.

Sports.title: Man Utd consider Lewis Hall transfer raid with Red Devils ready to capitalise on Newcastle disarray
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are weighing up a move for left back Lewis Hall amid the latest disarray at Newcastle.

United consider Hall, 21, to be the ideal long-term replacement for Luke Shaw, who is out of contract next year.



Sun Sport revealed Hall is keen to leave Newcastle, whose manager Eddie Howe has resigned after a 4-1 pre-season loss at Bristol City.

Well-placed sources say Hall felt his positional change towards the end of last season cost him a place in England’s World Cup squad.



Newcastle have already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali for a combined £170million and Bruno Guimaraes is wanted by Arsenal. Hall is also under contract until 2029.

Hall could be persuaded to stay, depending on who replaces Howe, but an added complication is that Newcastle have not sold a player to United since Andy Cole’s then-British record £7m move in January 1995.



United want to bring in a left-sided player and are now prepared to cash in on teenage left back Harry Amass.

The struggle to sell Marcus Rashford, United’s highest earner on £325,000 a week, effectively prohibits United from recruiting a left-wing specialist.

United have several specialist and auxiliary left backs but Shaw recently turned 31 and lacks an outright competitor.

Patrick Dorgu has started all three of his games under Michael Carrick as a winger, Amass spent last season on loan and rookie Diego Leon is still training with the under 21s.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Hall was unhappy that his role briefly changed during Newcastle’s run-in last season and believes it contributed to his omission from Thomas Tuchel’s 26-man squad.

He played out of position to offset the absence of injured right back Tino Livramento, who was ironically included in Tuchel’s squad.

Hall was switched to right back for Newcastle’s 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest Howe in their penultimate fixture before Tuchel announced his 26-man squad.

Former Chelsea defender Hall was also substituted at half-time in the 2-1 defeat to Bournemouth in April before starting the next two games against Arsenal and Brighton on the bench.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool talks planned, Vinicius Jr Arsenal latest, Bruno Guimaraes admission
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior has been linked with a sensational move to Arsenal this summer.

The latest transfer news from Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and more as they look to improve their teams ahead of the Premier League season

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Thursday, July 30th.

The summer transfer window will slam shut in just over a month's time with business strarting to ramp up in preparation for the new campaign. Morgan Rogers, Sandro Tonali and Elliot Anderson have all moved clubs is mega-money deals, in excess of the £100m mark, and that could be just the beginning.

Arsenal remain keen on signing Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior, whose future at Real Madrid is unclear heading into the final 12 months of his contract, and the Gunners are willing to move for the Brazilian if the opportunity arises.

Mikel Arteta's side are prepared to offer the 26-year-old star the biggest deal in the club's history, but also have their eye on improving other areas of the pitch. They remain keen on signing Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes, and there is ample drama on that front with the Magpies' denying any talk of negotations between the two clubs.

Elsewhere, Liverpool are reportedly planning on holding talks with Paris-Saint Germain in an attempt to sign French international Bradley Barcola. Andoni Iraola's side are in the hunt for a successort for Mohamed Salah and have made the PSG star their number one transfer target.

Manchester United remain hopeful of adding another midfielder to their ranks ahead of their return to the Champions League, having already signed Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. There's also the small matter of Marcus Rashford's future at the club needing resolved.

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York

Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha was handed a positional switch last night as Andoni Iraola makes plans for the possible arrival of Bradley Barcola from PSG

View 2 Images Rio Ngumoha scored for Liverpool in pre-season

Rio Ngumoha handed Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola a timely reminder of his quality - all whilst leaving scope for him and Reds' target Bradley Barcola to thrive in the same team.

‌



Ngumoha was a bright spark for the Merseysiders last season, in what was largely a forgettable campaign. He continued to excel during his limited opportunities and came off the bench to score the winner as Liverpool saw off Wrexham in pre-season.

‌



The 17-year-old's deflected goal in New York kept up the team's perfect record so far and his deployment off the right, having played almost exclusively off the left previously, serves to highlight what could come next for Iraola.

‌



There have been clamours for Ngumoha to play more regularly, but he and Barcola, another left-sided forward, could've been in a scenario whereby they were battling for the same spot.

Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star READ MORE :

Liverpool are ready to ramp up their interest in the PSG man, whose exit from the European Champions is looking all the more likely, and Ngumoha's impressive cameo off the right shows that he and the Frenchman could play in tandem either side of a striker, whoever that may be.

Iraola, should he get a deal for Barcola over the line, could spend up to £140million, which is what the Parisians are demanding. He'd need a return on that investment, which could've left Ngumoha's route towards more minutes blocked off, but playing off the right is now a viable option.

‌



The teenager said on his new boss: “The manager has been very good, getting his points across really well. He’s been top and all the coaching staff have been very good as well.”

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is being linked with a blockbuster move to Anfield (Image: Dan Mullan - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Iraola's style earned him huge plaudits at Bournemouth but the Spaniard insists his Reds side still have a way to go before they've locked in his principles.

‌



"I think we’re still not there," he said. "We are sometimes arriving late, but I think it’s a step forward, since especially the first half against Sunderland. That is more of a reference than the second half.

"Slowly, slowly I hope every game we are closer and closer. We start to add new bodies, because now we are playing with a lot of the young players. Slowly, slowly we have to add the senior players that are starting to train with us, so we can arrive to the beginning of the season in a good place."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up

Eddie Howe is to leave Newcastle after five years in charge with Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle lined up to replace him

View 2 Images Eddie Howe is set to leave Newcastle (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Eddie Howe is set to leave Newcastle with immediate effect after five years as Toon boss. Howe oversaw a humbling 4-1 defeat by Championship side Bristol City in a pre-season friendly last night.

‌



Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle has reportedly been lined up as his replacement.

‌



Following the defeat at Ashton Gate, Howe hinted his time may be up and that he had lost control of transfers in light of Arsenal's interest in Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



"What will be, will be," he said. "We can’t control the forces that are at play here, we’ve just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I’m sure he will do.

"And he makes a difference as he always has done."

UEFA holding emergency meeting over World Cup boycott to stop FIFA villain Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star READ MORE :

Howe joined Newcastle in November 2021 following the sacking of Steve Bruce. Newcastle had been taken over by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund the previous month.

‌



The Magpies won 12 of their final 18 games of the season to finish 11th and become the first team in Premer League history to avoid relegation after going winless in their first 14 fixtures.

Howe penned a long-term extension in August 2022 and later that season led Newcastle to the League Cup final where they were beaten by Manchester United.

Newcastle qualified for the Champions League for the first time in 20 years by finishing in the top four, but finished bottom of their group with just five points.

‌



Howe took charge of his first Tyne-Wear derby in January 2024 as Newcastle beat Sunderland 3-0 at the Stadium of Light in the FA Cup third round.

The Toon fell out of Europe but registered their first major trophy for 56 years when they beat Liverpool in the 2025 League Cup final under Howe's stewardship.

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle is in line to replace Howe at Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Newcastle again qualified for the Champions League but could only muster a 12th-placed finish in 2025-26, also losing both games to newly-promoted Sunderland who finished in seventh.

Previously, Howe spent the entirety of his playing career with Bournemouth, other than playing twice for Portsmouth in the early 2000s.

He became Bournemouth boss in 2008, leaving in 2011 for Burnley. But he returned to the south coast in 2012 and spent eight years in charge of the Cherries, leading them to the Premier League for the first time in their history.

‌



German boss Jassile, 38, was Red Bull Salzburg manager between 2021 and 2023 before moving to Saudi Arabia to take charge of Al-Ahli.

He won the Austrian Bundesliga in consecutive seasons and has led Al-Ahli to back-to-back Asian Champions League titles.

Sports.title: UEFA holding emergency meeting over World Cup boycott to stop FIFA villain Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
UEFA holding emergency meeting over World Cup boycott to stop FIFA villain Gianni Infantino

UEFA are set to hold an emergency meeting about a potential World Cup boycott

View 2 Images UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and FIFA president Gianni Infantino have a strained relationship. (Image: (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images))

UEFA will hold an emergency meeting at 2pm today, Thursday, July 30, to discuss a potential World Cup boycott in protest against Gianni Infantino's plans to privatise the tournament. The proposals have received major backlash from those across Europe.

‌



The Football Association, European Leagues, European Football Clubs, the Union of European Clubs, the Football Supporters Association and Football Supporters Europe have all released strong statements in protest, calling for major change at the top of FIFA

‌



Infantino recently unveiled plans to create a commercial subsidiary to run it's main events like the World Cup, and claims its 211 member associations will receive 40m US dollars (£30m) under those plans. However, Infantino has set a September 19 deadline for access to an initial $20m (£15m).

‌



Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott READ MORE :

FIFA come down hard on Argentina stars as charges handed out after World Cup final brawl READ MORE :

Associations within UEFA have been left infuriated by Infantino's privatisation plans, how its been presented to football federations and the 53 day timeframe given, with those who agree to the terms being given guaranteed higher returns.

Infantino defended the proposals in an interview on Wednesday, claiming they provide "a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally."

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has publicly issued a statement (Image: FIFA)

‌



He added: "The fans remain the cornerstone of the beautiful game, and the sport they watch and love will not change. FIFA obviously continues to govern football without any external interference. We want to help creating the next ‘Cabo Verdes’.

"Fans from everywhere in the world, would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries. But again, it is simply a choice for our members."

European football’s governing body UEFA responded in a statement: "Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off pay out offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan.

‌



"But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends.

"We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritize associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



UEFA have reportedly been in contact with European Commission to dicsuss how Infantino’s plan can be challenged and former Football Association chief executive, Mark Palios, believes UEFA holds a trump card over FIFA.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Palios said: "UEFA have a real card to play, and that is if they don’t turn up at the next World Cup that’s going to be an absolute financial disaster for FIFA, in the sense that you’re not going to get the sponsorships, the eyeballs, and so forth.

"If you don’t have Spain, France, England, Germany there, then it’s not going to be anything like the spectacle that it normally is.

‌



"There’s a consequence, that’s the major card they have to play and I hope they do play that. There’s a real danger that this crosses the line. The ideal of sport is being suffocated by the raison d’etre of business.

"I would hope (UEFA nations) would all be on the same page, but there are a lot of small FAs within FIFA. They all have one vote, which was part of the strength that (former FIFA president) Sepp Blatter had for so many years in terms of garnering their support.

"And, of course, these smaller FAs do benefit from this in terms of some fairly large amounts of cash."

Sports.title: England's World Cup win 60 years on: Why heroes of 1966 should be celebrated more than ever
Sports.content:
When they had all finished playing, most of the squad that won the World Cup on this day in 1966 would meet up for a couple of days’ golf on a summer weekend every year.

It was a bit old school. The lads would take to the course, the wives and partners would go shopping or pamper themselves. They all had a lovely dinner and shared stories of what they had been up to. But they only shared those stories amongst themselves.

Those get-togethers were always kept away from the public glare. True, it was an age before mobile phones and social media, but they could have staged some photographs or offered to do some publicity to get a free holiday or some preferential treatment.

Not a chance. They were special times to relive a special time created by humble men.

‌



And that is what struck you whenever you met any member of the ’66 England squad. Their humility.

FIFA come down hard on Argentina stars as charges handed out after World Cup final brawl READ MORE :

Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes facing same transfer dilemma that Man Utd stars got wrong READ MORE :

Were those members of the squad who had to wait 43 years to get their winners’ medals ever angry? Were those who had to wait three decades after the World Cup win to get any recognition on the honours’ list ever bitter? Were these heroes resentful when some had to sell their medals because they never earned enough money for an enjoyable retirement?

No, no and no.

But the bottom line is that while the names of those who gave England its only World Cup will always be in legend, the acclaim has never been sufficient. Their rewards were never sufficient.

‌



Sir Alf Ramsey was paid an annual salary of £4,500 by the Football Association. Based on overall consumer inflation, that is £109,000 in today’s money. That is pretty much what the Football Association pay Thomas Tuchel A WEEK.

Obviously, comparisons must be made within the context of the huge influx of money into the game over so many years.

View 3 Images Geoff Hurst scoring England's third goal (Image: Getty Images)

Captain Bobby Moore, hat-trick scorer Sir Geoff Hurst and their team-mates received a winning bonus of around £1,000… before tax. Gianni Infantino is currently trying to sell off the World Cup for TEN BILLION dollars.

‌



The finances of the 1966 tournament and the 2026 tournament were, quite literally, worlds apart.

Football’s finances are unrecognisable from what they were six decades ago. It is why Moore was on £100 a week at West Ham. It is why so many of that wonderful squad of players had to pursue other careers after they finished playing.

I grew up watching Roger Hunt’s lorries heading out on jobs. Hunt was an all-time Liverpool great… and a haulage contractor.

In terms of material reward, there is no comparison between then and now. But the game was the same - probably with a bit less cheating.

‌



View 3 Images Bobby Moore and Co celebrate with the famous old trophy, which they lifted 60 years ago today (Image: Getty Images)

And while it is easy to look back and believe there was a bit more class in the game, have a look back at the celebrations at Wembley on July 30, 1966.

Joyous, yes. Dignified, of course. But that was an era when sportsmen and women were not deified for singular achievements. They were not even deified for stellar careers.

The heroes of ’66 were quite happy with that. I am sure Sir Geoff Hurst, Ian Callaghan and Terry Paine - the three members of the squad who are blessedly still with us - are quite happy with that.

‌



Today is a day to celebrate the boys of ’66 for their brilliance, their achievement… and their humility.

Sports.title: Dream Liverpool attack for 2026/27 as £125million man starts and Barcola replaces Salah
Sports.content:
Dream Liverpool attack for 2026/27 as £125million man starts and Barcola replaces Salah

Liverpool still have a way to go before Andoni Iraola gets his wish in the summer transfer window

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola is a crucial target for Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola’s search for Mohamed Salah’s successor continues, but Liverpool may have just received a huge boost in their pursuit of top target Bradley Barcola. The Reds' right-wing position is yet to be filled with Liverpool's season-opener against Newcastle less than a month away.

‌



The Reds boss had targeted RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande with Liverpool's offer of £85million swiftly rejected by the Bundesliga side. Attention then turned towards Barcola, 23, who had played second fiddle to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for parts of last season at Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



The Frenchman has been an important player for the Champions League winners in the past two campaigns but has reportedly rejected a contract renewal with the Ligue 1 champions. In the midst of his uncertain future, news broke this week that Barcola had clinched a verbal agreement to join the Reds.

‌



However, landing the highly sought-after Frenchman will carry a massive financial burden, with PSG setting his asking price at £140million. The Reds are reluctant to meet that figure, which would smash the club's transfer record, and are hoping to negotiate a compromise with the French champions.

L'Equipe has reported that the two clubs are currently in talks over a possible deal for Barcola. Predominantly a left-winger, Barcola is also adept on the right flank, with Liverpool not expected to pursue another wide player should they land the Frenchman.

Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp given strict instruction about managing Germany days after making quit threat READ MORE :

The forward has featured on the right side 37 times throughout his career, chipping in with seven goals and 15 assists. That leaves the left-wing berth as a three-way contest between Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

‌



Gakpo may hold the edge over the two youngsters in terms of experience, but is considered less suited to Iraola's high-pressing system. A starting berth for Liverpool this coming season might arrive too early for the 17-year-old Ngumoha.

View 4 Images The Frenchman has reportedly declined a new deal at PSG (Image: FRANCK FIFE, AFP via Getty Images)

Given his exceptional talent, the Reds will be carefully monitoring his workload to avoid placing excessive physical demands on him. That could pave the way for Munoz - who arrived at the club in a £34m transfer last month - to establish himself as a regular for the Premier League outfit, following his World Cup success with Spain this summer.

‌



Both players will be anticipated to carry some of the goalscoring burden, as befits the modern-day winger's role. Nevertheless, the bulk of that responsibility will rest with Alexander Isak. The Swede endured a disappointing maiden season with merely four goals in 22 appearances across all competitions.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 4 Images Victor Munoz has had a dream summer with Spain (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

‌



Fitness concerns and injuries disrupted his campaign, but after featuring - and finding the net - at the World Cup, the 26-year-old will be prepared to demonstrate the form that convinced the Reds to invest £125m in his signature last year.

It's a sharp contrast to the heavily interrupted summer Isak experienced this time last year. And he'll effectively be like a fresh signing for Iraola as a consequence.

View 4 Images Alexander Isak will lead the line for Liverpool with Hugo Ekitike injured (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Isak's quality of finishing and capacity to combine with his team-mates, particularly Florian Wirtz, provides the Reds with a distinctive presence up front and one that could establish them as a serious challenger for the biggest honours.

Liverpool's attacking options still raise plenty of unanswered questions at this stage. However, should Iraola succeed in assembling his ideal frontline at Anfield, the rest of the league will undoubtedly be put on notice.

Sports.title: 'I cried after leaving Real Madrid for Arsenal – I wanted new contract but my agent messed up'
Sports.content:
'I cried after leaving Real Madrid for Arsenal – I wanted new contract but my agent messed up'

A former Arsenal star recalled his experience of joining the Gunners from Real Madrid

View 3 Images A former Arsenal star reflected on what led to him signing for the Gunners (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Mesut Ozil became an Arsenal icon but the midfielder never planned to leave Real Madrid. The Germany international joined the Gunners in a marquee £43.5million deal on deadline day in 2013 but Ozil later admitted to crying as he left the Spanish capital.

‌



Arsenal are interested in making another statement signing from Los Blancos this summer as the club explore a move for Vinicius Junior. The Brazil international has entered the final year of his Real Madrid deal, prompting speculation over his future, and contract discussions are what ultimately led Ozil to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



The attacking midfielder had signed for the Spanish giants after starring for Germany at the 2010 World Cup. In 159 appearances, Ozil scored 27 goals and provided 80 assists. However, Real were prepared to cash in on him after his father and agent clashed with club president Florentino Perez, a decision that moved Ozil to tears.

‌



“It was bad. I was very sad when I left Madrid,” Ozil recalled to Marca in 2023. “I had a great time for three years at Real Madrid and in this city. I was truly happy. But things happened.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“Suddenly, at the beginning of that season, I wasn't getting many minutes of playing time anymore, and there was a conflict between Mr Florentino Perez and my father and agent.

‌



Liverpool given free run at Bradley Barcola as Arsenal make transfer decision READ MORE :

Thierry Henry slammed Jose Mourinho for treatment of Vinicius Jr as Arsenal move arises READ MORE :

“We had to find a new club. It was hard for me. The moment the plane took off and flew away, tears streamed down my face. That was the moment I realised it was over.”

Asked if he would go back and change his decision to leave, Ozil added: “At the time, it seemed fine to me, because after the conflict between my father and Mr Perez, I was worried I wouldn't get any playing time again if I didn't leave. So it's hard to say. But, of course, I wish we could have handled the situation differently back then.”

Ozil was an instant hit at Arsenal, clocking up seven goals and 14 assists at the end of his debut season. During his seven-and-a-half years at the club, he made 254 appearances and won three FA Cups.

‌



View 3 Images Ozil scored 44 goals in 254 games for Arsenal (Image: GLYN KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

He is not the most recent Real Madrid player to make an impact at Arsenal, as shown by Premier League-winning captain Martin Odegaard. The Gunners will hope that Vinicius Junior can help build on last season’s success if they can get a deal over the line. However, Ozil also reflected on the circumstances surrounding his Real Madrid exit during his Arsenal heyday.

"The only and also self-critical truth [about my Real Madrid exit] is the following," Ozil wrote in his 2017 book The Magic of the Game. "My father Mustafa represented me at this time as an adviser. He was convinced that by now he would understand enough about the profession and no longer depend on the help of other agents.

‌



"I did not intend to leave Real Madrid at all. My father and I both had the goal of extending prematurely for a further year. My father then took over the negotiations. He contacted Florentino Perez and made appointments. It was not about greed. It was just a fair payment. And at first Real did not match us. But the situation was new to my father.

View 3 Images Ozil spent three years at Real Madrid (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

“He did not know how to be placed under negotiation pressure in this form. He had not done dozens of negotiations with the biggest club managers, and accordingly, he had to be honest, he had to admit that he had to deal with such a provocative offer.

Article continues below

"That is why he did not keep a cool head as it would probably have been important," Ozil continued. "In contrast to a man like Florentino Perez, who expects people to dance to his pipe, stubbornness was not appropriate. And it was not at all right for my father to leave the office and slam the door to Perez's office shut."

Sports.title: 'PSG owner promised me Liverpool transfer before manager changed his mind'
Sports.content:
'PSG owner promised me Liverpool transfer before manager changed his mind'

The former international forward was sorely disappointed that his permanent move to Liverpool failed to materialise

View 3 Images Nicolas Anelka enjoyed his time on Merseyside (Image: Clive Brunskill/ Getty Images)

Former Liverpool frontman Nicolas Anelka previously revealed he was promised a permanent transfer to the Reds from PSG before then-manager Gerard Houllier changed his mind on sanctioning the move. Liverpool are currently embroiled in yet another transfer battle with the French giants over winger Bradley Barcola, with the European champions reportedly demanding £145million for the World Cup star.

‌



While Barcola's future at Liverpool remains unclear, Anelka is adamant that his failed move to Anfield will haunt him forever. The ex-Arsenal forward made an unexpected loan switch from PSG to Anfield back in December 2001, netting five goals in 22 outings.

‌



Yet Liverpool's top brass chose not to make the Frenchman's arrangement permanent the following summer. Instead, they opted for El Hadji Diouf, who had just caught the eye representing Senegal at the 2002 World Cup.

‌



In hindsight, Liverpool's choice of Diouf over Anelka has gone down as one of the most costly mistakes in the club's recent memory.

While Diouf struggled, managing just six goals across two seasons and finding himself mired in a string of controversies, Anelka thrived at Manchester City, netting 45 goals over three seasons.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool can grant Bradley Barcola’s first demand after PSG transfer READ MORE :

The French forward told the Liverpool ECHO in 2020: "This is my biggest regret as well because I knew it was the perfect match. Everything was perfect! I loved everything about the club. I had an amazing relationship with the fans. I loved them and I think it was reciprocal.

"Looking back, I am proud to have worn the jersey of this legendary club and to have known this stadium and these amazing fans."

The 47-year-old represented 12 different sides throughout his senior career. While his spell at Liverpool was the briefest, his fondness remains evident and he revealed why the transfer fell through.

‌



"It's simple: it didn't happen because Gerard Houllier wanted to pay a lower salary," he said. "It's acceptable but you have to say it. I wanted to sign from the first minute. Of course a permanent move was discussed from the first day I joined the club.

View 3 Images Nicolas Anelka was a hit at Liverpool (Image: Clive Brunskill/ALLSPORT)

"If you look at the first time they introduced me in the press conference, I said if I could sign now, I would, but Gerard Houllier wanted a loan because he was not sure. In the middle of March, we were in negotiations to sign.

‌



"PSG shareholder Alain Cayzac said to me Gerard told him that Liverpool would sign me. Later on, Gerard told me face-to-face he'd sign me permanently.

"In the middle of April we reached an agreement about the salary, which had stalled things a little, but I was expecting to sign my contract when the league was over but there was no news from PSG and no news from Liverpool.

"I heard on the news that Gerard Houllier was after another player so that's how I knew they were not going to sign me!"

‌



Former Liverpool assistant manager Phil Thompson, who was serving as interim manager during Anelka's proposed move to the club while Houllier recovered from a heart operation, claimed the club opted against signing the Frenchman after his representatives allegedly attempted to engineer a return to Arsenal.

"I heard about this Arsenal story," Anelka said. "If it was true, why didn't I sign for Arsenal when Liverpool announced in the press they weren't going to sign me?"

View 3 Images Nicolas Anelka of Liverpool and Assistant Manager Phil Thompson look on (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



"And even if it was true, it's a normal situation. It's like I'm saying I don't wanna sign for a club because they are speaking with another striker. It makes no sense. The reality is at the time it was very easy to point the finger at me with my reputation."

Anelka added: "I loved my time with Phil Thompson, more so than Gerard Houllier. Phil Thompson was a typical Scouser. Direct and straight. He'll tell you what he likes and when he doesn't like it, you would know. This is exactly what I want and what I like from people.

"I know if Phil was the manager I would have signed and stayed many years but fate chose otherwise and I had to take another path to find a big club."

Article continues below

Anelka went on to represent Chelsea, Bolton and West Brom on home soil, as well as the likes of Fenerbahce and Juventus on the continent. During his spell at Chelsea, he claimed the Premier League, two FA Cups and featured in the Champions League final defeat to Manchester United in 2008.

Sports.title: Howe leaves Newcastle - Saudi-based Jaissle favourite to take over
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left his role as Newcastle United head coach.

The decision has been taken following discussions with the club's hierarchy over the last 48 hours, although Howe had started the ball rolling on a potential departure a number of weeks ago.

In this time, Howe continued to focus on preparing the Newcastle team for their season opener against Liverpool on August 23, live on Sky Sports. Howe's departure comes 25 days before that fixture.

Matthias Jaissle of Al Ahli Is the favourite to replace Howe. Sky Sports News understands talks are at an advanced stage with the 38-year-old German coach. Al Ahli is one of the four clubs owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) - who also own Newcastle.

Kieran McKenna and Antonio Conte were also names on Newcastle's shortlist.

Newcastle have already had a challenging summer after the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon - and that continues with uncertainty over their captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is wanted by Arsenal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Howe discussed the rumours surrounding Bruno Guimaraes and revealed he wanted to keep him at the club, before news of his departure emerged

Those sales have played a factor in Howe's decision amid concerns about what the squad will look like at the start of the new campaign. Newcastle also sold striker Alexander Isak for a British-record £125m to Liverpool last summer.

Howe has spent a number of months reflecting on his time at Newcastle and believed he could take the club forward this season, providing Newcastle recruited well this summer.

Eddie Howe's Newcastle reign November 2021 - Howe replaces Steve Bruce as Newcastle United head coach

May 2022 - Howe guides Newcastle to 11th-placed finish in first season in charge. Newcastle become first Premier League team to stay up after failing to win any of their first 14 games

August 2022 - Howe signs new long-term contract

February 2023 - Howe leads Newcastle to first final in 24 years but they lose Carabao Cup final 2-0 to Manchester United

May 2023 - Howe leads Newcastle to a fourth-placed finish earning the club qualification for the Champions League for the first time in more than 20 years

January 2024 - Howe leads Newcastle to victory in an FA Cup Tyne-Wear derby - their first win over Sunderland in almost 13 years

May 2024 - Newcastle finish seventh despite scoring 85 goals and posting their highest Premier League goal tally ever

Mar 2025 - Newcastle beat Liverpool 2-1 in the Carabao Cup final to win their first major trophy in 56 years

May 2025 - Howe leads Newcastle into the Champions League again with a fifth-placed Premier League finish

September 2025 - Howe loses star striker Alexander Isak to Liverpool in a £125m deal on Deadline Day

February 2026 - Newcastle advance to the knockout stages of the Champions League via the play-offs, where they are later beaten by Barcelona

May 2026 - Newcastle finish the season 12th

May 2026 - Anthony Gordon leaves for Barcelona in a deal that nets Newcastle almost £70m

July 2026 - Howe sees Sandro Tonali leave for Spurs in a deal worth £100m

July 2026 - Club captain Bruno Guimaraes tells Newcastle he wants to leave

July 2026 - Howe steps down as Newcastle head coach less than 24 hours after 4-1 pre-season defeat to Championship side Bristol City

Newcastle have signed 20-year-old winger Bazoumana Toure from Hoffenheim for £42m, 18-year-old midfielder Sean Steur from Ajax for £23m and 20-year-old goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen from Reims for £18.5m.

They have recently, however, appeared to miss out on Johan Manzambi, who decided to move to Aston Villa - which was a big blow for Howe and the club.

Howe has been one of Newcastle's greatest-ever managers, winning the League Cup to end the club's 70-year wait for silverware as well as taking the club into the Champions League on two occasions after sealing top-five finishes in the Premier League.

Last season, they progressed further in the Champions League than they had ever done before.

Howe's final game in charge was a brutal 4-1 pre-season loss to Championship side Bristol City on Wednesday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of the pre-season friendly between Bristol City and Newcastle. Credit: Robins TV

When did Howe decide to leave Newcastle?

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie:

Eddie Howe informed his coaching staff upon return from Bristol City, where they lost 4-1 in a friendly. The decision had nothing to do with the match, it had been in the pipeline for two weeks.

Howe gave his full commitment to the club at the end of the season, but has changed his mind. He is set to take a break from football and Howe wanted the club to have a replacement lined up before he left.

This is Howe's decision, the club tried to convince him to stay. He feels he has taken it as far as he can after nearly five years at the helm.

There is no acrimony, the club love him and think he's done an amazing job.

The players have yet to be told. They are on a day off today. The squad fly out to Spain for a pre-season training camp on Friday. Newcastle are yet to comment or put out a statement.

This is not ideal timing as far as the club are concerned, but they are moving swiftly to try and replace Howe. They are in advanced talks with Jaissle of Al Alhi, having also spoken to Antonio Conte and Kieran McKenna.

'I cannot assure Bruno future' - Howe's final words as boss

In his final words as Newcastle boss, Howe refused to offer assurances over the future of captain Guimaraes amid heavy interest from Arsenal - but added the player is not in control of his own future.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this month that Guimaraes had told Newcastle he would like to leave the club in favour of a move to the Premier League champions, but the Magpies had no intention of selling the 28-year-old Brazil international.

Asked about Guimaraes, who is yet to rejoin his team-mates following the World Cup, Howe said on Wednesday night: "Assurances - I don't think you can push too hard for those. I think I've said many times you want players that are committed.

"Bruno's always been committed here. His training performances, his game performances, have been outstanding. Every time he's worn the shirt, he's played with the fans by his side. I'd love to see that continue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at when Arsenal target Guimaraes took on the Gunners in a fiery clash at St James' Park in 2023

"I think we want to keep all of our best players. They're so valuable, and as I said numerous times, there aren't many of them, and to get them and develop them is so difficult.

"So when you have them, you want to keep them. And Bruno's very much in that category; he's an outstanding player."

Asked if this saga dragging on creates a negative mood, Howe replied: "Any distraction, if it's not healthy, is unhealthy. So, yeah.

"But we're not in control of that. And to some degree, I don't think Bruno's in control of that either.

"What will be, will be. We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done."

Bothroyd: Newcastle in relegation scrap without Howe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Arsenal and England striker Jay Bothroyd worries for Newcastle following the departure of Howe and predicts they could end up in a relegation battle this season

Sky Sports News' Jay Bothroyd:

"There's so many players leaving, so to be honest I can understand why he [Howe] would want to leave now.

"He's saying: 'I had a strong squad. You've taken away some of the best players I had. Some of the best players in the Premier League. You're replacing them with unproven players in the Premier League.'

"It seems to me that he doesn't have the control he wants. He doesn't want to see these players leave.

"It's just really bad times for Newcastle, yet again. This is even worse than last year. Losing [Alexander] Isak and him not turning up to training is one thing, but now you're losing one of the best managers in the country and all your best players.

"Where do Newcastle go from here? It's going to be an unproven manager because who wants to put themselves in a situation where you don't have a strong side.

"I said mid-table [as a Premier League prediction]. Now I'm saying bottom half of the table.

"They're way off it. They're going to be in a relegation battle this year."

Your views on Howe's exit...

HullToon: I cannot believe it. Does he feel supported enough? Does the project still match the original plan that he set out for? There are so many questions raised because of this. Last season was disappointing, but there's mitigating circumstances.

JimmiDee: Regardless of last years disappointment, Howe has done an unbelievable job, and he's had to put up with his team being pillaged the last two seasons and expected to produce the same results with bargain bin replacements which is just completely unrealistic. He deserves better.

SPritc80: A section of our short sighted fans are to blame for Eddie leaving and some big hitters choosing to leave. Results have not gone our way at times. Jumping on the back of players and the head coach in the way they have is disrespectful. No wonder they are all leaving.

BrettJ2002: Why didn't Eddie Howe decide to do this before pre-season started so new manager can get a lot more time in with the squad? Thanks to Eddie for what he has done, but his time was definitely up.

Chris W: Strongly support Eddie - that's two new statues we need this month!

Fez71: Didn't look like Eddie was getting backed, selling all our best players. Very sad times, thanks for all the memories, Eddie.

Sports.title: Norrie into Los Cabos quarter-finals as Osaka advances in Washington
Sports.content:
Cameron Norrie continued his return to form at the Los Cabos Open by beating James Duckworth in straight sets to reach the quarter-finals.

Norrie had lost six successive matches across clay and grass before starting his summer hard-court campaign with victory over Aleksandar Kovacevic on Monday night.

The British No 2 backed up that performance with a 6-4 6-4 win over Duckworth on Wednesday evening to set up a last-eight clash with another Australian, Bernard Tomic.

Norrie lost his first service game of the match to fall 2-0 down, but would then claim two successive breaks of serve himself to take a 4-3 lead, before routinely closing the set out with a couple of holds.

The 30-year-old looked to be cruising to victory when he went up a double break in the second set to lead 5-2, but had to survive a brief wobble before getting over the line.

Osaka, who is seeded third, will face Italy's Elisabetta Cocciaretto in the last eight.

On Thursday, all eyes will be on an all-Australian clash on the main stadium court as top seed Alex de Minaur takes on qualifier Cruz Hewitt, the 17-year-old son of former world No 1 Lleyton Hewitt.

Sports.title: Fleming frontrunner to become England Test coach
Sports.content:
Former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming is the frontrunner to be appointed as England men's Test head coach.

The 53-year-old appears set to succeed compatriot Brendon McCullum, who was sacked after the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June.

Fleming recently left his role as head coach of Indian Premier League franchise Chennai Super Kings, having been in charge of the T20 outfit since 2009, the year after his playing career ended.

The task facing England's next Test head coach is to revive a side that have lost eight of their last 12 matches across a 2-2 home draw with India last summer, the 4-1 Ashes battering in Australia over the winter and the recent era-ending 2-1 reverse against New Zealand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brendon McCullum speaks on what it will be like working with a new coach for England as well as the future of their white-ball side.

It remains unclear whether Fleming, if appointed, will be in charge for England's upcoming three-Test series against Pakistan - live on Sky Sports - which starts at Headingley on August 19.

Assistant coach Marcus Trescothick could serve as interim boss for the Pakistan series in the event Fleming was unable to start work immediately, with England's next Test fixtures after the end of the home summer not coming until December's tour of South Africa.

England also currently remain without a permanent Test captain following Ben Stokes' retirement at the end of the New Zealand series.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron Finch gives his thoughts on the current environment in the England test cricket team and what he believes is going on behind the scenes.

Former skipper Joe Root stepped in to replace Stokes for the second Test against New Zealand and appears to be the only credible alternative to Test vice-captain and white-ball skipper Harry Brook.

After three Tests in South Africa across December and January, England meet Australia in the day-night 150th-anniversary Test in Melbourne in March ahead of next year's home Ashes series between June 18-August 2.

Fleming familiar with English cricket

Sky Sports' Adam Williams:

Former Black Caps captain Fleming was a team-mate of McCullum's during his stellar Test career in which he averaged just over 40 with the bat.

The 53-year-old stood down as Chennai Super Kings head coach in July after an 18-year association with the franchise as both a player and coach that saw him win a record five IPL titles.

Fleming is familiar with the county set-up from his time as playing for Middlesex, Yorkshire and Nottinghamshire, who he captained to the County Championship title in 2005.
