Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Pyramid and Bintward headline Wolverhampton feature
Sports.content:
Wolverhampton is the centre of attention on Thursday night, with eight races scheduled on the all-weather, all live on Sky Sports Racing.

5.47 Wolverhampton - Exciting newcomers Pyramid and Bintward headline

Exciting newcomers Pyramid and Bintward headline a classy field of eight for the attheraces.com/marketmovers Maiden Stakes.

The Juddmonte-owned Kingman colt Pyramid has a fine pedigree, being related to the likes of Fingerpoint and Set Piece. With his trainers John and Thady Gosden arriving in red-hot form, he ought to go close under Rab Havlin.

Bintward cost a whopping €780,000 at the Deauville Arqana yearling sale and has been given plenty of time by his trainer Roger Varian. A daughter of Night Of Thunder, she is sure to be popular with Sean Dylan Bowen in the saddle.

Chimes Of Thunder rates the best of those with racecourse experience and William Haggas' 76-rated filly will hope to put that to good use as she switches to the all-weather. Sea The Stars filly Walking On Stars made little impression on debut

6.22 Wolverhampton - Angel Sense and Supreme Star seek first success

Angel Sense and Supreme Star feature among 12 runners for an open-looking Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes.

The Marco Botti-trained Angel Sense had finished in the first three on his opening three starts before suffering a heavy defeat when favourite at Newbury and he could be involved if able to bounce back.

Stablemate Supreme Star improved on his debut to finish an excellent second at Nottingham last month and that form entitles him to hit the frame.

Fresh from his Group Two win earlier this week, Kaiya Fraser will be looking for further successes and rides Location Location - who kept on when second at Thirsk on his last start and must be feared. Archie Watson's Ouragan is another for the shortlist, having ran well at Newbury the last day. If she adapts to the tapeta, she could trouble the judge.

10.14 Saratoga - Survie and Gezora seek Grade Two honours

A fantastic renewal of the Grade Two Glens Falls Stakes sees ex-European runners Gezora and Survie clash at Saratoga.

Gezora enjoyed a fruitful campaign last season, winning the Prix de Diane and Breeders' Cup Filly & Mare Turf when trained by Francis-Henri Graffard. However, she is yet to score since heading to the United States. Second in the Modesty Stakes at Churchill Downs on her first start of the campaign, she failed to fire when well beaten in the New York Stakes and has a point to prove on debut for Bill Mott.

Survie has been a fine servant for her connections picking up over £700,000 in prize money in her eighteen starts. George Boughey's five-year-old has run with credit on her last couple of runs at Newmarket and Royal Ascot and could be suited by this sharp 12-furlong test.

Last-time winners Massarat and Dona Clota make each-way appeal in a superb heat.

Sports.title: 'All to play for!' - Why Norris can still retain his F1 title
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris is capable of pulling off a stunning fightback to retain his Formula 1 drivers' title, according to Sky Sports F1's David Croft.

Norris claimed his and McLaren's first victory of the season in Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix to reduce his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 91 points as the sport enters its summer break with 11 of 23 currently scheduled rounds complete.

The emphatic nature of Norris' victory after McLaren brought a significant upgrade package to the Hungaroring has created hope that the Woking squad may have permanently joined the battle for victories, and that the Brit can surge back into title contention.

Spotify Spotify , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Spotify cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Spotify cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Spotify cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

Speaking on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show podcast, Croft suggested that the crucial factor will be whether McLaren can continue to outperform Antonelli's Mercedes team.

Croft said: "One of the big things coming out of the summer break, can McLaren carry this on? Are they going to put their eggs in a Lando Norris basket? And is it going to come up trumps once again?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

The Constructors' Championship, I think, is still very much up for grabs. The Drivers' Championship, I don't think Lando is that far behind that he can't make up a deficit.

"And seriously, I haven't even gone on holiday yet. I can't wait to get back to business at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort. I don't want a three-week break; I want the racing thick and fast!"

Can McLaren maintain form?

One of McLaren's weaknesses so far this season has been their inability to get full productivity out of the power unit supplied to them by Mercedes, which the Silver Arrows have better exploited.

The fact that Hungary is one of the least demanding circuits on the calendar from a power-unit perspective leaves some doubt as to whether McLaren can replicate the performance elsewhere.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater runs through the biggest talking points from the Hungarian GP as Norris finally wins in 2026, Hamilton gets another penalty, Piastri fumes at McLaren's strategy and Antonelli tops the Drivers' Standings heading into the summer break

However, Croft pointed out that the Hungaroring has similarities to Monaco, where Mercedes were still able to win in early June.

"We're 11 races into the season now, and I think McLaren are understanding the power unit way better than they were at the start of the year," Croft said.

"Is it a surprise they did so well in Hungary? Well, on past form, no, they were one-two for the last two years in Budapest.

"But it is a little surprise given how strong Mercedes were in Monaco. I mean, that might be driver-specific in that respect. It might just be that Kimi was exceptional that weekend. But I don't think the Mercedes are necessarily weak at a track like Budapest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris reacts to his first win of 2026, saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

"What delighted me in terms of stronger competition to the championship leaders, and we want to see this championship go right to the wire because that's way more fun, was that McLaren's upgrade worked.

"They've taken their time this year to play catch-up, but they are now catching up, I think. And I think the signs were there right from the start as Lando built up the pace into the weekend that this was a good upgrade, they had the pace, and they were ready to challenge Mercedes."

Bernie: All to play for after summer break

There remains some doubt over whether all 12 of the remaining scheduled rounds will be able to go ahead due to ongoing conflict in the Middle East, but Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins thinks there is time for Norris to turn things around regardless.

"I think this year is going to be about upgrades," Collins said on The F1 Show podcast. "It's going to be about who can get on top of these cars, who can get the best out of the cars, the best out of the engines.

"At the moment as the calendar sets, we've done 11 rounds; we've got 12 still to go. So there's still lots and lots of points on the board."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris snatches pole off Lewis Hamilton as Max Verstappen and George Russell struggle in Q3 at Hungaroring

Max Verstappen trailed then championship leader Oscar Piastri by 104 points with nine rounds remaining last season, before fighting back to ultimately finish just two points behind title winner Norris in the final standings.

Collins added: "We've seen McLaren this weekend at least have a little bit of the upper hand. And maybe Mercedes have been a bit distracted with each other in some of the earlier races as well.

"So, I think that it's still all to play for. I think you've pretty much got three cars, maybe Verstappen as well in that fight, that I think who knows as we go through later races who will be at the front week in, week out. And that's really interesting to watch."

The former world No 4 has endured an injury-strewn 2026 which saw him miss all three Grand Slam tournaments, but he enters the National Bank Open after a late withdrawal from this week's DC Open in Washington.

The Brit, who is coached by Sir Andy Murray, has slipped to world No 147 in the ATP rankings, leaving him likely to face qualifying if he is to compete at September's US Open after missing out on direct entry into the main draw.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe leaves Newcastle United after almost five years in charge
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left his role as Newcastle United head coach after 231 games and just under five years at St James’ Park.

His exit comes in the wake of a 4-1 defeat by Bristol City in a pre-season friendly at Ashton Gate on Wednesday evening, after which he hinted at changes at the club. “There has been a lot of change at the football club and potentially more to come,” he said when asked about his optimism ahead of the new season.

Howe was hired in November 2021 to replace Steve Bruce as the manager of Premier League club. In January 2023, the 48-year-old former Bournemouth manager guided Newcastle to Carabao Cup triumph, their first major silverware since 1955. Howe oversaw Champions League qualifications via a fourth-place league finish in 2022-23.

Despite considerable investment from their Saudi backers, Newcastle underperformed last season, finishing in 12th place last season, a slump from fifth place in the previous campaign. From 7 January, they won just five of their last 17 league games.

The club have been depleted by the departures of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and England forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona in recent weeks. Speculation continues over the future of captain Bruno Guimaraes.

The club are due to be heading to south-east Spain later this week to step up their preparations for the new season. Included on their itinerary is a visit to La Liga side Valencia on Saturday 8 August for their annual Trofeu Taronja (Orange Cup) game.

Sports.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
Sports.content:
Uefa has called an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A European boycott of Fifa tournaments is among the options under consideration.

As the next major event in the Fifa calendar, a boycott of next year’s Women’s World Cup has been ­mentioned in preliminary ­discussions, although there would be a reluctance in some quarters to make the women’s game suffer as a consequence of a protest against Fifa proposals that primarily revolve around ­monetising the men’s World Cup and Club World Cup.

Uefa’s initial condemnation of Fifa’s plan to “sell the soul” of ­football has received strong backing from Concacaf – the North, Central ­American and Caribbean ­confederation – and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). If their members follow their leads there should be sufficient votes to block the proposal.

Those three confederations make up 143 of the 211 Fifa members, but unanimity is not guaranteed, as was made clear when Czechia’s ­football association became the first in Europe to back the plan.

Having received more than 200 ­letters of endorsement backing his re-election next year, Infantino is confident he has enough votes – although it is unclear whether the proposal requires a simple ­majority to be passed. Several sources have said that creating a new commercial entity – Fifa Forward Enterprise [FFE] – and selling a 20% stake to investors would necessitate a change of Fifa statutes, which requires a 75% majority that would be much harder to obtain.

View image in fullscreen Fifa’s branding was impossible to miss during the World Cup. Photograph: Mike Segar/Reuters

On Wednesday evening, Infantino released a video to address the ­backlash. “FFE is actually a ­proposal, an offer,” he said. “It’s part of a democratic process – a ­consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an ­obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally.”

Earlier, Uefa redoubled its attack on Fifa by accusing the world ­governing body of “using our sport to enrich themselves and their friends” after it emerged that ­Infantino had ­presented members with a deadline of 19 September to decide whether to apply for an ­initial payment of $20m (£15m) from the proposed sell-off.

A further $20m for each ­association would also be made available at a later date, although it is unclear whether accepting the money would equate to a formal ­endorsement and therefore remove the need for a vote.

“Today we have learned of Fifa’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn,” Uefa said. “This says everything you need to know about this plan. But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition to Fifa’s scheme. Fifa cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.”

Uefa’s second statement of condemnation followed a similarly strong intervention from ­Concacaf, which is particularly ­significant given the confederation has just hosted the most ­lucrative World Cup and covers the region that has brought the proposed new investment from the New York-based Thrive Eternal.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, was instrumental in the success of the US, Mexican and Canadian bid for the tournament, but along with the seven other Fifa vice‑presidents and Fifa council members he was kept in the dark over the plans.

“Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” Concacaf said. “We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the ­disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the ­relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, Fifa, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino announces Saudi Arabia as the 2034 World Cup hosts. The AFC’s statement is understood to have the backing of the Saudi Arabian federation. Photograph: Fifa

“This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the Fifa family will act in the same manner.”

The AFC issued a similar statement of disapproval, which significantly is understood to have the backing of the Saudi Arabian football federation, a close ally of Infantino and the host of the 2034 World Cup.

“The AFC was not consulted on the proposal and is disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels,” it said.

“While the AFC recognises the importance of exploring innovative approaches that can strengthen the future of global football, initiatives of this scale and consequence must be founded upon the principles of good governance, transparency and meaningful consultation.

“Decisions that may reshape the commercial and financial future of the game require comprehensive prior engagement with confederations, member associations and other relevant stakeholders before any proposal is made to the appropriate decision-making bodies.”

Elite clubs also expressed their unhappiness, with the European Football Clubs organisation pointing out that Fifa had not consulted it despite the two bodies having signed a memorandum of understanding.

“As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in Fifa’s competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude,” it said.

“EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media.”

Sports.title: Experimental Liverpool down Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s winner
Sports.content:
Liverpool turned the Empire State Building red when launching a new away kit on Tuesday but neither they nor Wrexham could illuminate Yankee Stadium 24 hours later. It was rough in the diamond, although Rio Ngumoha’s deflected goal made it two wins out of two for Andoni Iraola on his first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach.

Ngumoha, a second half substitute who Iraola deployed on the right, satisfied the majority of a 42,204 crowd with a 75th-minute shot that looped in off Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt. Wrexham’s Hollywood co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) were in attendance for what the former had labelled a “punch-me moment” but in truth few blows were traded at the iconic baseball stadium.

Liverpool’s preparations for the second game of pre-season were not exactly smooth, in fairness to Iraola’s team. Their flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday night with players and staff on the tarmac ready to take off. Poor weather conditions in the New York area delayed their arrival until the day of the game, and Liverpool only checked into their Midtown hotel around midday. They were flying back to Chicago straight after the match too.

Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch did not make the trip from Liverpool’s training base despite joining up with the squad following their post-World Cup holidays. The game came too early in their pre-season preparations to be considered. With Joe Gomez injured and Federico Chiesa also absent through illness, Iraola had little choice but to select another young and experimental side. Six of Liverpool’s starting line-up had no Premier League experience whatsoever but at least the emphasis on youth offered the crowd a glimpse of the highly-rated Joshua Abe.

View image in fullscreen Joshua Abe reacts after failing to score at Yankee Stadium. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

Abe, a pacy and prolific right winger, is regarded as one of the brightest prospects in the country and was inundated with offers before committing his future to Liverpool when turning 16 earlier this month. Manchester City, Manchester United and Chelsea were all interested in the Warrington-born England youth international, with deals worth £40,000-a-week reportedly on his table. There was understandable relief inside Anfield when he agreed scholarship terms in June with a three-year professional contract to follow on his 17th birthday next July.

Abe could have marked his first senior Liverpool start with an early goal when released clear of the Wrexham defence by Harvey Elliott. A heavy first touch gave the Wrexham and former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward opportunity to save at the feet of the teenager. Iraola started with a front line of Calum Scanlon, Lewis Koumas and Abe. Koumas went close from distance and had a penalty shout waved away but, aside from a few surging midfield runs by Dominik Szoboszlai, it was a quiet friendly.

Wrexham are further along in their pre-season work – their first competitive game is a week on Friday against Middlesbrough in the Carabao Cup – and it showed as the first half progressed and Phil Parkinson’s team gained a physical edge. Sam Smith and Callum Doyle were unable to trouble Giorgi Mamardashvili with the chances that fell their way.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Abe, Scanlon, Milos Kerkez and Trey Nyoni were replaced at half-time by Ngumoha, Kieran Morrison, Kostas Tsimikas and Curtis Jones respectively. Elliott was presented with a sight of the Wrexham goal by Koumas minutes after the restart but his first-time shot from 20 yards was well saved by Ward. The Wales international also denied Szoboszlai from distance but this was a Liverpool performance – and pre-season friendly – that failed to ignite.

Wrexham substitute Nathan Broadhead almost succeeded with a powerful drive from 25 yards that was pushed away by Mamardashvili. Brunt and Kieffer Moore both had good late chances to equalise but miscued from close range.

Sports.title: WSL brings back Sunday evening kick-offs after indifferent viewing figures
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League will bring back Sunday evening kick-offs this season as part of an overhaul of its broadcast strategy after indifferent viewing figures last season.

The Guardian has learned that the WSL will offer six different TV slots to broadcasters after releasing its fixtures for the 2026-27 campaign later on Thursday in a significant change from last season, when the majority of televised games took place on Saturday and Sunday lunchtimes.

Sky Sports, which has the live rights for 163 of the WSL’s 182 games, retains the Saturday 12.45pm slot and noon on Sundays, but has also been given new regular kick-off times of 7pm on Friday and 6pm on Sunday.

The BBC will broadcast 19 matches live at 12.30pm on Saturdays and 2.30pm on Sundays.

The WSL’s new strategy is to spread games across the weekend after scheduling most fixtures at noon on Sundays last season, with multiple televised matches kicking off at the same time in a move that diluted the audience.

The change this season follows a lengthy consultation with broadcasters, clubs and fans, with the WSL seeking a schedule that maximises its TV audience and matchday attendances.

The Sunday evening kick-off was dropped last season after negative feedback from clubs and fans, as attendances were generally poor, but it was popular with broadcasters and was Sky’s best performing slot in 2024-25 with an average audience of 144,000.

In an attempt to balance these competing interests, the Sunday evening game will mostly be brought forward 45 minutes to 6pm – with some changes likely to avoid clashes with the 4.30pm Premier League games – while the WSL will attempt to schedule derbies for that slot and Friday evenings where possible.

The Guardian revealed last December that the WSL was considering further changes to its kick-off times this season after concern from Sky in particular at some of their viewing figures for lunchtime games.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

An average audience of 59,000 watched Sky’s live coverage of Arsenal’s home win over Liverpool that month, even fewer than the 71,000 people who watched Arsenal v Chelsea on Sky in the same noon kick-off slot the previous month.

As well as struggling to attract a casual audience the decision to schedule up to four of the six weekly matches at the same time proved unpopular with the most committed WSL fans, who were unable to watch multiple matches live.

Sky are paying the vast majority of the joint £65m broadcast deal with the BBC, who are believed to contribute around £8m in rights fees, so have a significant say but the WSL has consulted widely.

Sports.title: England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars
Sports.content:
With each passing World Cup I am reminded of the times I spent in the company of those wonderful “Boys of 66”. What a privilege it was getting to know them in a much simpler era when, unlike today’s mollycoddled stars, household names remained unaffected by money and fame.

Where were you on 30 July 1966, the day England won the World Cup? I was at my nan and grandad’s house. They had a minute television which seemed no bigger than a matchbox. Intermittently the picture, which was in black and white, would roll around the screen. It was infuriating. My grandad talked about needing to get the “horizontal hold fixed” (unless you are of a certain age you will need to Google that). I was nine years old.

Thirty years (of hurt) on from that final, there was a knock at my front door. It was a surreal experience to see Geoff Hurst standing on my doorstep and even more bizarre as he went to one end of my front room and stood behind the settee. I went to the other end and sat on a chair.

Geoff, England’s World Cup hat- trick hero, had come to my house to rehearse his after-dinner speech. The settee acted as a makeshift top table. I was the only member of his audience.

His performance began. “I was at Paddington station one day and a chap came running up to me and said, ‘Geoff, Geoff, I’ve been waiting 20 years to meet you, I know exactly where I was that day in 1966 when you scored your hat-trick.’ ‘Where was that?’ asked Geoff. ‘Pentonville prison,’ replied the man. ‘We were so happy we smashed the cell up.’”

View image in fullscreen Geoff Hurst, shown speaking at an FA gala dinner in 2013, is a natural performer. Photograph: WPA/Getty Images

I had written some of Geoff’s script and I helped him with his presentation, but he quickly became a natural performer.

Another of Geoff’s stories provides a fascinating insight into how the manager, Alf Ramsey, made sure his players never became complacent. In one England match Hurst played in, after the World Cup final, the players returned to the team hotel. They said their goodbyes and Hurst turned to Ramsey and said: “See you next time Alf.”

“Perhaps, Geoff, perhaps,” replied Ramsey. Geoff said it was a comment that really made him think that, despite scoring a hat-trick, his place wasn’t guaranteed.

Ramsey’s starting salary as England manager was £4,500 a year rising to a maximum of £5,000. He also asked the Football Association to help him buy a house.

In the 1980s, and for many years afterwards, there was a huge circuit of sporting dinners. They were often in the north of England and held at the traditional working men’s clubs. Many of the 1966 England team were regular performers. Unlike today’s Premier League stars, who earn hundreds of thousands of pounds a month the “Boys of 66” supplemented their income by performing on the circuit, which is where I got to know them.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Charlton raises the Jules Rimet trophy in the air after the 1966 final at Wembley. Photograph: Hulton Archive/Getty Images

Sometimes they would do their own routines, on other occasions I would interview them and tee them up for their anecdotes. On stage one night I said to Jack Charlton: “Jack, how’s your brother Bobby?” Bobby could sometimes be very serious and he didn’t smile very often. “Not great” replied Jack. “Oh, why’s that?” I enquired. “Well, he’s now been banned from his local pub, the landlord said he didn’t want him there during the happy hour.”

Those England players were involved in English sport’s greatest day but you would never have known. They didn’t act like unapproachable superstars. If I left a message on their home answerphone they would call straight back. It was so different to the majority of football personalities I tried to interview in later years for the BBC.

Some of the events I worked at with the 1966 team were for amateur football clubs. We would be part of the entertainment alongside a tribute act, or a local comedian. The evening would sometimes start with a game of bingo. One dinner was very different. I was asked by the Institute of Directors to host a show and book as many of the England team as possible for a corporate lunch in London. I waited in the green room and they started filling in. It was like being in a dream and I imagined I was in the Wembley dressing room. In they trooped: George Cohen, Ray Wilson, Nobby Stiles, Hurst, Roger Hunt, Alan Ball, Martin Peters, Bobby and Jack Charlton, and for good measure BBC TV’s Kenneth Wolstenholme, who delivered the greatest commentary line in the history of sports broadcasting.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Stiles was a great raconteur. One of his favourite anecdotes was based around the game England played against Argentina in the quarter-final. Before the match, Nobby, the hard man of the team, was taken to one side by Ramsey. “Nobby, Argentina’s best player is Antonio Rattín, I want you to mark Rattín,” said Ramsey. After a perfectly timed pause Nobby delivered the punchline: “Alf, do you want me to mark him for the match or for his entire life?”

View image in fullscreen England’s manager Alf Ramsey (left) celebrates his team’s 4-2 victory over West Germany with the captain, Bobby Moore, and Nobby Stiles. Photograph: Keystone/Getty Images

It was a story that brought the house down.

In 1982 I was asked by Ian Thomas, my editor at BBC Radio Sport, to meet Ramsey at Liverpool Street station. Ramsey had been booked by the BBC to give his reaction to the draw for the 1982 World Cup finals. He immediately reminded me of Captain Mainwaring from Dad’s Army. He spoke with a posh voice, in clipped tones, and came across as a very serious man. I was just 24 years old, and I couldn’t believe my luck.

These were very different times. I still find it incredible that, on the morning of the 1966 final, Peters told me that, “time seemed to be dragging” so some of the players went shopping on Hendon’s high street. And after England’s win at Wembley the FA arranged an evening banquet for the players but, astonishingly, their wives were not invited. The players were very angry and when the dinner finished Hurst told me that he and several of the other players and their wives headed to Danny La Rue’s cabaret club.

How times have changed and how lucky was I knowing the 1966 team? They were humble and really fun to be with and I still find it incredible that I spent so many great times with them.

Garry Richardson presents a special 1966 World Cup anniversary programme on Boom Radio on 30 July

Sports.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
Sports.content:
Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta.

As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

The dispute over the islands, which have been ruled by Britain since 1833, is long running and led to a 74-day conflict in 1982, during which more than 900 people – 649 Argentinians and 255 Britons – lost their lives.

Fifa’s disciplinary code ­prohibits “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature” and the banner prompted political debate on both sides of the ­Atlantic. A spokesperson for the then UK prime minister, Keir Starmer, said: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands ­definitely are.” Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House Fifa taskforce, defended Argentina’s players, saying the US believed in free speech.

The incident was not the first time an Argentina team had expressed such sentiments. In 2014, Fifa fined Argentina £20,000 for a far larger banner held ‌up by players before a friendly with Slovenia in La Plata.

Fifa’s full World Cup charge sheet against the Argentinian Football Association also includes ­“discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches”.

0:18 Ugly scenes as Argentina lose World Cup final – video

Several players are also under investigation in relation to the ­chaotic scenes that followed ­Argentina’s 1-0 extra-time defeat by Spain in the final. As Spain attempted to celebrate, ­altercations broke out across the pitch at New York New Jersey Stadium.

The Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes, who was seen wrestling Spain’s Eric García to the ground, faces three counts of assault under the Fifa disciplinary code, while the defender Nahuel Molina faces two counts of assault (one completed and one attempted) and one count of unsporting behaviour.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The assistant coach, Roberto Ayala, faces one count of assault, and Thiago Almada, an unused substitute in the final, one count of unsporting behaviour. Spain’s Gavi also faces an unsporting behaviour charge.

“In accordance with the Fifa ­disciplinary code, the respondents have now been provided with the opportunity to present their position, following which a decision will be issued by the Fifa disciplinary committee in due course,” said Fifa.

Sports.title: ‘I’m very sorry’: Mancini apologises after being reappointed as Italy head coach
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini issued an apology in his first public comments after being reappointed as the Italy head coach, three years after he abandoned the same job for a lucrative contract with Saudi Arabia.

“I’m very sorry,” Mancini said. “It was like losing the woman of your life. And it means you did something that shouldn’t have been done. So I’m sorry, very sorry also for everything that happened over these last three years … I’m going to try to bring the national team back where it belongs.”

Italy failed for a third straight time to qualify for the World Cup, prompting the resignations of Gabriele Gravina as federation president and Gennaro Gattuso as head coach in April, shortly after the playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The 61-year-old Mancini led the Azzurri to the European Championship title in 2021 but resigned as Italy coach in August 2023, taking over Saudi Arabia’s national team two weeks later. “It was completely my fault,” Mancini said, referring to a lack of communication with Gravina.

Mancini’s first match back in charge will be against Belgium in the Nations League on 25 September at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome. He was asked about what type of reception fans might give him. “I realise some people will be against me,” Mancini said. “I’m hoping the squad plays well enough that maybe people will forgive me.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Mancini was fourth-choice option for the Italy job after Carlo Ancelotti and Pep Guardiola turned it down and Andrea Pirlo was dropped as a candidate amid political concerns over a sponsorship deal with a Russian betting firm.

Sports.title: Manchester City leading opposition to Premier League’s £1.5bn EFL proposal
Sports.content:
Manchester City are leading the opposition to the Premier League’s plans to offer £1.5bn to the English Football League in a landmark financial settlement which will be discussed at a meeting of the 20 clubs on Thursday.

The Premier League wants to put its proposed offer, which would be spread over 10 years, to a vote in the hope of getting the matter resolved before the start of the season, but City are understood to have come up with a counterproposal amid concerns about how the package will be funded.

A number of City’s misgivings are shared by other members of the so-called big six, who will be asked to pay more than other Premier League clubs towards the New Deal for Football, but it is unclear how many of them are prepared to back their rivals.

City remain short of allies within the top flight as they wait for the much-anticipated judgment of an independent tribunal after being charged with 115 breaches of financial fair play rules, despite settling a long-running legal dispute with the Premier League over its associated party transaction rules last year.

Quick Guide How do I 

The Guardian has learned that City irritated several clubs by submitting a series of late amendments to proposed rule changes before the Premier League’s annual general meeting in June, which were defeated by 19 votes to one.

City and other big clubs are understood to be unhappy with the Premier League’s proposal to fund the financial redistribution package by increasing the levy on transfer fees from 4% to 6%, which would leave the bigger spending clubs with a large bill. The Premier League will only ballot clubs on Thursday if it is confident of getting the 14 votes required for the proposal to pass, with sources describing executives as cautiously optimistic despite facing some opposition.

At an average of £150m a year, the Premier League’s proposed contribution has not altered significantly since a similar offer of £750m over five years was put forward in September 2023, although it has doubled the length of the deal.

If approved by the clubs and accepted by the EFL an initial payment of £100m would be made this season, with larger contributions to be made in subsequent years until the 2035-36 season.

It is unclear whether the EFL would accept the Premier League’s first offer however, with its chair, Rick Parry, believed to be holding out for a bigger deal.

If approved the EFL would allocate 80% of the New Deal to the Championship clubs, 12% to League One and 8% to League Two.

City and the Premier League declined to comment.

Sports.title: Leon Bailey left out of Aston Villa pre-season squad as he closes in on Premier League transfer
Sports.content:
Leon Bailey left out of Aston Villa pre-season squad as he closes in on Premier League transfer

Leon Bailey has not travelled with the Aston Villa squad on their pre-season trip to Asia as an exit from the club nears.

The 28-year-old winger has been left out of Unai Emery's traveling group amid ongoing talks over a transfer to Hull City.

3 Bailey is set to leave Aston Villa for Hull after five years at the club Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Bailey's move to Hull is not done yet, but negotiations over the switch are progressing.

He is reported to still be training with Villa as he remains in the UK, while his teammates play two games in Indonesia and Thailand.

Villa face an Indonesian All Stars XI on Saturday, August 1, before taking on Thai side GB Pathum United on Tuesday, August 4.

Newly-promoted Hull have been linked with Bailey throughout the summer window so far, with owner Acun Ilicali hinting that talks were underway in a cryptic update last week.

In a message on social media, Ilicali posted 11 different national flags on X, with one of them being the Jamaica flag, which was believed to be related to Villa's Jamaican forward.

At the time, he stated that the transfer was 70 per cent complete, with talks now understood to have progressed.

On the move

Bailey looks set to leave Aston Villa after five years at the club, following a move from Bayer Leverkusen in 2021.

He played 163 times for Villa across that spell, scoring 23 goals and providing 25 assists across all competitions.

But his time at the club appears to be coming to an end after a tough campaign under Emery in the 2025/26 campaign.

After being sent out on loan to Roma last summer, he would eventually be recalled by Villa in January.

3 Bailey spent half of last season on loan at Roma before being recalled by Emery Credit: Getty

However, following his return, he would play just 452 minutes in the Premier League, providing one assist in 13 games.

Bailey also featured five times in the Europa League, but he didn't make a single start, playing 98 minutes in total.

He will hope that his potential move to Hull will bring more regular football on their return to the top flight this season.

Summer business continues

Emery is on the brink of losing Bailey, who will follow two other stars out of the door at Villa Park this summer.

Youri Tielemans has already departed for Manchester United, while Morgan Rogers has joined Chelsea in a record deal.

But Aston Villa have done some swift business to replace them, signing World Cup star Johan Manzambi, as well as Wolves midfielder Joao Gomes.

3 Hull owner Ilicali is closing in on his fourth summer signing after promotion Credit: Getty

And they have also signed Alejandro Garnacho on loan from Chelsea, with that deal including a conditional obligation to buy.

As for Hull, they have made three summer signings following promotion to the Premier League last term.

Jack Butland and Matt Targett have joined, with experienced Champions League star Hidemasa Morita signing too.

The Tigers are scheduled to play Aston Villa in their third game of the new season at the MKM Stadium on September 5.

So, Bailey won't have to wait long for a reunion with his old teammates should this move go through.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle as deal agreed for Saudi Pro League manager to replace him
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle as deal agreed for Saudi Pro League manager to replace him

Eddie Howe is set to leave his role as Newcastle manager, talkSPORT understands.

The Magpies have already agreed to appoint Matthias Jaissle, who currently manages Saudi Pro League side Al Ahli, as his replacement.

7 Howe will leave Newcastle after five years as manager Credit: Getty

It is understood that Howe informed the club he wanted to leave his role several weeks ago.

But he stayed on until the replacement was found, with Jaissle set to come straight in to take his place in the dugout.

Jaissle, who won back-to-back Asian Champions League titles with Al Ahli, has a release clause in his contract.

Meanwhile, Howe is now expected to take a break from football, as he has no plans for an immediate return to management.

However, he has been tipped to potentially replace Thomas Tuchel as England manager should the FA opt to make a change.

Shock departure

Howe has been Newcastle boss since 2021, but his shock departure comes just weeks before the new Premier League season.

The Magpies disappointingly finished 12th in the top flight last campaign under Howe, which led to concerns over his future.

But his exit, midway through the club's pre-season schedule, comes after the sale of star players Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.

Meanwhile, club captain Bruno Guimaraes is linked with a summer move to Arsenal.

And it is understood that Howe's frustration over the summer exits of his star players was a big factor in his decision to leave.

7 Howe delivered Newcastle's first trophy in 70 years by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025 Credit: Getty

7 Al Ahli manager Matthias Jaissle is set to replace Howe instantly Credit: Getty

Howe leaves Newcastle just over a year since he ended the club's 70-year-long wait for a domestic trophy.

He led the Toon to historic success in the Carabao Cup in 2025 and into the Champions League twice in recent seasons.

Across his 231 games in charge in all competitions, he won 116 of them, drawing 43 and losing 72.

His final match in charge was a 4-1 friendly loss to Bristol City on Wednesday evening.

Newcastle have another four friendlies to come before the new Premier League campaign, but they will potentially have Jaissle in charge for those remaining clashes.

Their top flight opener comes against Liverpool on Sunday, August 23 at 4:30pm, live on talkSPORT.

7 Howe won 116 of his 231 games in all competitions in charge of Newcastle

7 Howe is leaving Newcastle and he has no plans for an immediate return to management Credit: AFP

A telling conversation

Former Newcastle manager and England 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton's son, John, has revealed that he felt he knew Howe was going to leave after speaking to him recently.

"I spoke to Eddie in a local shop near where I live and we were having a conversation," he told talkSPORT Breakfast.

"We were maybe there for half an hour talking about Newcastle...I said to him: 'I suppose there's only one thing you can do, it's either yes I stay, or no I don't'.

"He said: 'Yeah, you're quite correct, that's the decision that needs to be made.'

"The conversation went on, talking about my dad, and when I left, I went to a friend of mine's house and the first thing I said to him was: 'Eddie Howe's going to leave'.

"Just by his demeanour and what he said, he didn't say he was leaving, but just by his body language and the way he was talking, he was very non-committal."

7 Jack Charlton's son, John, admitted he felt Howe would be leaving after a recent chat Credit: Getty

Newcastle fans react

Reacting to the news on talkSPORT on Thursday morning, Newcastle supporter Rich said: "My initial reaction was shock.

"I think he's great with young players and I was thinking with him still in charge and young players coming in, but I felt confident we would have a good season.

"Now he's left, it just seems a bit odd...very odd timing, I can't quite work out why he's left just when the World Cup players are coming back."

He added: "It's very bizarre. Last season wasn't the best and at the end of last season, everyone could have parted ways mutually after five years that have been full of highs and lows, leaving with your head held high and being the best Newcastle manager in 60 years.

"And then to leave now leaves a little bit of a sour taste in your mouth, he could have gone before pre-season started and the model got put into play."

Meanwhile, Magpies fan Andrew said: "I'm devastated. Absolutely devastated. If it was down to me, Howe would have been manager for the next 10 years.

7 Howe led Newcastle to the Champions League twice in his five-year spell Credit: Getty

"I think he's been let down by the owners, board, you've only got to look at how the club's being run, how many Directors of Football, different people coming in above him.

"I respect him for walking. We missed out on targets, we're signing young kids, losing our best players and apparently these owners are the richest people in the world.

"It's an absolute joke."

Sports.title: Liverpool told they have made a transfer mistake as list of free agents is revealed
Sports.content:
Liverpool told they have made a transfer mistake as list of free agents is revealed

While clubs have been busy splashing the cash this summer, it's worth remembering some of the huge names still available for free.

Manchester City, Tottenham and Chelsea have stolen the headlines in the Premier League so far this transfer window, with all three completing deals worth £100million or more.



10 Mohamed Salah bid an emotional farewell to Liverpool in May, and he is still yet to find a new club Credit: Getty

The Citizens kicked things off by breaking the transfer record for a British player by signing Ellliot Anderson for a fixed £116m fee from Nottingham Forest.

Spurs then joined the party by smashing their own biggest-ever fee for a player, poaching Sandro Tonali from Newcastle in a £100m deal.

But Anderson's reign as the most expensive British player lasted mere weeks, as Chelsea have now sealed the £117million capture of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.



While all of this has been going on though, there are some huge names that clubs across the globe can still nab at no extra cost.

Casemiro, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate may all have already sorted their next move, but there are plenty more free agents that remain up for grabs.



And talkSPORT's Rory Jennings and Ade Oladipo have taken a deep dive into this, putting together an XI made up of the best unattached stars who can save teams millions in transfer fees.

Back line

There are a number of goalkeepers still without a club, including Mathew Ryan and Neto, while Manchester City keeper Stefan Ortega this week joined Greek side Olympiacos.



Moving on to the back line, the talkSPORT Drive presenters had plenty to choose from and began with Dani Carvajal at right-back.

Arguably the best of his generation in the position, Carvajal left Real Madrid in the summer after two spells covering 23 years in which he won 27 major trophies, including six Champions League titles.

10 Dani Carvajal bid an emotional farewell in his last game for Real Madrid against Athletic Club in May Credit: Getty

10 Zinchenko played his last game for Arsenal in 2025 Credit: Getty



Slotting in on the opposite side of defence is another Premier League winner in ex-Arsenal and Man City left-back Oleksandr Zinchenko.

The Ukraine star is available after his short-term deal with Ajax ran out, who made just two appearances after joining in February before an ACL injury ruled him out of the rest of the campaign.

And while Zinchenko boasts four Premier League winners' medals on his CV, talkSPORT's Jennings believes his race is run at the top level.

Jennings said: “Zinchenko doesn't get a Premier League club. He was so out of his depth the second that he left Arsenal. Where would he go? What club? Name one Premier League club where he would get a game.”



At centre-back, John Stones and David Alaba made up the talkSPORT pairing at the heart of defence, following their respective departures from Manchester City and Real Madrid.

Stones recently brought a trophy-laden decade at City to an end, but is now set to join Italian champions Inter on a two-year deal.

10 John Stones is still a free agent, but that could soon change Credit: Getty

10 David Alaba featured just 16 times last season for Real Madrid Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Alaba left Madrid after seeing his last three years ravaged by injury, but returned to start for Austria at the World Cup, and has a strong reputation dating back to his 11-year stint at Bayern Munich.

On Stones, Oladipo said: “John Stones - without a club, still. He's probably going to go to Inter Milan.

“Obviously, for you [Jennings], second-best centre-back ever in the Premier League, England's greatest ever defender since Bobby Moore.”

As for Alaba, his co-host Jennings admitted the 34-year-old's age and lack of game time in the last three years - who has missed 126 in total for club and country - could stand in the way of any big moves.



Speaking on talkSPORT Drive, he said: “The problem is as well, the kind of club that he's going to want to go to, the kind of club that is going to satisfy him, is going to not want him. So, that's where they're kind of at an impasse.”

Midfield three

In midfield, Jennings and Oladipo named a trio of ex-Liverpool star Fabinho, former Bayern Munich enforcer Leon Goretzka and Colombia icon James Rodriguez.

10 Goretzka won seven Bundesliga titles and the Champions League whilst at Bayern Credit: Getty

10 Fabinho helped Liverpool to Premier League and Champions League glory in a glittering five years at Anfield Credit: getty



After leaving Anfield in 2023 having won the Premier League in 2020, Fabinho has since spent three years with Al Ittihad in the Saudi Pro League, before his contract expired at the end of last season.

Meanwhile, at 31, Goretzka is available on a free transfer after leaving Bayern Munich having won 15 trophies in eight years at the club.

But neither of the duo appealed to Jennings, who claimed Fabinho's legs 'fell off' in his final season at Liverpool three years ago, while he insisted Goretzka will 'Get a club if he wants one', but not in the Premier League.

As for Rodriguez, Colombia's 2014 World Cup star left MLS side Minnesota United in May after just four months in the USA, and talkSPORT's Oladipo had some harsh words for the 35-year-old.



He joked about the ex-Real Madrid player who also popped up for a stint at Everton: "Minnesota United said: ‘You're not good enough’ - just let it go. Even Saudis won't respond to the emails.”

Attack

There were some household names in talkSPORT's free agent front three, with none other than Mohamed Salah kicking things off.

10 Salah left Liverpool as a certified club and Premier League legend Credit: Getty

Arguably the biggest player currently available, the Egyptian King bid an emotional farewell to Anfield after a glittering nine years which saw him win nine trophies, whilst scoring 257 goals.



While Salah endured a disappointing final season in Red as the team, scoring just seven league goals, Jennings insisted that he would still back him to perform at the highest level.

He said: "I think Mohamed Salah is worthy of playing still Premier League football, arguably for Liverpool.

“Arguably for Liverpool, considering that the players that were signed last season were supposed to take the baton on from him, haven't exactly hit the ground running.

“There have been injury issues as well. I think you could argue that Mohamed Salah could actually play a role for Andoni Iraola.”



Another huge name joined Salah on Oladipo and Jennings' team sheet, in the form of four-time Premier League winner Raheem Sterling.

Having starred for Liverpool and Man City at the peak of his career, Sterling's career has dipped in recent years, and was not offered a new contract at Dutch side Feyenoord at the end of last season, months after joining in February.

Though still just 31, Jennings admitted his time at the top could be over already, after scoring 174 goals in 585 games at club level.

10 Raheem Sterling failed to score in eight games for Feyenoord Credit: Getty



10 Dusan Vlahovic was rated at the time of his move to Juventus as one of Europe's brightest attacking talents Credit: Getty

Hailing Sterling, the talkSPORT host said: “There comes a time in your career when it's over, and I think for Raheem Sterling [it is], and I say this with celebration, not with cynicism.

“Raheem Sterling will go down as a Premier League great. He will be in the Premier League Hall of Fame. He's scored over 100 Premier League goals.

“He was integral to one of the greatest teams ever assembled [at Man City]. That team, they scored over 100 goals and accrued over 100 points.”



Rounding off the talkSPORT free agents' XI was Dusan Vlahovic, who is without a club just four years after joining Juventus for £66m.

Despite registering a solid 68 goals in 168 matches in Turin, the Serbi fell down the pecking order under several coaches and was not offered a new deal by Juve chiefs.

But Oladipo backed him to find his way back to the top, saying: “Dusan Vlahovic, by the way, 26-years-old, he'll get a club as well. Last seen at Juventus, he'll get a club.”

Stay up to date with all the latest rumours with the talkSPORT transfer blog

Sports.title: AC Milan release statement to deny false rumours that Franco Baresi has died
Sports.content:
AC Milan release statement to deny false rumours that Franco Baresi has died

AC Milan have moved quickly to deny completely false rumours that Franco Baresi has died.

Baresi established himself as one of the greatest defenders in football history during a glittering 20-year career with AC Milan and Italy.

3 Baresi was named AC Milan's 'Player of the Century' in 1999 Credit: Getty

The 66-year-old captained the Rossoneri for 15 seasons, winning three European Cups and six Serie A titles.

Such is Baresi's legendary status with Milan, his iconic No.6 shirt remains retired.

The legendary defender continues to operate within the club as an honorary vice-president, although he has experienced health problems in recent years.

Baresi underwent surgery in August 2025 to remove a pulmonary nodule and has since been undergoing immunotherapy treatment.

Milan were forced to address his health situation on Wednesday night as a death hoax spread on social media.

"AC Milan denies the false reports concerning Franco Baresi that have begun circulating in recent minutes," the official statement read.

"Franco is going through a difficult and delicate time, and the Club stands firmly alongside him and his family.

"We urge everyone to respect their privacy and refrain from spreading entirely unfounded information."

The greatest ever?

The late Argentina legend Diego Maradona, who played in Italy against Milan, once described Baresi as his greatest adversary, while multiple Italian legends such as Paolo Maldini have described him as their inspiration.

Nicknamed 'Piscinin', which translates to 'the little one', the former centre-back stood at 5ft 9ins, relying on skill and football IQ rather than strength.

3 Baresi led one of Italian football's greatest-ever teams to European glory three times Credit: Getty

Like Germany legend Franz Beckenbauer, Baresi helped to popularise the 'sweeper' role in a career which spanned across the 70s, 80s, and 90s.

Late Chelsea legend Ray Wilkins once said of Baresi: "Franco was the best player I have ever played with.

"The guy was world class to his core. He had everything – pace, two feet.

"And he was a leader of men."

Writing in the Guardian in 2009, Rio Ferdinand, then of Manchester United and England, wrote: "I've asked [Fabio Capello] about Baresi and he said he was one of the best players he's ever worked with.

"He played as a sweeper for Milan, coming out of nowhere to thwart any danger.

3 Baresi used his intelligence and reading of the game better than perhaps anyone in history Credit: Getty

"Baresi was a special footballer, someone who marshalled his whole back line, who was good on the ball, was comfortable, who led his defence... I'd love to be the player he was, bloody hell."

One club man

After making his senior debut in the 1977/78 season, Baresi was a league champion the following year at 18 years old, earning the club a tenth title.

Playing under Arrigo Sacchi and Capello, Milan were the dominant team of the late 1980s and much of the 1990s.

He later captained the club and went on to play 719 games before retiring in 1997, having only ever represented one club.

Sports.title: Paul Mullin signs for EFL club after Wrexham contract terminated this summer
Sports.content:
Paul Mullin has signed for Rotherham United after seeing his Wrexham deal terminated.

The striker became a cult hero for the Welsh club, helping them win promotion from the National League and League Two in back-to-back years.



2 Mullin's later years at Wrexham haven't been what he was hoping for Credit: Getty

He even found a role in Deadpool with Ryan Reynolds as 'Welshpool', and the striker gained a large number of fans.

However, his contract was mutually terminated in June, and the Championship side elected not to keep him around.

Still, his record for Wrexham was very good, scoring over 100 goals in just over 160 appearances.



And now he's back in League Two to try and help the Millers. Mullin has signed a two-year deal with south Yorkshire-based side.

Speaking to the club's website, he said: "It's been a long summer for me. Just, obviously, after the last couple of years, it was just about taking my time and making sure something was right for me, my family to the next part of the chapter of my career and Rotherham was an opportunity I couldn't pass up.



"I spoke to the manager beforehand, who obviously highlighted the plans he has for the club and that the people above him have for the club going forward, and although it hasn't been a great time the last couple of years, we've all seen what can happen at this place once it takes off and, hopefully, this year we can get back going that way."

Mullin on Wrexham

Mullin spent five years with Wrexham and became one of their most important players of recent times.



He still had one year left on his deal, but it was agreed by mutual consent to terminate it.

And it was an emotional goodbye for the striker, who said: "From the bottom of my heart, thank you very much to all the fans, near and far. What we create together is something I'll always be proud of.

"This club is special and has been to me and my family from the very start. I want nothing more than to see this club continue to progress - for all those people who came together to keep it alive and for Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac who are a special pair of people.

2 Mullin is a legend for Wrexham, and now he has the chance to carry on his career Credit: Getty



"This might be the end for me as a player, but there's not a chance it's the end of my love and affection for the club."

Manager Phil Parkinson also paid tribute, saying: "This settlement enables him to take his time and find the right club for him, going forward.

"It can't be underestimated the role Mulls (Mulliin) has played in the story of Wrexham Football Club over the last five years, with so many memorable goals and moments. He'll be a player always remembered and revered by our supporters."

Bagsman

Rotherham are hoping that Mullin's excellent League Two record can continue.



In 274 appearances in that division, he has 93 goals and 26 assists.

At the fourth tier of English football, he is a proven goalscorer.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand’s son, Tate, signs first pro deal with Premier League club
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand's son, Tate, has signed his first professional contract with Premier League side Brighton and Hove Albion.

It follows his oldest son, Lorenz, doing the exact same thing a year ago.



2 Two of Ferdinand's sons are now following in his footsteps Credit: Getty

Tate, who is 17 years old, is a centre-back, just like his dad.

His other son is a goalkeeper, so they'll likely be playing together at some point in the near future for one of Brighton's youth sides.

In a post on Instagram, Ferdinand revealed the news and just how proud he was.

He said: "Proud moment with the family, my boy @tateferdinand5 signed his first pro contract @officialbhafc.



"Keep up the hard work."

Tate became an official part of the Brighton Under-18s squad in 2024.

They are the only club that he has played for in his career so far, though, he is yet to appear for the club's Under-21s and make his Premier League 2 debut.

In the replies, loads of Manchester United legends and Ferdinand's former teammates sent their congratulations.



Edwin van der Saar said: "All the best, Tate."

Joleon Lescott, who was an England international with Ferdinand, said: "Sick."

Tate's career and play style

Unlike his older brother, Tate is very much in the mould of his dad. He is a centre-back and also wears the number five jersey.



Rio was a leader when he was at Manchester United, and Tate has been described as being the same.

But he was also excellent on the ball, and after a game late in October last year, people at the match believe he was just like his father.

However, his manager, Bjorn Hamberg believes the attention is water off a duck's back.

He said: “I am sure he doesn’t care about that (attention).

“Tate Ferdinand is Tate Ferdinand and he needs to be play his game and have his pathway and career.



2 Tate is following exactly in his father's footsteps Credit: Getty - Contributor

“For us as a team, for the under-18s as a captain, he is a big voice in our dressing room.

“He is obviously a leader in the back line and playing very well for the moment. I am really pleased for him as well.”

Brothers in arms

Tate and Lorenz are now both professionals with Brighton, and Rio will be hoping the future is very bright for both of them.



There are only two years separating the siblings as well, so it's possible we'll see double Ferdinand in the Brighton first team one day.

But as Rio said in his post, this is actually where the hard work starts.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford could make shock move to Premier League rival of Man United in £30m deal
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford could make shock move to Premier League rival of Man United in £30m deal

Marcus Rashford could join Tottenham this summer, despite continuing to be linked with north London rivals Arsenal.

The England forward has long been tipped for a move to the Gunners, although no attempt to sign him has been made this summer as his future remains in limbo.



6 Rashford is weighing up his future after featuring six times for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty

After spending last season on loan at Barcelona, Rashford saw his hopes of joining them permanently fall apart when England teammate Anthony Gordon completed a £70million move from Newcastle to the Camp Nou.

This means that, as things stand, the 28-year-old will report back to Manchester United for pre-season training in the coming days.

Rashford hasn't played for the Red Devils since the back end of 2024, spending time on loan at Aston Villa and then Barcelona.



However, United are still expected to try and offload the academy graduate before the end of the summer, with the club keen to get his wages of more than £325,000-a-week off the payroll.
