Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

And Rashford is also keen to leave Old Trafford, having fallen out with the club's hierarchy, as well as previous boss Ruben Amorim.



Rash decision

As speculation continues over Rashford's future, Arsenal have once again been linked with the winger, after long being touted to sign him in previous transfer windows.

The Gunners are keen to strengthen in the left-wing area following Leandro Trossard's departure, and were recently dealt a blow in their pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior, who is set for new contract talks with the Spanish giants.



And while Rashford is expected to be available for a cut-price £30million, talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent believes Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta could be put off signing him.

Crook said talkSPORT's Hawskbee and Jacobs show: “I'm just not sure Marcus Rashford is a Mikel Arteta-type player.

“If you look at what he's done, and why Arsenal have been so successful in his tenure, he weeded out the sort of problematic characters from the dressing room, so I'm not sure that he would necessarily welcome Marcus Rashford with open arms."

6 Arteta has made ruthless decisions on big-name players in his Arsenal tenure, including Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Mesut Ozil Credit: Getty



6 Rashford scored 14 goals and provided 14 assists for Barcelona last season, but the Spanish giants opted not to sign him permanently Credit: Getty

Gunner go across town?

Moving on to where Rashford could go instead of Arsenal, Crook then surprisingly pointed to bitter rivals Tottenham.

He insisted that head coach Roberto De Zerbi could be drawn to the prospect of turning the Englishman's career around, while Spurs haven't been afraid to splash the cash this summer.

After narrowly avoiding relegation last season, the north London outfit have spent heavily as they look to strengthen, spending £237m on new players which includes record signing Sandro Tonali.



On Rashford, Crook continued: “I think if he goes anywhere in London, I'm keeping an eye on Tottenham.

“I could see that deal happening. Roberto De Zerbi believing that he can get the best out of Marcus Rashford.”

Outlining the finances of a potential deal, Crook explained that while Rashford is set to be available for an appealing transfer fee, he admitted his wage demands could be a stumbling block.

6 Roberto De Zerbi has been ambitious with his player recruitment at Tottenham so far this summer Credit: AFP



Crook added: “When you say a cheap deal, I think probably an offer of £30million will be accepted by Manchester United, but you have to factor in he's on £325,000 a week at Old Trafford, and doesn't seem too willing to take a pay cut.”

'Every top-six team' would want Rashford

While Rashford's time as a United player looks to be up, talkSPORT's Rory Jennings believes he will still be holding out hope to be given a second chance by newly-appointed permanent boss Michael Carrick.

The local lad graduated from United‘s academy and has scored 138 goals in 426 games for the senior side – but has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024.

Rashford joined Aston Villa on loan in January 2025 after falling out of favour under ex-United head coach Ruben Amorim, and has previously drawn attention for off-the-field issues, including a controversial trip to a Belfast nightclub in January 2024.



Jennings told talkSPORT Drive: "Carrick's done an excellent job at that club.

"If he now looks at Marcus Rashford and thinks that there is a world where Rashford could come back into the fold, maybe get him playing again, maybe get the Stretford End singing his song again to the Stone Roses, that would be I think the dream for Rashford.

6 Rashford has spent almost 18 months away from Old Trafford across two loan spells Credit: Getty

"It feels optimistic but that's as good as it can get for Rashford now."



Jennings insisted that if it weren't for previous disciplinary issues, Rashford would be of interest to all top Premier League clubs.

He continued: "If you remove all of the baggage, all of the compensation. Just as a footballer, on form. I think he's excellent.

"I think he's an excellent footballer and if he didn't have the baggage and didn't have the wage expectation, I think basically every team in the top six… [would be interested].

"I think there is reputational damage, I think there is professionalism. I remember when he was meant to be playing for Manchester United, he missed training, he was in Belfast, he was boozing. I think there is reputational damage to Rashford."



He added: "There is also the financial demands of having Rashford in your camp. If we forget everything and we just talk about the footballer on his best day, I think every team in the top six would want him.

6 There is no question about Marcus Rashford's ability on his day Credit: Getty

"The reason they don't want him is the reputational damage and the wage demand."

Sports.title: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi teases 'bomba' signing in attack - and says club's summer business is nowhere near finished despite £237m spending spree!
Sports.content:
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi has teased a 'bomba' signing in attack, insisting the club's summer business is only '60 per cent' complete despite already breaking their transfer record twice in this window alone.

Spurs have spent £237million on signing Sandro Tonali (£100m), Mateus Fernandes (£85m) and Jan Paul van Hecke (£52m). They have also brought in Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League.

De Zerbi, who described himself as a 'shark' in the market, is now keen to add to his attack before the next season gets going. Daily Mail Sport understands the 'bomba' referenced by De Zerbi is not believed to refer to Savinho, the Manchester City winger who Spurs are also trying to bring in.

'The transfer market, it's not finished for sure, but we completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market,' De Zerbi said. 'Now we have another bomba.'

Asked whether it was close to completion, with De Zerbi having compiled his transfer targets during his negotiations with Spurs' bosses, he added: 'I hope, but it's not finished for sure.

'(We want) attackers, and then we find the position. I normally don't love working with plan A, plan B, plan C. It's plan A, then stop. Because the players are not the same. There are not two players the same.'

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi insists they are not done with transfers despite a big spend

Spurs are closing in on Manchester City winger Savinho as De Zerbi looks to bolster his attack

De Zerbi also revealed how Djed Spence, who enjoyed a breakout summer for England at the World Cup, has previously spoken to him about leaving Tottenham this summer. That goes along with others interested in exiting, including Cristian Romero, Guglielmo Vicario and Lucas Bergvall.

'At the beginning of my time, in April I had, I don't know, one million individual meetings, and they (Romero and Vicario) told me their idea,' De Zerbi explained.

'I said: "Yes, help me to stay up, and then I help you to leave. If you don't help me to stay up, you stay underwater with me." But Romero with me was unbelievable. Top.

'In his behaviour, his respect, he suffered when he did not play the last game. It is not true that he wanted to leave for Argentina to prepare their World Cup. It's not true. After the semi-final (of the World Cup) we text a message, but I never called him to convince him to stay. I respected what he told me. Like for Vicario. Like for every player.

'What I normally say to you is the same that I said before to the players. For example, Djed Spence, or Lucas Bergvall, both are sensitive topics for you, no? I repeat what I said to Djed, and to Lucas, 'I would like you to stay, not I want you to stay. I would like you stay if you want to stay. If you don't want to stay, if you want to leave, you have to leave.'

'If you want to leave, speak with Vinai (Venkatashem, chief executive) and Johan (Lange). Because I don't manage the price, the sale. I can speak with Vinai and Johan about the best strategy to do, but I don't decide £30m, £40m, that's not my position and I don't want to change my position. It's tough enough to be a coach and I want to stay as a coach.

'But I respected the players' ideas and opinions or projects. But if they stay, they have to stay following my rules, decisions on the pitch.'

Sports.title: Eddie Howe to LEAVE role as Newcastle boss in bombshell news as turbulent summer at St James' Park continues
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe to LEAVE role as Newcastle boss in bombshell news as turbulent summer at St James' Park continues

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Eddie Howe is set to leave Newcastle United with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport understands the head coach has been contemplating his future and has come to an agreement with the club to end his four-and-a-half-year tenure.

Howe took time at the end of last season to consider the best way forward for him and the club, but decided to carry on.

However, the 48-year-old has now informed the hierarchy of his belief that the time is right to part ways. There has been no falling out and the agreement has been reached amicably.

Newcastle are in talks with candidates to replace Howe, including Matthias Jaissle of Al Ahli. The German, 38, was previously in charge of Red Bull Salzburg between 2021 and 2023 and has since managed in Saudi Arabia, where he won the Asian Champions League in 2025 and 2026. Sources say no deal has yet been agreed with Jaissle.

Eddie Howe is set to leave his role as Newcastle United manager in bombshell news

Howe led Newcastle to their first major trophy in 70 years in 2025 and also took them to the Champions League on two occasions

But news of Howe’s departure has rocked Tyneside, even though it has not come as a surprise on the back of a turbulent 12 months.

After losing star striker Alexander Isak last summer, England winger Anthony Gordon and Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali have been sold this summer. Captain Bruno Guimaraes also wants to join Arsenal and, should the Premier League champions present an acceptable offer, the expectation is the Brazilian will go.

Newcastle have bought four players this window but all are aged 20 and under. They have opened pre-season with a draw against non-League Gateshead and a 4-1 defeat by Championship side Bristol City on Wednesday night.

Howe said after that match that the focus was the opening game of the season against Liverpool, but the wheels were already in motion for his departure. A club statement will follow confirming the end of his hugely successful period at St James’ Park.

The former Bournemouth boss arrived in November, 2021 with the team 19th in the Premier League on the back of the Saudi-led takeover the previous month.

After leading them to survival, Newcastle qualified for the Champions League the following season and were beaten in the final of the Carabao Cup.

His exit continues a turbulent summer at Newcastle after the exits of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali

Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle is an early contender to replace Howe at St James' Park

In 2025, Howe became the first manager in 70 years to win a domestic trophy for the Magpies when they beat Liverpool in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. They also qualified for the Champions League for a second time.

However, last season was a struggle and, despite making the last 16 of the Champions League and the semi-final of the Carabao Cup, a 12th-placed finish was reflective of the drop-off in performance.

Howe met with the club’s owners during a summit at Matfen Hall in April and the intention was to carry on into this season. But after careful thought in recent weeks, he will now take a break from football.

Sports.title: Club at centre of 'Clicky Ponting' scandal break their silence on cheating storm: Saltburn CC confirm player who tricked umpires has been BANNED after he was 'knocked sideways' by outrage
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A cricketer who has become known as 'Clicky Ponting' for his role in a cheating scandal has been banned by his club – who have finally broken their silence.

Saltburn cricketer Brian Devine is accused of clicking his fingers to imitate the sound of the ball hitting the bat, to fool the umpire into thinking the batter is out.

The amateur cricket scandal has caused convulsions around the cricketing world.

Now, more than 24 hours after clips of Devine went viral, Saltburn have confirmed that the player has been banned from the club.

'This statement is issued in response to the widely publicised complaint made against a Saltburn Cricket Club member and, as a consequence, against the Club more generally,' the statement, shared on social media, began.

'We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric Club, we are fully cooperating with the NYSD League's investigation.

Brian Devine has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his cricket fielding actions

Saltburn Cricket Club have broken their silence on the ordeal, revealing the player has been banned pending an investigation

'We believe that the Club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the Club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation. Initial discussions have already taken place between Club officials and the league.

'This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club entirely run by volunteers.

'We will be making no further comment at this time.'

Devine is accused of clicking his fingers while fielding for the club to make it sound as though the ball had hit the bat when it had in fact not.

If the ball hits the bat and is then caught, it means a batter is out.

The minor league cricketer at the centre of the scandal is 'completely bewildered' to find himself engulfed by a global furore.

Friends say Devine's 'head is all over the place' after the accusation that he clicked his fingers to imitate the sound of the ball hitting the bat.

A friend of Devine's said he was not expected to play and would 'lie low' while the cheating row continues.

Amateur cricket player Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Other incidences have been found of Devine clicking his finger in previous matches for wickets

The friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first that he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible for him.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world, in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction all over the world to all this has knocked him sideways.'

Mr Devine, 38, a father who lives with his partner in Guisborough, North Yorkshire, has continued to decline to comment. His mobile phone number was also removed from the company website at the auction mart in Northallerton where he works.

At Saltburn Cricket Club's clubhouse, prior to their statement, journalists were angrily told to leave by a club official, who said: 'We're sick of this now, you have no right to come here.'

A Durham-based amateur cricketer named Ben Mummery, who had been tipped off about the series of events, posted footage to X, where he dubbed it 'about the worst case of cheating I have ever seen in cricket'.

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

That clip had soon clocked up millions of views.

Viewers then began to trawl the archives for other similar incidents. They promptly turned up dozens, suggesting that Saltburn had been employing the cynical scam for more than a season.

In almost every one of the clips that have emerged, Devine can be seen standing at first slip, clicking his fingers as the ball whistles past.

One particularly damning video was posted by Rory Cotterill, the captain of Middlesbrough CC's second XI. He said there had been two more incidents like it in a single game they played on Saturday, June 27, which Saltburn won by 29 runs, 'leading to a 15 and 16-year-old being cheated out of an innings'. He added: 'I was at the non-striker's end at the time, unknowingly watching them cheat in real time.'

Other cricket fans to weigh in included Piers Morgan, who dubbed the club's behaviour 'outrageous cheating' and a 'shameful scam'. Several posters dubbed Devine 'Clicky Ponting' – a play on the name of former Australian captain Ricky Ponting – on social media.

Georgina Vaughan, the mother of Devine's partner Clare, said the family had been shocked by the scale of the cheating row.

She said: 'It was only a little village cricket match and now it's become this thing that's all over the news and social media.

'It has got totally out of hand and there is nothing that any of us want to say.'

Asked whether Devine was a man of integrity, she replied: 'He certainly is.'

A statement from the North Yorkshire and South Durham League read: 'The League has received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday 25th July 2026. A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete, no further comment will be made.'

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha steps up amid Bradley Barcola speculation, the classy 18-year-old at the back and the star of the show shines again: Liverpool 1-0 Wrexham
Sports.content:
The Andoni Iraola era continued to gather pace in New York as Liverpool beat Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s second-half goal.

At the iconic home of the New York Yankees baseball team, Ngumoha cut in from the right wing – pretty much second base on this slapdash, bumpy football pitch – and scored via a deflection.

It is Liverpool’s second win of this pre-season tour of the United States having beaten Sunderland in Nashville last week and they now fly back to their training base in Chicago to take on Leeds on Sunday.

Like in the first friendly, there were plenty of minutes for youngsters given the long list of absentees from Iraola’s first fortnight.

Florian Wirtz, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexander Isak remained at base in Chicago while Federico Chiesa was ruled out through illness, according to boss Iraola.

Daily Mail Sport's Reds expert LEWIS STEELE was in situ in The Bronx to bring you the top talking points from leg two of Liverpool’s tour.

Liverpool narrowly beat Wrexham 1-0 in a pre-season friendly at Yankee Stadium in New York

It means that Andoni Iraola has now won his first two games in charge of the Reds

Rio’s right in the thick of it

Liverpool are stepping up their pursuit of Bradley Barcola and hope to strike an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over the £145million-rated winger.

When Sky Sports posted on X asking readers whether it would be a good signing, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher replied: ‘No he plays on the opposite flank!

‘LFC currently have three players who could play from the left in Rio (Ngumoha), (Cody) Gakpo and (Florian) Wirtz and no one who plays from the right.’

It is a salient point – their attack is and will be more lopsided if and when Barcola arrives. Victor Munoz, the early-summer signing from Osasuna, also prefers playing on the left though is said to be more versatile.

Ngumoha, therefore, was trialled on the right wing here in New York.

Was it a perfect performance? No, he was quiet at times – just as he was in Nashville on the left, by the way – but it was Ngumoha who stepped up with the decisive moment to open the scoring in the 75th minute.

It was a slightly lucky finish given the significant deflection off the Wrexham defender but it counts the same and probably a product of players backing off him to his frightening speed and trickery.

Anyone for Barcola and Ngumoha on either side of Isak on the opening day?

Rio Ngumoha scored the only goal of the game and showed why he can be an asset on the right wing

Can Nyoni save Reds millions on midfield upgrade?

There are plenty of calls from the fanbase for Liverpool to sign a new midfielder but Trey Nyoni might be the answer they are all craving.

Nyoni, 19, signed from Leicester in 2023 and has made 20 appearances for the first team, largely off the substitutes bench in the cups.

He played 21 minutes in the Premier League last term but given Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch both saw their form dip, the teenager could probably feel aggrieved that he did not get on the pitch more.

Nyoni can play as a No6, as he did here, or further forward and has even played at centre-half and in the front three over his career. Mr Versatile.

But the deep-lying position is where he truly thrives. Having watched him extensively for the youth teams, Nyoni is best when showing for the ball and making the game tick, dictating possession with a simple pass-and-move, Spanish-like style.

Could this be his year? If so, it could save the Reds millions.

Shame about Ndukwe

Ifeanyi Ndukwe has looked a classy defender in his two pre-season appearances – but do not get excited just yet.

The 18-year-old, who signed from Austria Wien this summer, cannot play for Liverpool this season as he does not yet have the required points total to obtain a work visa. That’s Brexit for you, folks.

There will be a long list of clubs queuing up to take him on loan, then, given his calm performances against Wrexham and Sunderland in pre-season. He is composed in possession and sniffs out danger defensively.

Dominik Szoboszlai was head and shoulders above the rest at the Yankee Stadium

Noting Liverpool’s defensive crisis – Joe Gomez, Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are unfit, while Virgil van Dijk is now 35 and not on this tour – Ndukwe could have got some minutes this year so it is a crying shame that red tape will prevent that.

Alongside him, Luke Chambers looked equally as assured. Now 22, Chambers has had loans at Kilmarnock, Wigan and Charlton but is a classy footballer whose journey has been halted somewhat by injuries.

Chambers can play at left back and left centre-back so could be a handy squad player to keep around.

Szoboszlai Hungary for more as Elliott steps up

Dominik Szoboszlai was head and shoulders above the rest at the Yankee Stadium – fitter, stronger, faster. Wrexham could not get near him.

The Hungary captain was also wearing the armband for Liverpool with Virgil van Dijk absent from this pre-season tour.

Szoboszlai, who signed a new long-term contract earlier this month, has eyes on taking on the captaincy long-term and might get the nod for vice-captain this season, with Alisson also in the running for said vacancy after Andy Robertson’s departure.

Whether or not he takes on that mantle, it is clear he is growing as a leader on and off the pitch. Time and again here, the midfielder stormed through the Wrexham midfield like a hot knife through butter.

Harvey Elliott also dazzled and should have had an early assist, though young Joshua Abe fluffed his lines after a clever run off the ball. Elliott could have had a goal for himself later on but was denied by former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward.

Sports.title: Is Gianni Infantino 'untouchable', how could the FIFA president be stopped and who could replace him? All the big questions answered amid fury over plans to sell stakes in the World Cup
Sports.content:
Is Gianni Infantino 'untouchable', how could the FIFA president be stopped and who could replace him? All the big questions answered amid fury over plans to sell stakes in the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA have set the wheels in motion on a radical plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

In proposals exposed on Tuesday, it emerged that FIFA want to set up a subsidiary to control the operational delivery of tournaments and their commercial interests – such as ticketing and TV rights.

FIFA hopes to raise over £3billion from investors for the project, with investment bank J.P. Morgan advising world football’s governing body.

American venture capitalist firm Thrive, of which Joshua Kushner – brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – is CEO, are expected to lead the proposed investor group.

Despite FIFA maintaining that outside investors will not play any operational role, there are grave concerns that investor interest will increase the frequency of tournaments – such as the Club World Cup and World Cup – to help maximise the return on investment.

Football associations are being incentivised to support the proposition with the promise of £15million in additional revenue.

Daily Mail Sport digests the biggest danger to football since the European Super League.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has set the wheels in motion over a racial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors in a highly controversial move

Why is Gianni Infantino untouchable?

It’s simple: he’s the money man. FIFA’s voting system of one association, one vote means that each national association – regardless of size or standing in the game – gets one vote on FIFA policy and presidency.

Therefore, the English FA has the same influence as Botswana's FA, despite the African nation having never qualified for a World Cup.

It allows Infantino to lobby and curry favour with smaller nations by promising increased funding and expanded tournaments. His masterplan is to increase the 2030 World Cup to 64 teams, meaning 30 per cent of FIFA nations would be present at the tournament.

More teams, more matches, more revenue. That promise is too transformational for smaller nations to turn down. The FA, whose turnover is over half a billion per year, can perhaps afford to take the moral high ground.

Infantino has tactically created a block vote of those who need the money – particularly nations from the African federation – to support and protect his presidency, giving him a free pass.

Then there are the likes of San Marino and Curacao, where an extra £15m in revenue – generated by these new plans – offers unprecedented funding for football projects.

At this summer’s expanded World Cup, Curacao earned £7.5m while Cape Verde banked £9m – it's plain to see the appeal of a lucrative 64-team tournament to minor nations.

Earlier this year, the South American, African and Asian confederations said they would back Infantino for another four years as FIFA president. Those three associations represent 111 countries, with Infantino needing the support of 106 to win another term. Unless they withdraw their support, he has already won.

UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Conmebol have all voiced organisational concerns about the project and the lack of consultation. But it is down to each nation to set their respective stance.

Infantino is backed by a large number of smaller nations who benefit from FIFA's funding

Curacao were among those to benefit from Infantino's expansion of the World Cup to 48 teams

How can Infantino be stopped?

UEFA are set for crisis talks on Thursday as they attempt to get all 55 UEFA nations pulling in the same direction. However, that effort has already hit a roadblock, with the president of the Czech FA, David Trunda, backing Infantino’s plans.

Even if the talks build consensus, UEFA would still be 51 associations short of blocking Infantino’s plan – and that is assuming all UEFA nations agree to vote it down, which already looks unlikely.

Concacaf and the AFC have already voiced their concerns, but their member nations are much more susceptible to accepting FIFA’s cash incentives.

There is another way, though. UEFA could pressure FIFA by threatening to withdraw from the next World Cup, but that would require unprecedented collaboration. Even then, it could be seen as an empty threat with the next tournament four years away – although it could still scupper the upcoming broadcast tender process.

However, the Women’s World Cup is just around the corner, and any threat to derail it would have to be taken more seriously. That will surely be on Thursday's agenda.

But those decisions are down to each nation – UEFA can only act as a broker, facilitating talks in the hope of mobilising associations behind the same course of action.

Take Spain, for example. They will be determined to defend their crown as women’s world champions, so it will be difficult for UEFA to persuade them to pressure FIFA by threatening to withdraw.

The dissent is encouraging, but stopping Infantino presents an almighty challenge.

Next year's Women's World Cup would be the next realistic event if nations were to threaten a boycott

What is the relationship between FIFA and UEFA like?

UEFA's two damning statements aimed at Infantino are the latest flashpoint in an increasingly turbulent relationship between European football's governing body and FIFA. Reflecting on the plans, UEFA said FIFA have ‘crossed a line’ – it is the second time they have aimed that phrase at FIFA this summer.

Tensions between UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and Infantino have been public since FIFA unveiled plans to expand the Club World Cup, stretching an already congested calendar and threatening the commercial dominance of the Champions League.

FIFA's biggest revenue driver is the men's World Cup, held every four years, with the latest edition generating £11.2bn, while UEFA benefits from both the European Championship and the Champions League.

Over a four-year cycle, the Champions League generates more revenue than the World Cup – bringing in around £3.7bn annually.

That disparity has long frustrated Infantino, and the launch of the 32-team Club World Cup represented FIFA's attempt to establish a lucrative club competition under their own control.

FIFA is now considering a further expansion to 48 teams from 2029, heightening UEFA’s concerns that an enlarged Club World Cup could dilute the value of European club football.

Relations deteriorated further at FIFA's annual Congress in May 2025 when Infantino arrived more than two hours late after accompanying US President Donald Trump on a diplomatic tour of the Middle East. During a break, Ceferin led a walkout before UEFA accused the FIFA president of putting "private political interests" ahead of football's governance. He boycotted the following year.

Tensions between UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and Infantino have been played out in public, with Europe's governing body this week claiming the plans have 'crossed the line'

Infantino's close relationship with US president Donald Trump has also let to friction with UEFA

That was not his last no-show either. Ceferin failed to show up for Spain’s World Cup final win over Argentina earlier this month – disillusioned with the FIFA president and his antics during the tournament.

Infantino took a call from President Trump, where he pleaded with him to investigate Folarin Balogun’s red card and subsequent one-game ban. FIFA’s one-man disciplinary council then suspended the ban for a year as a workaround for the absence of a mechanism to overturn a red card at the World Cup, an unprecedented step.

They have also indirectly criticised FIFA by awarding the Super Cup final to the Somalian referee who was due to officiate at the World Cup before his visa was revoked and announcing low ticket prices for Euro 2028 while FIFA were facing criticism for extortionate ticket prices.

Who could rival Infantino for FIFA leadership?

Despite Infantino’s position as FIFA president seeming entrenched right now, there remain eight months until the next elections – so there is still time for a challenge to be mounted.

However, the deadline for candidates to formally present their nominations with the support of at least five national federations is November 18.

In the previous election in 2023, Infantino ran unchallenged. That is unlikely to be the case in 2027 with the growing opposition – but candidates may be fighting a losing battle with 111 nations already backing Infantino.

PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi – who is the chairman of Bein Media and Qatari Sports Investments – is the most logical option to stand in opposition. He has backing from several European nations and is respected across the game.

PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi – who is the chairman of Bein Media and Qatari Sports Investments – is the most logical option to stand in opposition to Infantino as FIFA president

Al-Khelaifi is admired for his communication and his deep understanding of football governance. He is currently chair of the European Football Clubs group – the body which represents over 800 European clubs – which criticised FIFA’s investment plans.

The Qatari is a member of UEFA’s executive committee, making him the first Asian to hold a UEFA position, which could help him to win support from two continents.

It has also been reported that Dariusz Mioduski, the Polish owner and president of Legia Warsaw, may be a potential rival to Infantino. Victor Montagliani, the president of Concacaf and vice-president of FIFA, has not ruled out a future run for the presidency – although he is expected to seek re-election with Concacaf next year.

Meanwhile, president of the German Football Association Bernd Neuendorf declined to endorse Infantino’s re-nomination, while La Liga chair Javier Tebas has called for Infantino to step down.

Sports.title: Stephen Fleming in line to become England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum sacking - as New Zealander is chosen by ECB to lead post-Bazball project
Sports.content:
Stephen Fleming in line to become England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum sacking - as New Zealander is chosen by ECB to lead post-Bazball project

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England are closing in on Stephen Fleming as their new Test coach following the axing of his fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum.

Fleming, 53, is viewed as one of cricket’s great strategists, having played 111 Tests for his country, becoming their most successful captain with 28 wins.

Since quitting international cricket in 2008, he has enjoyed a successful coaching career, predominantly with Chennai Super Kings, claiming five Indian Premier League titles before quitting days after McCullum was removed from his position.

Defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge in what was Ben Stokes’ final international appearance meant England had not won a series for more than 12 months, forcing a re-think within an ECB hierarchy that resisted change following the deflating 4-1 Ashes defeat last winter.

The ECB declined to comment when contacted on Wednesday, but Daily Mail Sport understands he edged out Englishmen Richard Dawson and Jonathan Trott in the selection process.

One of Fleming’s first tasks will be to determine who succeeds Stokes as England captain.

New Zealander Stephen Fleming is in line to become the new England Men's Test head coach

Fleming has worked as a coach since 2009, but his only roles have come in franchise cricket, including 14 years over two spells at Chennai Super Kings

England are still looking for a new captain after Ben Stokes' retirement earlier this summer

Joe Root stepped in when Stokes was suspended for The Oval Test last month and was being lined up to work alongside McCullum until the end of next year’s Ashes.

That particular succession plan was put into place in order not to over-burden Root’s fellow Yorkshireman Harry Brook.

However, Brook revealed it would be a ‘privilege’ to lead England in all three formats, having made a success of turning around results in his 15-month captaincy of the limited-overs teams.

Appointing Brook, who at 27 is Root’s junior by eight years, now would maintain some continuity as England return to split coaching roles and avoid another captaincy switch within the next 18 months.

Fleming indicated his interest in the post immediately after mutually severing ties with the CSK organisation a fortnight ago. The franchise said it was ‘bringing to a close one of the most successful and enduring partnerships in IPL history.’

Adding: ‘The decision was reached with respect and gratitude, following a series of open and honest discussions between Fleming and the Super Kings management.’

Fleming also ended ties with Super Kings' other franchises - Joburg Super Kings in the SA20 and Texas Super Kings in the United States - where he was head coach.

His appointment would reunite him in a working capacity with McCullum, who viewed his fellow Kiwi as a mentor during their playing days.

It would also take the numbers of New Zealanders across England’s coaching set-up to four: Jeetan Patel and Tim Southee are currently spin and fast bowling coaches respectively.

Some will feel that a lack of homegrown presence is a concern, particularly after managing director Rob Key turned to Australian Marcus North as national selector.

Indeed, only two Englishmen featured on a nine-strong list of potential candidates. Not all received calls, however, suggesting that Fleming became their preferred choice after Andy Flower, the original No 1 target, turned down the chance to interview.

Fleming is well known to the English game, however, having captained Nottinghamshire to the County Championship title and also represented Yorkshire.

As a coach, he also took Southern Brave to the knockout stages of the 2023 and 2024 editions of the Hundred.

Sports.title: Idi Amin's grandson accuses boxing officials of bias after being disqualified for headbutting English opponent at Commonwealth Games: 'It's bulls***!'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Idi Amin’s grandson accused officials of conspiring against him after he was disqualified for headbutting England’s Damar Thomas.

Ugandan super heavyweight Aziz Abdul is a descendant of the country’s brutal despot who murdered hundreds of thousands during his regime.

Before he became president in 1971, Amin was also an accomplished boxer.

He is alleged to have fathered 50 children and Abdul, 25, who goes by the nickname Ringo, claimed he was on a mission to be crowned ‘the new King of Scotland’ before his fight was terminated by judges in the third round.

The Last King of Scotland is a 2006 historical drama that depicts the Amin dictatorship through the perspective of Nicholas Garrigan, a fictional Scottish doctor.

‘All I can say about this is the referee’s decision is not right and I am not happy,’ said Abdul. ‘This n***** next time, I will get him. Anytime in the future. Two years, five years, 10 years. I will show him that Aziz Ringo is a real warrior.

Idi Amin’s grandson Aziz Abdul (left) accused officials of racism after he was disqualified for headbutting England’s Damar Thomas (right) in their Commonwealth Games bout

‘When you watch the previous fights of England, their boxers create a lot of fouls and they play a lot of bull****. They cannot judge them wrong. I took a light punch and they counted. I landed a heavy punch on him and they deduct my points and warn me.

'Of course it’s unfair. I’m a black African, I know. It’s God’s plan. I don’t know why the officials are scared about this fight. Why can’t they let this fight continue.’

Abdul claimed the officials wanted to see a British representative in the final.

‘How can I headbutt someone?’ he said. ‘I would not headbutt someone. He is the real person they wanted to win. He was the winner before. I knew if I could not get a knockout then I would not win the fight because he’s at home. It’s an away match for me here. All I say is it’s God’s plan and I wish him good luck for his next fight.’

Sports.title: UEFA accuse FIFA president of BRIBING nations to back Gianni Infantino's plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - as they step up criticism of controversial proposal
Sports.content:
UEFA have seemingly accused FIFA of bribing associations as they continue to scold Gianni Infantino's plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - criticising FIFA’s self-interest as they pressure associations with a £30million incentive.

FIFA wrote to national associations on Wednesday morning to explain their leaked plans, detailing that a £30m funding package will become available to associations should they sign off on the World Cup private investment plan.

In a letter to the associations, Infantino says associations must decide on the proposal - which would see private investors procure a £3bn interest in the World Cup - by September 19 and explains the financial benefits of approving the project.

In response to the letter, UEFA said: 'Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan.

'But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.'

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport that UEFA have scheduled crisis talks with all 55 member nations on Thursday as they rally the troops against FIFA.

Tensions have long been growing between FIFA President Gianni Infantino and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, who boycotted the World Cup final

FIFA hope to set up a company responsible for the commercial activity and 'operational delivery of FIFA tournaments', called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

FIFA hope to raise more than £3bn for the venture from a diversified, global investor group which is thought to include sovereign wealth funds.

There are major concerns over what the proposals could mean for the game, including whether FIFA could increase the frequency of tournaments to create more opportunities for financial backers to see a return on their investment.

The European Leagues Association, of which the Premier League is a founding member, said: 'The World Cup should not be for sale. It is not the FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal.'

Philippe Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation, called it a 'worrying project that raises many questions'. He added: 'This is worrying because there are no details, yet it touches on one of football’s fundamental assets, the World Cup, which is the world’s greatest sporting event.'

The Confederation of African Football offered a more conciliatory tone, saying in a statement: 'CAF is committed to continue consulting and working together with its Member Associations, FIFA, other Football Confederations and stakeholders in support of increasing financial and other resources for the development and growth of football in Africa and worldwide.'

Infantino and FIFA conducted their own in-house 'interview' on Wednesday without taking any questions from the media.

Sports.title: 'Marcus Rashford should be embarrassed – how can his Man Utd team-mates trust him'
Sports.content:
'Marcus Rashford should be embarrassed – how can his Man Utd team-mates trust him'

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has been told "he should be embarrassed" as transfer talk continues to whirl following his return from a successful loan spell at Barcelona

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has been told he "should be embarrassed" at the manner of his Barcelona exit after returning to Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Marcus Rashford has been told he "should be embarrassed" returning to Manchester United this summer. The England forward has reunited with Michael Carrick's squad following his successful spell on loan at Barcelona last season.

‌



Rashford, 28, looked all but guaranteed to join Barca on permanent terms once his temporary spell in Catalonia concluded. However, Los Cules opted to not trigger his £26million clause and signed England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle instead.

‌



Paul Parker, who won two Premier League titles at Old Trafford, has said Rashford is now on "absolutely his last chance" as he potentially looks set to stay at United this season. However, the retired full-back said Rashford must show humility and "prove a point" as he aims to win over fans (and possibly some team-mates).

‌



Parker told PariuriX: "The biggest thing is, how can he ever be trusted by his teammates again? He wasn't doing his job properly but everyone allowed him to do it [and] now they have figured him out.

"Back in my time you would have been grabbed by one of the senior players and they would do something to you which you wouldn't find very funny.

‌

"He has been given this small chance to come back again and honestly he has only been given this chance because of the fact that Barcelona didn't want him. They decided to spend more money on Anthony Gordon, which Rashford should be feeling embarrassed about. The moment they spent that much money on Gordon, he should be embarrassed."

Gordon's £69.3m move to Barcelona took many by surprise, especially given previous reports suggesting Barca's lack of available finances was a major factor in why they didn't sign Rashford. Not to mention the fact Hansi Flick's side could have had Rashford for nearly a third of that amount.

Alternative transfers are still being explored for Rashford, whose last appearance for United was way back in December 2024. Roma are reportedly interested in the player, while Tottenham have also been linked with his signature.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford finds himself in a difficult position after returning from his loan at Barcelona (Image: Josep LAGO / AFP via Getty Images)

However, the forward's wages are likely to present a significant hurdle for just about any team likely to make a move. Rashford is the highest earner at Old Trafford on wages of £325,000 a week.

"If he is serious about wanting to prove himself again, it will be a serious challenge for him," added Parker. "Because the fans won't accept him just after one game or one goal, he needs to work hard consistently.

‌



"How does he conduct himself when he is sitting at the bench watching the matches? How is he conducting himself in the training and socially? That is one of the big issues and a big reason that he is where he is.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s dream final month of transfer window as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez moves sealed
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s dream final month of transfer window as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez moves sealed

Mikel Arteta and Arsenal must secure several world class signings ahead of the new season

View 4 Images Arsenal must sign Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Getty )

Speaking in the wake of Arsenal's agonising Champions League final penalty shootout defeat to PSG in May, Gunners manager Mikel Arteta made no attempt to hide what he expects from the club in the transfer market.

‌



"If you want to reach another level, we're going to have to show that ambition because we are more than capable of doing it, but it demands to be very, very ambitious, very fast and very smart," Arteta said.

‌



So far, however, the Premier League champions have not lived up to those words. With sporting director Andrea Berta at the helm of transfer business, their cautious start to the window has already come at a cost, with Jeremy Monga and Morgan Rogers both moving to rival Premier League clubs in a somewhat damning turn of events.

‌



To put it into context, the Gunners completed six signings during July alone last summer — yet only two new arrivals have been announced so far this time around. The quality of those deals has not been hugely impressive, either.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius Jr has already promised to join club as Arsenal handed transfer timeline READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Piero Hincapie's loan was made permanent, Illan Meslier arrived on a free transfer as a third-choice goalkeeper option, and Greek winger Christos Tzolis — largely unproven at this level — was signed from Club Brugge for £34m.

‌



That said, Berta and Arteta are understood to be pushing hard behind the scenes on a number of fronts, and there are signs that progress is being made. Now, Mirror Football takes a look at the deals Arsenal need to get over the line before the window closes to put themselves in the best possible position to challenge for honours this season.

£80m Bruno Guimaraes deal

Arsenal have, understandably, shown reluctance to splash the same extravagant sums that rivals Tottenham spent on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes on a central midfielder this summer. They are currently engaged in third-party negotiations with Newcastle over a deal for their primary summer target Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been informed they must produce a transfer fee in the region of £80m for the Magpies captain, or the deal will collapse. Despite reports suggesting the Gunners had submitted a £70m bid, there have been no direct club-to-club negotiations between the two sides as it stands.

‌



Intermediaries - namely super agent Kia Joorabchian - have reportedly been heavily involved in the potential deal. The two clubs are yet to reach an agreement over the 28-year-old, however.

£80m in today's market for a Premier League-proven talent of Guimaraes' quality is far from an outrageous figure. Arsenal should pay whatever is necessary, and swiftly, to reinforce their midfield before the campaign kicks off, particularly given Declan Rice's recent injury concerns.

Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez

View 4 Images Julian Alvarez is Mikel Arteta's dream signing (Image: Getty)

‌



There are very few players in today's market who truly fire the imagination of fans. Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Junior are among those rare footballers who seem to carry a certain world-class aura in the modern game.

Atletico Madrid's Alvarez has been a long-standing target for Arsenal, with Arteta widely understood to be an admirer. The Argentine's preference is plainly to join Barcelona this summer, yet Atletico's firm stance against allowing him to move to a La Liga rival hands the Gunners a genuine opportunity to land his signature.

The striker represents a clear step up from both Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres, with the latter potentially featuring in a player-plus-£51.7million package to secure Alvarez, given Atletico's reported interest in the Swede. The crucial question, therefore, is whether Alvarez would rather remain in Madrid or make a return to England.

‌



Arteta and Berta must pull out all the stops to persuade him to choose Arsenal, as he would undoubtedly represent a transformative acquisition. Much the same applies to Vinicius, whose ongoing contract uncertainty at Real Madrid has fuelled reports of a potential Arsenal approach.

football.london reports that senior figures at the Emirates Stadium are prepared to bring the Brazilian to N5, despite the enormous expense involved. However, no formal discussions have yet taken place between Arsenal and Los Blancos.

Consequently, no transfer fee has been put forward regarding Vinicius, whose deal runs out next summer, although reports emerging from Spain indicate that Madrid have slapped a £137m valuation on the Brazilian.

‌



For Arsenal, Alvarez and Vinicius represent two world-class talents capable of striking fear into any defence in Europe. The financial challenge of securing both players is considerable.

However, should they succeed, the two deals would transform Arsenal's standing on the global stage, firmly establishing them amongst the true elite.

View 4 Images Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius Jr is ambitious but not impossible (Image: Getty Images Europe)

‌



£26m defender signed

The Gunners are heading into the new season fully aware that they are lacking in defensive cover. Several key components of their backline, including Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White have demonstrated a susceptibility to injury, which proved problematic last season.

Exacerbating the situation is news that William Saliba could reportedly be sidelined for as long as five months with a back injury. Therefore, a right-sided defensive addition is vital.

Ezri Konsa has been identified as a potential target, though the Gunners are reluctant to match Aston Villa's current asking price, understood to be around £60m. Should Villa refuse to lower their demands, long-term target Ivan Fresneda of Sporting CP is the ideal signing.

‌



Fresneda, 21, is a talented prospect understood to be obtainable for around £26m. Such a modest fee would enable Arsenal to preserve resources and focus their spending further forward. The Spaniard would slot in at right-back, allowing Timber, White and Cristhian Mosquera to fill Saliba's role until the Frenchman's return.

That would bring Arsenal's combined expenditure on Alvarez, Vinicius, Guimaraes and Fresneda to roughly £295m – while providing the squad with the sufficient quality to progress further this campaign.

Player departures sanctioned

View 4 Images Fabio Vieira is no longer needed at Arsenal (Image: Getty )

‌



Arsenal need to shake off the perception that they are a poor selling club. Neither Berta nor predecessor Edu Gaspar have managed to get rid of the deadwood at London Colney, let alone secure impressive fees for departing players.

That has to change, starting with Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus, Reiss Nelson and Christian Norgaard being sold. None of these four are expected to feature prominently next season and sanctioning their departures will help alleviate the wage bill, even if minimal funds can be recovered through transfer fees.

Meslier's arrival also suggests Tommy Setford, aged 20, could be loaned out to further his development. Given the congested midfield, Ethan Nwaneri would likewise benefit from consistent game time on loan, with the caveat that his destination club provides a settled environment - unlike the disastrous Marseille loan stint he suffered last season.

Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola negotiations opened as target hands in transfer request

Liverpool's push to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola has moved up a gear after reports the Reds are entering discussions with the French giants to reach an agreement

View 2 Images Liverpool have reportedly opened talks with Paris Saint-Germain over a move for Bradley Barcola (Image: Dan Mullan - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola could be closing in on a transfer signing that has the potential to transform Liverpool's summer window. The Reds' major priority remains a replacement for Mohamed Salah and Bradley Barcola has taken huge steps towards landing that role.

‌



Liverpool already secured the £60million signature of Jeremy Jacquet before Victor Munoz's surprise acquisition. However, Barcola could become Iraola's first superstar capture in a deal that has the potential to set a new British transfer record.

‌



He's not the only forward signing being tipped for a move to Anfield as major developments unfold elsewhere. Mirror Football has all that and more as we break down the latest Liverpool transfer headlines.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool open Barcola talks

Sky Sports News has reported Liverpool could be on track to land their dream Salah replacement after opening talks to sign Bradley Barcola. The player has reportedly verbally agreed to the move, with PSG the only party left that needs convincing.

Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made READ MORE :

That won't be an insignificant hurdle to climb, however, with Les Parisiens reportedly demanding £145million for their man. To put that figure into context, it would easily eclipse the British transfer record £125m Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak last summer.

‌



Barcola, 23, has entered the final two years of his contract at the Parc des Princes. He's also reported to have turned down the offer of fresh talks over an extension, further evidence the winger is open to joining the Reds this summer.

Iraola has received further encouragement following reports in France that Barcola turned down Chelsea earlier this summer. Given his club have managed to advance in negotiations, it suggests a move to Anfield holds special significance to the forward.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed as Michael Carrick set to axe four players
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed as Michael Carrick set to axe four players

Michael Carrick's first full Premier League season in charge of Manchester United will soon get underway

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is guiding Manchester United through pre-season (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has welcomed three new senior players to Manchester United so far this summer. But with pre-season now in full flow, there could also be a handful of exits.

‌



Champions League football will return to Old Trafford in the upcoming season after newly installed permanent boss Carrick turned the previous campaign from a disaster to a success.

‌



He has been backed in the transfer window to the tune of three new senior arrivals: Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow. Youngsters Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson have also joined.

‌



But one player whose future remains undetermined is Marcus Rashford. After spending last season on loan at Barcelona, the 28-year-old is stuck in limbo and a swap deal involving him has been mooted. Mirror Football takes a look at all the latest transfer speculation surrounding United.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd enter advanced talks for striker transfer with £30m clause proposed READ MORE :

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford swap deal

Despite impressing on loan in Catalonia last season, Barcelona did not exercise the £26m purchase option included in Rashford's deal and he therefore remains a United player.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford's future is uncertain (Image: Getty)

A route back to the Camp Nou has been sealed off with Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi signed and so it is currently unknown whether Rashford will return to fight for a place at Old Trafford or leave for pastures new.

Reports suggest neither side would ideally like Rashford to stay and Italian publication Gazzetta dello Sport states the Englishman could help get a deal for United target Manu Kone over the line.

‌



Kone, who currently plays for Roma, impressed at the World Cup for France and is reportedly available for £51m this summer. To help finance the move and offset his wage demands, it has been claimed that Rashford might head in the opposite direction.

Roma reportedly need a left-sided forward but are constrained by Financial Fair Play regulations. Rashford, whose £350,000-per-week wages have proved difficult to shift, could therefore be the makeweight in a deal for midfielder Kone.

Michael Carrick axes four players

Elsewhere, four of Rashford's team-mates appear set for the axe. The Daily Mail reports that goalkeeper Radek Vitek, defender Harry Amass and midfielders Dan Gore and Toby Collyer are all set to leave this summer.

‌



View 3 Images Gore and Collyer are likely to leave United (Image: Getty)

Young goalkeeper Vitek, as well as Amass, may initially be sent out on loan with an option to buy included. Vitek has become a target for multiple Championship teams and Amass is valued at about £6million.

Collyer spent last season on loan with Hull City and the newly promoted Tigers are reportedly interested in signing him permanently. Gore is on the chopping block following a loan with Rotherham United.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Gunners eye one deal before Bruno Guimaraes transfer as £75m bid submitted
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Gunners eye one deal before Bruno Guimaraes transfer as £75m bid submitted

Arsenal are closing in on multiple deals after a slow start to the transfer window

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is reportedly set to sign a defender (Image: Mike Hewitt, Getty Images)

Arsenal are ramping up their transfer activity as we enter the final month of the summer window. It has been a hectic few days in N5 regarding transfer news, with the Gunners’ interest in Vinicius Junior dominating the headlines.

‌



The Premier League champions are yet to submit a bid, however, with their pursuit of the Real Madrid superstar dependent on how the player’s talks over a new contract unfold this week. Elsewhere, Bruno Guimaraes remains a top priority, with the midfielder having been linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium for over six weeks now.

‌



The long list of rumoured targets also includes Julian Alvarez and a new target in striker Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who has reportedly informed Lille he wants to leave the French side. Nevertheless, Mikel Arteta’s only signings until now remain Piero Hincapie’s £34.5million permanent switch, Illan Meslier’s arrival as a free agent and Christos Tzolis’ £34m transfer from Club Brugge.

‌



Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer developments involving Arsenal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta could be forced to break his own Arsenal rule in major transfer U-turn READ MORE :

New £75m bid

Arsenal have reportedly submitted an improved offer for Bruno Guimaraes worth £75m. Reports last week claimed the Gunners had prepared a £70m bid for the Newcastle United midfielder, which was said to have been rejected.

‌



The English champions are understood to have used intermediaries in their negotiations with the Magpies rather than submitting a direct, official bid. But ESPN Brazil reports that Arsenal have now submitted an offer consisting of a guaranteed fee of £70m, plus £5m in bonuses and add-ons.

The report claims this bid is still below what Newcastle value their captain. However, the report adds that the likelihood of an agreement being reached is high, with negotiations very likely to progress this week.

Guimaraes has informed Newcastle bosses that he wants to leave if an agreement is reached with Arsenal, seeing the north Londoners as a clear step up in his career. Crucially, the 28-year-old will not try to force his way out of St James’ Park if the two clubs don’t agree on a fee.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are pushing to sign Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Getty )

Signing before Bruno Guimaraes deal

ESPN also claims Arsenal are close to completing the signing of a centre-back. The outlet reported on its YouTube channel that talks regarding a mystery defender are more advanced than the prospective deal for Guimaraes.

As such, it is claimed that a deal for the defender could be completed imminently, though his identity has not been disclosed. The Gunners have been linked to various defenders in recent weeks, given William Saliba’s back injury is set to rule him out for at least the first few months of the season.

Article continues below

John Stones was one potential target, but the England star is set to become an Inter Milan player this week. Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa is another defender Arsenal have been eyeing, though recent reports claimed the two clubs were far apart in their valuation of the England international.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino has come out to defend his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup as he underlines the global benefit despite major organisations in football looking to stop his proposal

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has attempted to sell his controversial World Cup plan

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has insisted that 'fans would gain immeasurably' from his proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup - which has been condemned by leading individuals and organisations within the game.

‌



Infantino has seen his popularity plummet following a World Cup that faced accusations of corruption and disregard for the laws of the game. Now, in what is seen as a major money grab, the FIFA president is looking to sell stakes in FIFA's major competitions.

‌



He has claimed that the planned deal would ultimately raise billions, which would be put back into the game, but auctioning off aspects of World Cup has not been well received.

‌



Infantino insisted the proposal was done so that FIFA could unlock "previously uncaptured commercial value" but maintained it would be the subject a democratic vote of FIFA's 211 member associations and approval by the FIFA council - even if he has threatened a lack of funding for those who don't back the idea.

UEFA and Andy Burnham among those to hit back at FIFA's World Cup sale proposal READ MORE :

Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date READ MORE :

In a video released on Wednesday the FIFA president has said: "FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It's part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

He went on to add: "Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport. It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA's 211 member associations."

‌



Infantino has appealed to the fans, claiming they would all benefit from the investment. "Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries," he said.

View 2 Images UEFA are looking to put a stop to Gianni Infantino's proposal (Image: Pau BARRENA/AFP via Getty Images)

UEFA have been outspoken against the idea and will hold a crisis meeting of its members to decide on action to hit back at Infantino’s World Cup plans. He has told countries that they have 53 days to sign up or face financial repercussions.

Article continues below

The 55 European associations are ­expected to discuss a range of actions, which includes a possible boycott of FIFA tournaments. Many of the leading figure in European football see Infantino's proposal as a bribe to the national associations.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star

Liverpool are keen on a deal for PSG star Bradley Barcola before the end of the transfer window but Reds legend Jamie Carragher is concerned over a deal for the Frenchman

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has shared his thoughts on Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool icon Jamie Carragher believes the Reds are targeting the wrong man in Bradley Barcola. Anfield chiefs are determined to add to their attacking options this summer following the exit of Mohamed Salah.

‌



A number of names have been linked including Yan Diomande - who looks set to join Real Madrid - and Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams. But it appears that the Reds are now putting all of their effort into signing Barcola.

‌



It has been reported that Liverpool are ready to submit their first bid for the 23-year-old, who is keen on a move, having turned down the chance to sign a new deal at the Parc des Princes. It has also been suggested that Liverpool may have to pay over £110m for his services.

‌



Liverpool icon Carragher has given his take on a move, but believes Liverpool would be better served spending their money elsewhere.

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

"No, he plays on the opposite flank!" Carragher wrote on social media. "LFC currently have three players who could play from the left in Rio/Gakpo/Wirtz & no one who plays from the right."

Asked if one solution could potentially be to switch academy graduate Rio Ngumoha over to the right-hand side, the former defender did not believe that would work either.

‌



"Well Rio has always played from the left so that’s obviously his best position," Carragher replied. "Gakpo should move really but who knows.

"I’m interested to see where Wirtz plays, if he’s 10 Dom plays CM. I’m not sure about that. Need a right winger desperately!"

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Liverpool have of course already added to their attacking options this summer, with a move for Osasuna’s Victor Munoz. The World Cup winner is set to arrive at Liverpool after a season in which he scored seven goals for the Spanish side in all competitions.

Asked if he had a number in his mind of how many players he would want to sign last week, boss Andoni Iraola replied: “No, I think it’s difficult to say a number when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

“There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

Article continues below

“But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things.”

Sports.title: Jack Grealish could take unlikely Man City exit route as record transfer snubbed
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish could take unlikely Man City exit route as record transfer snubbed

Jack Grealish has been overlooked for Manchester City's pre-season tour and the playmaker is attracting interest in Saudi Arabia, who could offer him a way out of the Etihad

View 2 Images Jack Grealish is now facing a tough summer (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Jack Grealish could be offered a shock route out of Manchester City with a move to Saudi Arabia potentially materialising for the out of favour playmaker.

‌



The former Aston Villa captain has been overlooked for City's pre-season tour to Hong Kong and Seoul. His foot injury was given as a key reason behind his omission, but it does little to suggested he will be part of Enzo Maresca's plans.

‌



Despite spending his entire career in England Al Hilal are considering a move, reports talkSport. They have already raided West Ham for Crysencio Summerville and Grealish is now on their radar as they eye quality on the flanks.

‌



The 30-year-old returned to his parent club this summer with his future unclear after spending last season on loan at Everton, where he impressed as he benefited from regular minutes for the first time in years.

Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes facing same transfer dilemma that Man Utd stars got wrong READ MORE :

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Despite that the Toffees chose not to take up the £50million purchase option in his loan agreement, leaving Grealish back at square one with his City days seemingly numbered as he remains on the periphery with his contract winding down.

Maresca, who has replaced Pep Guardiola, has worked with Grealish when he was an assistant at the Etihad and has already addressed the player's future, but was non-committal over their next move.

‌



"At the moment, he's here. He's a Man City player," he said during his first press conference. "I always said the same. In any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club. It's my duty to try to coach them. Jack is here. I have a good relationship with Jack since I left.

View 2 Images Manchester United are in talks with a move for Crysencio Summerville (Image: Getty Images)

"Also, we keep in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and he's a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens."

‌



Given he has 12 months left on his deal City are looking to secure a permanent exit, which will now come at a fraction of the £100m they spent to sign him in 2021 when he became their record signing - a tag Elliot Anderson has only just taken from him.

City have benefited from selling players to Saudi Arabian clubs with Riyad Mahrez, Aymeric Laporte and Riyad Mahrez all heading to the Middle East.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
