How did your social media followers react when you were unmasked?

They were so surprised because I usually take them with me everywhere I go in real time, I tell them everything. There are no secrets between us. So, when they saw me on the Masked Singer, they were like ‘oh my gosh, how did you manage to keep this from us’. They were very happy for me… for doing something outsdie my comfort zone. And they were sad that I left the show so early.



You’ve travelled across Africa. If you could have created a Mask inspired by your travels on the continent, what would it have been, and why?

It would definitely be an elephant, because I have searched for wild free roaming elephants in the barn and DRC many times and never found any, of course. But I also think that would have given it away, if I had designed my own costume.



The detectives had no clue who Pap & Wors was. What did you make of all their comments? Were you chuffed that they couldn’t figure you out?

I was very chuffed that they couldn’t figure it out. I think it would have been more interesting if they had found me out… they were way off the mark. So, that was funny to me. At some point Sithelo was like ‘oh my gosh’ I kow exactly who this is, and she was so sure of herself, that it made me nervous that she was about to reveal me. But she took a total left turn and named someone totally out of my field.

World.title: SA Rugby prepare unique response to All Blacks’ haka
World.content:
The All Blacks will soon tour South Africa. Images via X: @springboks/ @allblacks

A 30-year wait for the resumption of tours between rugby’s greatest rivals ended this week with the arrival of the touring All Blacks in South Africa for the start of an eight-match ‘odyssey’.

The All Blacks will first face the Stormers in Cape Town on 7 August, while matches against the Sharks and Bulls will precede the first Test at Ellis Park on 22 August.

There will then be a final midweek match against the Lions before the final three Tests in the series, which concludes in Baltimore, USA.



For the domestic sides, the lure of becoming the first South African provincial team to beat the All Blacks in South Africa since the 1976 tour will be a significant incentive.

Response to the All Blacks’ haka

As always, it will be interesting to see how supporters and opposing teams respond to the iconic haka, and SA Rugby have got something planned for the domestic games.

To give the four franchise matches a distinctive local flavour, SA Rugby launched a competition for schools, which has seen scores of impassioned and vibrant submissions.

The four selected winning schools will be given the opportunity to perform their war-cry as an answer to the All Blacks’ haka at each of the four franchise matches.

New Zealand were unbeaten in their provincial matches on their 1996 Tour, winning three and drawing one. They won the Test series – their first series victory in South Africa – by two Tests to one.

This time, the All Blacks will perform the haka in front of South Africa’s four United Rugby Championship teams and crowds.



Highly-anticipated tour

Tickets for the provincial matches and third Test are still available – CLICK HERE.

“Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry is more than a contest between two proud nations; it is a celebration of history, tradition and the enduring spirit of the game,” said Mr Mark Alexander, President of SA Rugby.

“Each encounter between South Africa and New Zealand carries with it the weight of decades of competition, respect and shared excellence.

“This rivalry has produced moments that have defined rugby itself, battles of skill, courage and resilience that inspire generations of players and supporters alike. It is a fixture that transcends sport, uniting communities and reminding us of rugby’s power to connect people across borders.

“As custodians of the game, we honour this rivalry not only for its intensity on the field but also for the values it represents: respect, sportsmanship, and the pursuit of excellence. Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry is a testament to the enduring bond between our nations and the global significance of our sport.”

World.title: eThekwini Municipality plans major upgrades for Durban ICC
World.content:
The eThekwini Municipality is investing R11.3 million in the Durban ICC. Image: wikimedia commons

The eThekwini Municipality has approved R11.3 million in upgrades to the Durban International Convention Centre (ICC) as the city prepares to host the 46th Southern African Development Community (SADC) Summit this August.

The investment comes as Durban welcomes delegates for SADC Industrialisation Week, currently underway at the ICC until 31 July, ahead of the summit of Heads of State and Government, which is expected to take place between 3 and 18 August.

President Cyril Ramaphosa is expected to attend the summit, which will bring together leaders and senior officials from across Southern Africa.



What the R11.3 million will pay for at the Durban ICC

The municipality said it had reprioritised projects within its 2026/27 capital budget to fund critical infrastructure and building upgrades at the ICC.

While earlier reports suggested the money would be used primarily to upgrade the venue’s toilets, the city has since clarified that the budget covers several essential improvements.

According to IOL, a report presented to the eThekwini Executive Committee revealed that the funding includes:



R6 million to replace the ICC’s defective Building Management System (BMS)

to replace the ICC’s defective Building Management System (BMS) R2 million to upgrade the front-of-house emergency door mechanisms

to upgrade the front-of-house emergency door mechanisms R3.3 million to refurbish the venue’s operable wall systems

The municipality also confirmed that the project includes upgrades to air-conditioning systems and other infrastructure required to ensure the venue is fully prepared for the summit.

Showcasing Durban on the regional stage

The municipality said the investment would not only ensure the successful hosting of the summit but also strengthen the Durban ICC’s long-term value as one of the city’s key strategic assets.

Hosting the event is expected to provide Durban with an opportunity to showcase itself as a leading destination for international conferences and business events while boosting its profile as a hub for regional cooperation, trade and investment.



The city added that the summit would attract heads of state and government, senior policymakers, business leaders and development partners from across the 16-member SADC bloc.

The summit will also mark South Africa’s assumption of the SADC chairship for the next 12 months, providing an opportunity to strengthen regional cooperation, economic integration, peace and security across Southern Africa.

World.title: Daily Snow Report: Severe weather forecast eases, but …
World.content:
SAWS says today's cold front has cleared, easing most of this week's severe weather warnings: Image ChatGPT

Today’s snow report for South Africa brings a much calmer picture than yesterday. Thursday, 30 July 2026 sees the cut-off low weather system that triggered this week’s orange-level warnings clear from the west, exactly as SAWS had forecast.

The only active alert now is a Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds and waves along the coast between KwaDukuza and Kosi Bay, a sharp step down from yesterday’s Orange Level 6 rain warning and Orange Level 5 snow warning across the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal.

Daily Snow Report: Cooler, calmer conditions across most of the country

According to SAWS, Gauteng can expect a partly cloudy and cool day, while Limpopo stays fine and cool to warm.



The Free State is cloudy with fog in places, and KwaZulu-Natal remains cloudy and cold, with scattered showers in the north; Durban itself sits cloudy with isolated showers, temperatures ranging between 14 and 20 degrees Celsius.

Mpumalanga can expect morning frost in places, becoming cloudy along the escarpment and Lowveld later in the day.

SAWS has confirmed only the one active wind and wave warning for today.



Mountain regions remain under close watch

While today’s system has largely moved through, the Maloti-Drakensberg range and the Lesotho border remain the country’s most snow-prone areas heading into the last stretch of winter, following Sani Pass’s closure under heavy snowfall back in June.

This snow report for South Africa will keep tracking the region as forecasters monitor the next system.

With winter’s final weeks still ahead, another cold snap could bring fresh snow before the season ends.



Is it snowing in your area? If so, please send your photos to info@thesouthafrican.com

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs transfer news: 3 players likely to leave
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have already strengthened their squad with four new signings this transfer window, but more arrivals could still be on the way. If that happens, further departures from Naturena are expected before the window closes.

‘s new recruits for the 2026/27 season include striker Khanyisa Mayo from CR Belouizdad, defender Thabo Moloisane from Stellenbosch FC, goalkeeper Renaldo Leaner from Sekhukhune United, and Tanzanian midfielder Adolf Bitegeko.

The Soweto giants have already released Happy Mashiane, George Matlou, Gaston Sirino and Tashreeq Morris as they continue reshaping the squad under new head coach Fernando Da Cruz.



Here are three players who could also leave Kaizer Chiefs before the transfer window shuts.

Ashley Du Preez

Ashley Du Preez has struggled to establish himself as a consistent starter during his four years at Naturena, despite producing flashes of brilliance.



One of his standout moments in Chiefs colours came when he scored a memorable brace in the Soweto Derby. However, injuries and inconsistent form have prevented him from becoming the club’s first-choice striker.

The 29-year-old has been linked with a return to Stellenbosch FC, with reports suggesting winger Langelihle Phili could move in the opposite direction as part of a potential swap deal.

Kaizer Chiefs to part ways with Cele?

Thabo Cele



Thabo Cele quickly became a fan favourite after joining Kaizer Chiefs in January 2025. His composure on the ball, accurate passing and ability to control the midfield made him an important player under former coach Nasreddine Nabi.

However, his role diminished following the arrival of Khalil Ben Youssef and Cedric Kaze to the technical team, with Cele often having to settle for appearances off the bench.

The 28-year-old also missed much of the club’s pre-season preparations, and under new coach Fernando Da Cruz, he appears to have fallen down the pecking order.



Samkelo Zwane

Samkelo Zwane spent last season on loan at Siwelele FC alongside Happy Mashiane. While Mashiane has since left the club, Zwane’s future at Chiefs remains uncertain.

The midfielder struggled for regular game time before his loan spell, and with Kaizer Chiefs boasting several options in central midfield, breaking into the starting line-up this season could prove difficult.



Unless the situation changes, another loan move or a permanent departure may be the most likely outcome for the 23-year-old before the transfer window closes.

World.title: Promoted Orlando Pirates winger chooses Mofokeng’s jersey number
World.content:
Mpho Padime winger has officially bearned promotion to the Buccaneers’ senior squad ahead of the 2026/27 Betway Premiership season after an outstanding campaign in the DStv Diski Challenge.

MPHO PADIME EARNS ORLANDO PIRATES PROMOTION

Born in June 2007 in Katlehong, Johannesburg, Padime first made his name in township football while playing for Khathorus Juventus FC. His dazzling dribbling, blistering pace and entertaining “Kasi Flava” style quickly attracted interest from several clubs.

Although Kaizer Chiefs offered him a development contract, the teenage star chose to join Orlando Pirates in September 2025.



His decision has already paid off. Playing under Roscoe Krieling in the DStv Diski Challenge, Padime scored 10 goals and provided nine assists during the 2025/26 season. His 19 goal contributions helped the Buccaneers win the reserve league title with a record-breaking 75 points.

The winger also travelled with the first team on their pre-season tour of Spain. He featured against Córdoba CF and UD Las Palmas, where he continued to impress the technical team.

ORLANDO PIRATES HAND PADIME ICONIC NUMBER

With Mofokeng completing his move to Europe earlier this month, Orlando Pirates have handed the number 38 jersey to one of the club’s brightest young prospects.



The shirt became synonymous with Mofokeng, who developed into one of South Africa’s biggest stars before securing his overseas move. Padime will now hope to build his own legacy in the same number.

The jersey change also reflects the club’s growing faith in academy talent. Padime is among several DStv Diski Challenge graduates promoted to the senior squad as Abdeslam Ouaddou prepares for his first season in charge of the reigning Betway Premiership champions.

World.title: Durban’s biggest beachfront hotel begins R250 million makeover
World.content:
Durban’s Golden Mile is set for another major boost, with Southern Sun officially beginning its R250 million makeover of the iconic Southern Sun Elangeni & Maharani Hotel.

The extensive renovation forms part of the continued revival of Durban’s beachfront and will see South Africa’s largest hotel transformed over the next three years while remaining open to guests.

A new look for one of Durban’s best-known hotels

The 734-room hotel, which dominates Durban’s beachfront skyline, was originally built as two separate towers by legendary hotelier Sol Kerzner in the 1970s before being combined into a single hotel in 2012.



According to hotel general manager Lettisha Singh, work has already started on the first 11 guest rooms, the exterior of the Elangeni tower and a new pool deck on top of the 33-storey Maharani tower.

The project will be carried out in phases to minimise disruption to guests.

Once complete, the overhaul will include:

Refurbishment of all 734 guest rooms

A redesigned foyer at the Elangeni tower

Upgraded conference and events facilities

Refreshed restaurants

A new club lounge in the Maharani tower

A new rooftop pool deck

Speaking during the Southern African Association for the Conference Industry’s (SAACI) annual conference, Singh said the investment reflects Southern Sun’s long-term commitment to Durban.

She described the hotel as a key tourism asset for both the city and the province, adding that the refurbishment is an exciting project for staff and visitors alike.

Part of the city’s beachfront revival

The renovation follows Southern Sun securing a new long-term lease from the eThekwini Municipality for the land on which the hotel stands.



The group’s original 50-year lease, dating back to the Kerzner era, was due to expire, prompting the city to open a competitive tender process. Southern Sun ultimately emerged as the sole bidder.

At the time, eThekwini Municipality said the agreement would unlock around R1 billion in investment across Southern Sun’s beachfront hotel portfolio over several years.

The Elangeni & Maharani is Southern Sun’s largest hotel in South Africa and one of four properties the group owns along Durban’s beachfront.

Its other Golden Mile hotels include:

Garden Court South Beach

Garden Court Marine Parade

The Edward

The revamped Elangeni & Maharani is expected to reinforce its position as one of Durban’s flagship beachfront hotels while adding further momentum to the ongoing transformation of the Golden Mile.

World.title: Relay team-mates help Chad le Clos to historic 21st Commonwealth Games medal
World.content:
If ever there was a fairytale ending to a Commonwealth Games career, Chad le Clos delivered it in Glasgow on Wednesday evening. Image: ANTON GEYSER/TeamSA

If ever there was a fairytale ending to a Commonwealth Games career, Chad le Clos delivered it in Glasgow on Wednesday evening.

The South African swimming icon claimed his record-breaking 21st Commonwealth Games medal in the final race of the swimming programme, cementing his place as the most decorated athlete in the history of the Games across all sports.

The milestone came in the men’s 4x100m medley relay, bringing the curtain down on another successful campaign for Team South Africa at Glasgow’s Tollcross International Swimming Centre.



🥉 BRONZE for Team South Africa in the Men's 4 x 100m Medley Relay — 3:31.13 at Tollcross Swimming Centre!



The squad: Pieter Coetzé, Michael Houlie, Chad le Clos and Ruard van Renen.



The bronze medal also sees Chad le Clos become the most decorated athlete in Commonwealth Games… pic.twitter.com/p17QYlOFNL — Team South Africa (@OfficialTeamRSA) July 29, 2026

Fitting conclusion

It was a fitting conclusion to a journey that began nearly 16 years ago, when a 19-year-old Le Clos won 200m butterfly gold at the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi.

Now 34, Le Clos stands alone atop the all-time medals table after surpassing Australian swimmer Emma McKeon who held the record with 20.



His latest medal was his third relay medal of the Games, following South Africa’s podium finishes in the mixed 4×100 medley relay and men’s 4×100 freestyle relay earlier in the week.

Reflecting on the achievement, Chad le Clos admitted the moment was emotional.

“Tonight was emotional,” he said after the medal ceremony.



“But I think those first two (relay medals) were just a little bit more because I had to get over the hump and tonight I just had to stay cool and hopefully bring it home.”

The veteran revealed that one of his proudest moments came not from a race he swam, but from watching his team-mates compete.

“Tuesday night’s relay final was probably the most emotional of the Games. The way the boys and girls swam, they swam their hearts out. They keep saying, ‘legacy’, we are doing this for Chad before they walked down. It just means the world to me.”



Family support

Family support has been a constant throughout his remarkable career, and Glasgow was no different.

“I can’t describe the support over the years. This week has been special because my brother’s daughter was born on 1 October 2010 and she was here to watch me 16 years later. They’ve been there every step of the way – my parents, both my brothers and sister.”

Looking back on his Commonwealth Games journey, Le Clos admitted he never imagined becoming the Games’ greatest medallist.



“Looking back on the whole Commonwealth Games journey, from India through to now, I never thought I’d be standing here,” he said.

“To stand alone in history is unbelievable. Four years ago, I needed one more medal, then Emma came past me, and suddenly I needed three more. We just took it one day at a time.”

Record to stand for many years

Le Clos finishes his Commonwealth Games career with an extraordinary haul of 21 medals – seven gold, five silver and nine bronze – a record that may stand for years to come.



Ten of Le Clos’ medals have come in relays.

His achievement also capped a successful swimming campaign for Team South Africa, which picked up 22 medals in the pool, comprising six gold, seven silver and nine bronze.

And on what the future of South Africa swimming looks like going into LA28, he had one response, “unbelievable.”

World.title: Bride advert seeking young girls sparks child protection concerns
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A newspaper  by a 58-year-old Free State man seeking a bride aged between 16 and 25 has sparked widespread backlash, with child protection advocates warning that it could expose vulnerable young women and girls to exploitation.

The man, whose name is known to eNCA, describes himself in the  as a wealthy farmer seeking what he calls “a pure, marriageable lady” with “biblical values”.

The advert, published in Die Burger on 24 July, promises a R100,000 bride price for the woman’s parents and a R5 million inheritance for the successful applicant.

The inclusion of 16- and 17-year-olds has drawn particular concern.

While the age of consent in South Africa is 16, anyone under the age of 18 is legally regarded as a child, and child-protection organisations say the advert raises serious safeguarding concerns.

Shaheda Omar, director of the Teddy Bear Foundation, said the advert could place vulnerable young people at risk, regardless of whether it was intended as a genuine proposal, satire or a publicity stunt.

"Whether it's genuine, a publicity stunt or intended satire, the potential consequences are serious because vulnerable individuals may perceive it as a legitimate opportunity," she said.

"The promise of a R100,000 bride price and a R5-million estate provision could be particularly appealing to young women and girls experiencing poverty, unemployment or family hardship."

Omar said financial desperation can impair judgement, making people more susceptible to exploitation and coercion.

She also criticised the inclusion of 16-year-olds, saying the advert shared characteristics commonly associated with grooming.

"The inclusion of 16-year-olds in such an advert is deeply concerning because it targets an age group that requires protection rather than recruitment into intimate relationships with unknown adults."

The advert states that the prospective bride should be a non-smoker with “deep core beliefs”, and that the husband would be the head of the household in accordance with what it describes as “original Biblical principles”.

World.title: L'Vovo fundraiser highlights entertainment industry's failure, says Devnarain
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The entertainment industry needs to acknowledge its own failure, says Jack Devnarain.

“We have failed to provide social security for our creatives,” he says.

His comments come after members of the public took to social media to raise funds for musician Thokozani Ndlovu, better known as L’Vovo.

Ndlovu suffered a near-fatal stroke in December 2022, forcing him to step away from the spotlight to focus on his recovery.

He had been performing at a show in Ndwedwe when he suffered the stroke, which left the left side of his body weakened and affected his speech.

Last week, Ndlovu gave an emotional interview to Gagasi FM, prompting social media user Yenziwe Qiniso Ndimande to launch a fundraising campaign.

She wrote on Facebook: “Please note that L’Vovo did not ask for donations. Many people were touched by his interview, and from there, we decided to come together and support him.”

Within hours, more than R100,000 had been raised. By the end of the week, that amount had doubled.

Devnarain said the news of Ndlovu’s health struggles had been unsettling.

“He is one of those iconic performers. He is recognised and celebrated,” he said.

“To hear that he’s going through this difficult time is where the industry itself needs to acknowledge its own failure.”

Devnarain said the industry has failed to establish structures to regulate the entertainment sector.

He said these structures would ensure that creatives’ earnings and workers’ rights are protected by law.

“We have petitioned the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture, which has failed to introduce the necessary safeguards,” he said.

World.title: FIFA proposal 'an opportunity but not an obligation', says Infantino
World.content:
PARIS - FIFA president Gianni Infantino said that the proposed launch of a private subsidiary to exploit the commercial benefits of the World Cup was "an opportunity but not an obligation".

A proposal to sell stakes in FIFA's major competitions sparked disbelief and outrage globally since it was revealed Tuesday, but Infantino defended the idea, saying too little of football's commercial value reached the parts of the game that need it most.

"FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It's part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation," Infantino said in a video released Wednesday evening.

"It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

Infantino insisted the proposal was centred on unlocking "previously uncaptured commercial value" and was conditional on a democratic vote of FIFA's 211 member associations and approval by the FIFA council.

"Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport," he said.

"It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA's 211 member associations."

Infantino said the game would not change and the fans would be happier.

"Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries," he said.

World.title: New Zealand foreign minister in racism row with Chinese ambassador
World.content:
WELLINGTON - New Zealand's top diplomat Winston Peters drew the ire of Beijing's ambassador in Wellington on Thursday after telling a lawmaker of Chinese descent to "go back to your own country".

During a debate about New Zealand's response to the Covid pandemic on Wednesday, populist NZ First leader Peters was asked by China-born Green Party member Lawrence Xu-Nan: "Are you vaccinated?"

In response, Peters said the lawmaker, who was born in the Chinese city of Tianjin but grew up in Auckland, had "come here five minutes ago".

"Go back to your own country. That's where they lie like a flatfish, but they don't lie like that here," Peters said.

"This is called a democracy, unlike what you're used to. Go back to where you've come from, you loudmouth."

The comments sparked a rare intervention from Chinese ambassador to New Zealand Wang Xiaolong.

Wang said on X on Thursday that while he preferred to stay out of domestic politics, "suffice it to say, sometimes, a statement says more about the person that makes it than anything or anybody else".

Peters fired back at Wang, saying his comments had "proven my point".

"We live in a democracy that includes free speech and rights -- those two values that other certain countries not only limit, but do so with force," Peters said on X.

"If that offends the pearl clutchers and the communist shills labelling it as 'dangerous' -- welcome to New Zealand".

It's not the first time Peters and his party -- seen as kingmakers in New Zealand's fractured political system -- have received criticism for racist comments.

Earlier this year Peters' deputy Shane Jones criticised New Zealand's free trade deal with India as risking a "butter chicken tsunami".

Last year Peters and Jones were forced to back down after the deputy yelled "send the Mexicans home" at Mexican-born MP Francisco Hernandez during a debate.

Peters had followed up that comment by telling Hernandez and Xu-Nan to "show some gratitude" for being in New Zealand.

World.title: Japanese population below 120 million for first time in decades
World.content:
TOKYO - The number of Japanese people living in the country has fallen below 120 million for the first time in 42 years, government data showed as the nation confronts a low birth rate and an ageing society.

As of January 1, the population of Japanese residents in Japan stood at 119.74 million, down 0.76 percent from the previous year, according to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.

The population of Japanese residents has been declining for 17 consecutive years since peaking in 2009, according to the survey, which began in 1968.

However, the population of foreign residents living in Japan reached its highest level since record-keeping began in 2013, according to the ministry.

Including them, the total population stands at 123.8 million.

With a median age of 49.9 years, Japan has the second-oldest population in the world after Monaco, according to the World Bank.

Data in June showed that Japan's fertility rate fell again last year to a new record low, underscoring the demographic crisis gnawing at the world's fourth-largest economy.

The slow-burning emergency is already leading to labour shortages, a ballooning social security bill and a shrinking tax base.

Government figures showed the total fertility rate -- the average number of children a woman is expected to have during her lifetime -- dropped by 0.01 from a year earlier to 1.14, the 10th straight year of decline.

The number of babies born in the country fell by nearly 15,000 to just over 670,000, the lowest figure since records began in 1899.

A chink of light came this month with news that 265 couples had married thanks to an AI-powered dating app launched by the Tokyo government.

TOKYO Enmusubi went live in September 2024 after a survey found that around 70 percent of people interested in marriage were not actively engaging in matchmaking.

To overcome this reluctance and ensure that only people interested in tying the knot joined, those signing up had to prove that they were legally single and pass an online interview, among other conditions.

As of June 30 this year, the app had 16,000 registered members -- whittled down from around 36,000 applicants -- and 760 couples in "serious relationships", according to government data released this month.

The government quoted one woman with the pseudonym "Turtle" as saying she tried the app "as a last chance" as she approached her 40th birthday.

"After going on several blind dates, I met my current husband at the end of August, and we started a serious relationship in mid-September," she said.

"I accepted his proposal at the end of December."

World.title: Madlanga Commission to recall Andrea Johnson over fresh claims
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) head Advocate Andrea Johnson will be summoned back to the Madlanga Commission to respond to fresh allegations.

It emerged during proceedings on Thursday morning that additional serious allegations have been made against Johnson.

A formal notice will now be issued compelling her to return to the witness stand to respond to them.

The allegations are expected to be revealed during the testimony of IDAC state advocate Drushantha Ramsamy, who is on the stand.

The commission received an electronic statement from Ramsamy on Wednesday.

Johnson concluded her six-day marathon testimony before the commission on Wednesday.

This is a developing story.

World.title: LIVE | Madlanga Commission continues focus on IDAC
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) is not off the hook yet as the Madlanga Commission continues its focus on the anti-corruption unit.

A new witness will testify on Thursday morning.

But what has come out during Andrea Johnson's final day has South Africans talking.

The Commission exposed the former IDAC head's relationship with Crime Intelligence Officer Feroz Khan.

Johnson had described their relationship as professional, but it went beyond that, with the pair calling each other pet names and protecting each other.

World.title: Key witness under pressure as Mapisa-Nqakula trial resumes
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula is back at the High Court in Pretoria for her corruption trial.

She is accused of soliciting bribes from Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlovu in return for defence contracts.

The businesswoman is the state's key witness in the R4.5-million bribery trial.

She is under cross-examination after testifying that she feared for her life when the scandal became public.

The defence argues this is just a ploy to paint Mapisa-Nqakula as heartless and immoral.

The court heard the former Minister threatened to clear funds from a defence tender account if her demands for money were not met.

World.title: Man jailed for 15 years over bhang trafficking in Nyeri
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nyeri Senior Principal Magistrate Faith Munyi convicted John Githinji on Thursday after finding him guilty of trafficking narcotic drugs contrary to section 4(a)(ii)of the narcotic drugs.

Githinji was charged that on June 4,2025 at Lusio trading center in Kieni East sub-county -Nyeri County was found trafficking bhang by selling 50 rolls and 1350 grams of cannabis sativa with a street value of Sh 40,500 which was not in medicinal form.



He was also faced with an alternative charge of possession of narcotic drugs to section 3(2)of the narcotic drugs and psychotropic substance control amendment act of 2022.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).
