World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to India fall as New Delhi diversifies import sources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil exports to India fell in the first half of 2026, as Indian refineries diversified their crude import sources to minimize the geopolitical risks associated with shipping via the Straits of Hormuz.

According to officials at Indian refining companies and the Indian Ministry of Petroleum, the goal of this measure is to improve supply security.

The drop in Iraqi supplies to India comes at a time when the global oil market is under increased pressure due to security worries along critical maritime routes. This pressure is causing consumers in Asia to split their purchases among many producing countries.

Iraqi oil remains a vital resource for India due to supply security and the high quality of Basra crude.

Indian refiners confirmed they have secured their crude oil requirements until the end of September and have begun arranging purchases for the fourth quarter of the year, despite persistent concerns about the impact of any interruptions to shipping routes on global supply chains.

Meanwhile, Russia remained India’s top crude oil supplier in the first half of the year, while imports from the UAE and Brazil increased.

India’s purchases from Iraq and the United States fell as New Delhi attempted to diversify its supply sources and reduce the risks associated with reliance on a single source.

Indian refiners have warned that increased shipping risks and higher insurance costs, along with declining discounts on Russian oil, are affecting profit margins.

Experts anticipate that continuing instability in the Middle East will raise oil prices and pose new hurdles for Asian oil-importing countries.

World.title: Six Iranian advisors killed in US-Saudi attack on Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A joint US-Saudi attack on targets in Iraq killed six Iranian advisors on Wednesday, according to two Iraqi officials who spoke to the Associated Press (AP).

A meeting that was set for Thursday in Saudi Arabia between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was called off due to recent attacks by armed groups targeting Saudi Arabia.

Al-Zaidi ordered an emergency meeting of Iraq’s National Security Council following the coordinated attacks on the country.

The Iraqi Security Media Cell said in a statement that the meeting was ordered in response to the evolving security situation and the airstrikes that targeted several Iraqi provinces early on Wednesday.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Wednesday that US forces, in cooperation with Saudi armed forces, carried out precision airstrikes targeting sites linked to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

The coordinated airstrikes were in retaliation for a series of drone attacks targeting US interests and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

CENTCOM said in a statement that the strikes, carried out on July 28, targeted logistics sites and weapons depots allegedly used by Iranian-backed groups. It added that these groups were directed by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to attack US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

US and Saudi fighter jets carried out the strikes, an operation described by CENTCOM as a strong response to more than 30 drone attacks that the IRGC had conducted in the past few days.

Headquarters and sites belonging to the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) in several Iraqi provinces were targeted by the US-Saudi airstrikes in the country.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes test Iraq’s fragile security balance
World.content:
Baghdad – US-Saudi strikes on Iraq killed at least 20 militants, including several Iranians, on Wednesday, according to the Hashed al-Shaabi, an armed Iraqi alliance that includes pro-Iran groups.

The United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed armed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Washington and Tehran are Iraq’s main allies, but their enmity has long turned the country into a proxy battleground and left successive governments struggling to maintain a delicate balance between the foes.

The Hashed al-Shaabi, also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), said that at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll”.

Two Hashed officials told AFP that five Iranian advisors were among those killed in a strike in the central province of Diyala.

AFP correspondents saw coffins wrapped in Iranian flags during a funeral organised by the Hashed al-Shaabi in Baghdad for those killed.

The Hashed alliance was created in 2014 to fight jihadists before it was formally integrated into the Iraqi armed forces.

It now includes brigades belonging to Iran-backed groups reputed for acting unilaterally.

US President Donald Trump said the strikes were coordinated with the Iraqi government, according to Fox News.

They follow growing US pressure on Baghdad to disarm pro-Iran armed groups, which have frequently targeted US facilities in the country and have long called for the withdrawal of US troops.

Iraq’s new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who came to power this year with Washington’s blessing, vowed to ensure those groups would hand over their weapons, but has faced pushback from some powerful factions.

Earlier this month, Zaidi visited both the United States and Iran.

– ‘Inevitable response’ –

The strikes came after Riyadh said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities, blaming the Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

The most active pro-Iran armed groups are united under an alliance known as the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, which has acted in support of Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks against US bases in Iraq and across the region.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq said “our response to the American enemy is inevitable, and may target its tools in Saudi Arabia”.

But the group added that it would only retaliate after the Arbaeen day of pilgrimage, which falls on Tuesday.

The Arbaeen marks one of the most significant events in the Shia Muslim calendar, during which pilgrims, many from Iran, flock to Iraq to visit the holy shrines.

The pro-Iran groups denied attacking Saudi Arabia and they haven’t claimed any attacks since the US-Iran war resumed earlier this month.

– Violation –

Iraq denounced the US-Saudi strikes and said it rejects “all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented.”

The Ministerial Council for National Security said it would “confront any violation of Iraq’s sovereignty, and prevent any source from using Iraqi territory to threaten neighbouring states”.

It reaffirmed its commitment to ensure the state’s monopoly over weapons.

Zaidi’s government has given those groups that Washington designates as terrorist organisations until September 30 to disarm.

Oil-rich Iraq has been trying to move past decades of war and unrest, but it remains vulnerable to regional and internal flare-ups.

World.title: Iraq condemns US-Saudi strikes, vows tighter control over armed groups
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq condemned U.S.-Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday that targeted Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites, calling the attacks a violation of its sovereignty, and announced new measures to tighten state control over security and prevent Iraqi territory from being used to threaten neighboring countries.

Following the attacks, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, which the government said killed and injured many Iraqis.

As regional tensions rose, Al-Zaidi cancelled a planned visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

In a statement published after the meeting, the council said that the strikes happened when Baghdad was already in talks with US and Saudi authorities over suspicions that Iran-aligned armed organizations operating from Iraq committed drone assaults on Saudi land.

“The government was actively engaging with the relevant parties to verify and address the concerns raised by both the Saudi and US sides,” the statement stated, adding that the military action hampered such efforts.

The council authorized a comprehensive security strategy aimed at strengthening state authority across Iraq, combating breaches of Iraqi sovereignty, and prohibiting any party from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten neighboring nations.

The steps reflect Baghdad’s efforts to guarantee that no armed organization may launch assaults from Iraqi soil that could pull the nation into larger regional wars, while also confirming the government’s goal of bringing all security actions under state control.

The council also directed the Foreign Ministry to take legal and diplomatic measures under international law and the United Nations Charter to record the attacks and protect Iraq’s legal rights.

The government condemned the attacks but emphasized that responding to security threats and enforcing the law is solely the responsibility of Iraq’s constitutional institutions.

“The government rejects all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented,” the statement read.

The council underlined Baghdad’s commitment to addressing regional conflicts via diplomacy while maintaining efforts to keep all armaments under state control.

It also restated Iraq’s commitment to carrying out the security agreement guiding the departure of the US-led international coalition by the end of September 2026.

The emergency conference occurred hours after US President Donald Trump claimed that the midnight attacks were coordinated with the Iraqi government, something Baghdad has not officially verified.

Iraqi authorities have openly opposed the operation, emphasizing the political sensitivity of the attacks.

The events highlight Al-Zaidi’s increasingly precarious situation, as he seeks to boost Iraq’s connections with the US and Gulf Arab governments while retaining relations with Iran.

His decision to cancel the Saudi visit underlines the gravity of the problem, as Baghdad seeks to temper regional tensions while preventing Iraqi land from becoming a battlefield for opposing forces.

The government’s current security strategy also suggests a renewed desire to prevent armed groups from operating outside official control, as Baghdad wants to reassure neighboring nations that Iraq will not be used as a springboard for assaults that endanger regional peace.

World.title: Uptime Institute partners with T964 to expand Iraq’s digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Uptime Institute, based in the United States, and Iraqi digital infrastructure company Tech964 Holding Limited (T964) have formed a strategic partnership to help develop Iraq’s digital infrastructure, marking the latest technology agreement to result from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s investment-focused visit to Washington.

The agreement, signed earlier this month at the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit hosted by the US Chamber of Commerce, names T964 as Uptime Institute’s business partner in Iraq to promote international data center standards, professional training, and the development of resilient digital infrastructure.

The agreement is part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy beyond oil by increasing digital infrastructure, attracting technological investment, and bolstering industries including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, financial technology, and cybersecurity.

T964, one of Iraq’s major private digital infrastructure businesses, has announced that it would collaborate with the Uptime Institute to implement internationally recognized standards for the country’s expanding network of data centers, as well as increase technical competence and operational best practices.

The partnership is anticipated to help establish carrier-neutral data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud services, and AI-ready digital platforms, all of which the government believes are important to modernizing public services and stimulating private-sector investment.

The pact follows a series of technological ties announced during Al-Zaidi’s tour to the United States, during which Iraq inked more than 50 agreements totaling more than $60 billion in the energy, banking, infrastructure, industrial, and technology sectors.

Improving digital infrastructure has become a key component of Iraq’s long-term economic plan, as the country strives to lessen reliance on oil earnings and establish a knowledge-based economy capable of attracting foreign technology businesses while also encouraging homegrown innovation.

The alliance also underscores increased US private-sector interest in Iraq’s digital economy, especially as demand for secure data centers, cloud computing capacity, and AI infrastructure in the Middle East grows.

Iraq has increasingly prioritized digital infrastructure for foreign investment alongside energy and transportation, with officials claiming that internationally certified data centers and modern telecommunications networks will be critical to supporting e-government services, digital banking, e-commerce, and artificial intelligence, as well as strengthening Iraq’s role as an emerging regional technology hub.

World.title: OpenAI says rogue AI agent attack hit other companies
World.content:
San Francisco – ChatGPT maker OpenAI has revealed that an autonomous artificial intelligence agent which hacked a popular platform for computer programmers also attempted to breach four other companies during the incident.

In an update late Tuesday to a blog post detailing its probe into the incident, OpenAI said its AI agent affected these “publicly-available services,” though it did not name the companies.

The revelation broadens a cyber incident that OpenAI described as unprecedented and which began when two of its models hacked Hugging Face, a site developers use to store and share AI models and code.

OpenAI admitted last week that during testing, the models powering the agent broke out of their confined environment and connected to the internet to find ways to infiltrate Hugging Face.

AI agents — systems that act autonomously to complete tasks rather than just responding to step-by-step prompts in a chatbot — are hailed across the industry as the next chapter in AI.

But they raise the specter among the public of rogue computers acting on their own.

In its update of the events leading to the hack, OpenAI said it found a handful of instances where the AI models came across login details that other companies had left exposed online, and used them to get into accounts on outside services.

In the Hugging Face episode, the models broke into four accounts across four different services, OpenAI said. One served as a “staging path” — a kind of pit stop to route the agent’s activity and cover its tracks — and another as a place to store data.

The remaining two were only accessed in a “read-only manner” and were not used to help break into Hugging Face, OpenAI said.

The company said it was contacting the owners of the affected accounts and had “not seen evidence of broader impact to these providers or other accounts on their services.”

– Better sandbox –

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview published Tuesday that the company had “paused” its own testing after the incident while it improved the security around its “sandboxing” — the process of isolating safety testing in a controlled environment.

The incident also triggered a petition signed by over 1,000 employees at cutting-edge AI companies, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, calling on the US government to help slow the release of the most advanced AI models.

This in turn has sparked accusations from other Silicon Valley players close to the White House that the companies are inviting tighter government regulation on AI in order to protect their business models and block the emergence of rivals.

The incident has also drawn rumblings from some observers that OpenAI is taking advantage of it to market the power of its state-of-the-art models.

The same accusation was leveled at Anthropic when it held back the public release of its powerful Mythos model over cybersecurity concerns.

Anthropic released a stripped-down version of Mythos, called Fable 5, but the US government quickly forced it to take it down, citing national security risks.

It gave the green light in late June after some modifications were made.

World.title: Syria’s Kurds still waiting to go home despite govt deal
World.content:
Hasakeh – At a desolate Syrian camp, home to thousands of displaced Kurds, Ahmad Oussi appealed for help to return to his hometown, seven years after a Turkish offensive drove him out.

Residents of the Talaeh camp complain former Turkish-backed fighters are squatting in their properties in the Ras al-Ain area, around 70 kilometres (40 miles) away.

“The factions are living in our homes,” Oussi, 26, complained. “We get calls from them telling us, ‘You can’t go back to your homes … they’re our homes now’.”

Oussi is among tens of thousands of Kurds who were displaced when Turkey and allied Syrian fighters seized an Arab-majority strip of border territory, including Ras al-Ain, from Kurdish control in 2019 during the civil war.

Some of the fighters subsequently settled in the area with their families, with some reportedly still living in Ras al-Ain, a formerly ethnically-mixed region in Syria’s northeast.

Oussi said the former fighters “have nowhere to go, that’s why they haven’t left our homes”.

“I hope the Kurdish administration and the Syrian government, foremost the defence ministry, will get us out of this camp and return us to our town as soon as possible,” he said.

– ‘No safety’ –

Some 5.5 million people remain internally displaced in Syria following the more than 13-year civil war, according to the United Nations.

Near tents at the camp outside the city of Hasakeh, some people have built small mud-brick homes as refuge from the scorching summer heat and bitter winter cold.

A woman hunched over to sweep the dirt as people sold fuel in soft-drink bottles by the roadside.

“We’re always told we’ll go back this week or next but it hasn’t happened yet,” said mother-of-seven Kubar Qader, 43, picking through second-hand clothes stall.

“There’s no safety because they’re still living in our homes. We’re afraid of returning… we want to go back and live in our home without fear or threat,” she said.

Turkey launched successive military offensives against Kurdish-led forces in northern Syria before the new Islamist authorities, who are close to Ankara, ousted longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in 2024.

Human rights groups say residents’ homes and belongings were seized or looted after the 2019 offensive to capture Ras al-Ain.

The return of displaced Kurds was part of a deal reached in January between the under-pressure Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and Damascus on integrating Kurdish institutions into the state.

Since then, displaced people have returned to the Kurdish-majority Afrin region in northwest Syria, the scene of a 2018 Turkish-led offensive, but Ras al-Ain residents are still waiting.

– ‘Die there’ –

Abdel-Karim Omar, the Kurdish authorities’ representative in Damascus, said the return of the displaced to Ras al-Ain was one of the deal’s “main outstanding issues requiring implementation”.

Jawan Isso, from a committee representing displaced people from the area, said preliminary steps had been taken on returns, including visits and de-mining operations.

But “significant obstacles” remain, he added, citing the security situation and saying the town “is still under Turkish influence”.

According to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights monitor, Turkish troops are mainly present in three positions in the Ras al-Ain area.

A Hasakeh province official played down the problem, telling AFP that “dozens of families have returned” to their homes in Ras al-Ain.

“Some factional members were living in properties and homes but they left immediately after the owners” approached the local authorities, he said, requesting anonymity.

Some displaced Kurds, he added, are linked to the SDF and fear “acts of revenge and accountability unless they return through the state officially”.

Camp resident Fatna Abdel-Qader, 65, still dreams of Ras al-Ain.

“This tent is nothing like the home I left seven years ago,” she said, wiping away tears. “I long for the land of Ras al-Ain, and it is my wish to die there.”

World.title: Trump: US-Saudi strikes in Iraq coordinated with Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that US-Saudi airstrikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq were carried out in coordination with the Iraqi government, a statement that, if confirmed, would represent a significant shift in Baghdad’s approach to powerful armed groups aligned with Tehran.

In an interview with Fox News, Trump referred to Iran-backed militias in Iraq as “a cancer on the world” and stated that he is considering “additional warnings” against Iranian proxy groups following the strikes.

The strikes were coordinated with the Iraqi government, referring to a joint US-Saudi operation.

The Iraqi administration did not immediately respond to Trump’s accusations.

The raids targeted outposts of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), an umbrella organization that encompasses multiple Iran-backed militias and is officially incorporated into Iraq’s military forces.

The PMF said that at least 20 of its members were murdered and 32 were injured in assaults across seven Iraqi regions.

The action followed a series of drone strikes on Saudi Arabia’s eastern oil installations, which Riyadh said were carried out by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi territory.

The attacks were one of the most important military actions within Iraq in years, surprising many Iraqis and sparking fears that the nation was becoming a battleground for a broader regional conflict.

Hours after the strikes, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled travel to Saudi Arabia and held an emergency conference with top security officials, condemning the assaults as a breach of Iraqi sovereignty and urging caution.

Trump’s claim that Baghdad coordinated the operation seems to contradict his first public pronouncements.

If proven, however, it would imply that Iraqi officials covertly authorized action against forces that they increasingly see as acting beyond governmental authority.

Although the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its most prominent sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have repeatedly carried out military operations autonomously of the Iraqi government.

Baghdad’s regional allies have accused these organizations of dragging the country into conflicts that are detrimental to its national interests.

Analysts believe that any clandestine Iraqi collaboration with the attacks would signal rising irritation inside Baghdad with armed organizations suspected of working on behalf of Iran rather than the Iraqi state.

This change would also reflect Al-Zaidi’s larger attempts to reestablish government authority over security policy while boosting relations with the US and Gulf Arab governments.

The strikes occurred just one day after Al-Zaidi returned from a high-profile visit to Turkey, where Iraq signed agreements on energy, trade, and the Development Road transportation corridor, and weeks after visits to Washington and Tehran aimed at balancing relations with rival regional powers while attracting foreign investment.

The recent escalation highlights Baghdad’s increasingly precarious position as it strives to maintain relations with Tehran while strengthening security and economic ties with Washington and its Gulf allies.

Whether Trump’s assertion represents a major shift in Iraqi policy is likely to be one of the most keenly followed issues in the wake of the strikes.

World.title: 'Tweaking anti-paper leak law a hogwash': Kharge tears into Centre, backs NEET protest
World.content:
Mallikarjun Kharge said the bill has just been tabled to quell the anger of student.

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday tore into the central government over the "anti-paper leak Bill", saying the amendment to the law does not address the core issue of how to prevent paper leaks.The Congress leader said the Bill had been introduced merely to quell the anger of students, which has been witnessed on the streets over the past few weeks.

World.title: NCP to merge with Sharad Pawar faction? What party veteran Chhagan Bhujbal said
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Speculation over a possible reunion of the Nationalist Congress Party's two factions resurfaced on Thursday after senior leader Chhagan Bhujbal made fresh remarks on the issue, days after Sharad Pawar dismissed reports of a merger.

Speaking to reporters during a visit to Pune, the Maharashtra minister was asked whether the rival NCP factions could come together. Responding to the question, Bhujbal said the decision rested with party president Sunetra Pawar and suggested there was little point in debating the matter until the leadership took a call.

"Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar is the (NCP) president, and a decision will be taken under her guidance.

It is the media that fuels such speculation, so there is no point in discussing it. It will happen when it has to happen. Political leaders do meet one another on various issues. In democracy, dialogue should always happen."

His comments came two days after NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) chief Sharad Pawar rejected speculation over a possible merger of the two factions. Asked about the buzz by reporters on Tuesday, Pawar replied, "It has no relevance."





Bhujbal was in Pune to review the ongoing work at Bhidewada, the site where social reformers Mahatma Jyotirao Phule and Savitribai Phule started India's first school for girls.

After meeting officials of the Pune Municipal Corporation, the minister said the government wanted to preserve the legacy of Phule Wada and make its history accessible to students.

"...We want to showcase the history of Phule Wada to students.

Rs 200 crore have been allocated for the expansion of Phule Wada. The chief minister has held meetings on the issue, but the work has not been completed in a satisfactory manner. We are ready to provide the land and we have completed all the necessary work," he said.

Phule Wada, the former residence of Mahatma Jyotirao Phule and Savitribai Phule, is now a protected state heritage site and museum that commemorates their pioneering work in women's education and the fight against caste discrimination.

World.title: 'Expresses regret': Meta agrees to meet govt clarifying policy after PM Modi video glitch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Meta has agreed to appear before the government to clarify policy and technical issues related to its operations, ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) secretary S Krishnan said on Thursday.

Krishnan said the company would engage with the government to explain concerns surrounding its policies and technical framework.

Krishnan said the government has asked Meta to depute its senior-most representatives to explain the issues flagged by the authorities and provide clarity on both the policy and technical aspects of the matter.

"Meta, we have asked them to come in at the highest level and explain what is happening and why the kind of issues that we see...,"

Krishnan was quoted as saying by ANI.

According to Krishnan, Meta has also informed the government that it introduced new protocols on July 28 for handling accounts of prominent individuals to prevent similar incidents from recurring.

"Meta has written to government expressing regret over the incident and that it had happened. They have also given us the reasons, their understanding of the reason why it happened and they have also indicated that as of 28th of July, they have established new protocols relating to accounts of prominent persons to avoid such a situation from recurring."





He said the government wants to understand the concerns from both policy and technical perspectives and assess how the company can adapt its practices to address India's concerns.

Krishnan said the government is examining the matter and has sought inputs from several messaging platforms as part of its assessment. He added that Meta has written to the government expressing regret over the incident and explaining its understanding of the reasons behind it.

When asked about the timeline for Meta's representatives to appear before the government, he said, "I think within the next week, ten days. We are examining that. We have got the views of a number of the platforms, messaging platforms," he said.

World.title: 'Criticise govt, don't denigrate India': Harish Salve on dissent and social media
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Senior advocate Harish Salve on Wednesday said criticism aimed at "keep[ing] the government in control" is essential in a democracy, but urged people not to "denigrate India" in today's world of social media.

Speaking about the turmoil in the Western world, particularly in Europe, the former solicitor general said that despite its internal challenges, the West remains united in resisting India's rise, which he said it still views as "a third-world country".

"Trenchant criticisms within India of the government and its institutions is necessary to keep the government in control. But we should be very careful. Whatever we say, whatever we do in today's world of social media, do not denigrate India as a nation.

Always remember, 'Sare Jahan Se Achcha Hindustan Humara'," Salve was quoted as saying by the news agency ANI.

Speaking at the AK Sen Memorial Lecture and Photograph Unveiling Ceremony organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), Salve said holding those in power accountable is necessary in a constitutional democracy.

"One thing, as someone who resides outside India, is that India today is looked at with a great sense of respect.





The Western world is in turmoil as we see every day. Europe feels orphaned. US is making people wonder whether it ever had a Constitution. But they unite when it comes to resisting India's ascent. They still find it hard to accept that a country of not white people, a country which they call a third-world country, is aspiring to be a leader of the world, has become the fourth largest economy in the world," Salve was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.

The event marked the unveiling of a portrait of late Senior Advocate and former Union law minister AK Sen in Library No. 1 of the Supreme Court. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant joined Salve in unveiling the photograph.

Several senior members of the legal fraternity attended the ceremony. SCBA President and Senior Advocate Vikas Singh paid tribute to Sen's contribution to the legal profession, while Attorney General for India R.

Venkataramani also spoke about his legacy.

Addressing the gathering, Chief Justice Surya Kant described Sen as a distinguished lawyer, scholar and statesman whose career reflected a lifelong commitment to justice and public service. He said the portrait would honour Sen's contribution while inspiring future generations of advocates.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Today, we are not merely adorning our Library with a fitting tribute; we are enshrining in these walls the spirit of a life devoted to justice, intellect and public service...

For every Advocate who passes through the Library, this portrait would be a silent reminder that our calling transcends personal ambition, that the practice of law and the stewardship of justice are sacred trusts in service of the Republic," the Chief Justice said.

He added that the portrait should remind young lawyers of the values expected from members of the legal profession.

"A young lawyer rushing to Court with a first brief may pass this portrait. I hope the portrait will ask the more important questions that Mr Sen no doubt asked himself sometimes: Have I prepared enough? Have I been fair to the Court and to my opponent? Have I used the law to clarify, or merely to complicate?... May his presence here remind us that brilliance without balance is incomplete; that office without service is transient; and that law without humanity is barren," the Chief Justice said.

World.title: 'Proud of railways, want to be proud of govt promises too': Sonam Wangchuk hints at pending govt assurances
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Scientist and climate activist

on Thursday praised the

but took a veiled swipe at the Centre, urging it to honour the commitments made to students during the Jantar Mantar protest.

Sharing a video on social media, Wangchuk wrote, "m proud of Indian Railways. Want to be proud of Indian (govt) promises too."

In the video, Wangchuk described the railways as his favourite mode of transport and said he would travel to Ladakh by train. He also praised the Vande Bharat service between Delhi and Srinagar, calling it a pleasant journey.

Referring to the ongoing debate in Parliament over the NEET-UG paper leak, Wangchuk welcomed the discussion and urged the government to fulfil the written assurances it had given to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student protesters.

"Do not file FIRs and honour the trust of the youth," he said, urging the government to fulfil the commitments it had made to the student protesters.

Earlier this week, Wangchuk paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat before leaving for Ladakh. Addressing reporters, he said the movement had once again proved the relevance of Gandhi's philosophy of non-violent resistance.

Congratulating the organisers and participants, Wangchuk said the agitation succeeded because it remained peaceful despite police action.





The activist was discharged from Gurugram's Medanta Hospital on Monday after being shifted there from Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on court orders. He had been admitted to Safdarjung Hospital on July 18 after being taken there by police.

World.title: Ethanol blending rolled out through phased, scientific process: Gadkari to Lok Sabha
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Petroleum ministry has introduced the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme through a âphased, scientifically validated and consultative processâ, road transport minister

informed Lok Sabha on Thursday. He added that the ethanol blending has been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after creating the necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework.

In response to a question, the minister said, âThe transition to E20 was undertaken only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, material compatibility, emissions performance and consumer acceptance.â He added that the E20 programme has been developed through an extensive consultative and phased implementation process. Automobile manufacturers, component manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, vehicle testing agencies, Oil Marketing Companies, ethanol producers, sugar and grain industries and other stakeholders were associated at every stage of policy formulation and implementation.

He said laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not established adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. âThis is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending,â Gadkari said.





As per the reply, manufacturer service data have also confirmed that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 fuel, and automobile manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using specification-compliant E20 fuel. Recently, a major vehicle manufacturer had reported servicing 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025â26, including about 1.5 crore legacy vehicles, without finding any E20-linked engine damage, abnormal corrosion or reduction in component life.

A leading two-wheeler manufacturer has similarly reported no higher incidence of damage in E20-operated vehicles.

On the issue mileage loss, the reply said studies by govt agencies and automobile manufacturers indicate that reduction in fuel efficiency in certain E10-designed vehicles is limited to about 2-6%. However, this is influenced by several factors, including driving conditions, driving habits and vehicle maintenance.

The minister also said that public sector OMCs have informed that currently normal petrol sold at their retail outlets across the country is E20. âSince E0 or E10 petrol is not marketed at retail outlets, separate display of lower ethanol blends or printing of ethanol percentage on customer receipts has not been considered necessary,â he added.

On Wednesday, in a written reply to another question in Rajya Sabha, Gadkari had informed that BS-III vehicles, manufactured between 2005 and 2016, may require replacement of some rubber parts and gaskets when operated on E20 petrol, while adding studies have found no major impact of the blended fuel on overall vehicle performance.

The transition to E20 was undertaken only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, material compatibility, emissions performance and consumer acceptance. âThese studies confirmed that even legacy vehicles did not exhibit any significant variations in performance, nor do they show abnormal wear-and-tear when operated with E20 fuel. No issues were reported in parameters such as drivability, startability, metal compatibility, and plastic compatibility,â he had said.

World.title: 'Pellet guns can be used in exceptional situations': SC seeks RAF ammunition log from Jantar Mantar protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday observed that police are "empowered to use pellet guns in exceptional situations" while directing the Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) deployed at Jantar Mantar.

The court's observation comes at a time when allegations of pellet gun use against NEET protesters during the CJP-led student protest on July 20 have escalated into a political potboiler in Parliament.

A Bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed the Delhi government to provide adequate treatment to those protesters who were injured by alleged firing of pellet guns.

The bench also observed that when in extreme violent situations police are permitted to use bullets if violence does not get controlled by lathicharge and tear gas, how can they be barred from using pellet guns if a protest, which has turned violent after being hijacked by miscreants for ulterior purposes.

The court said all injured persons during protests should be given proper treatment.

The top court, however, questioned petitioner and ex-IPS offier Yashovardhan Azad for seeking ban on use of pellet guns against protesters.

Meanwhile, a CRPF post-event analysis has said that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun.





CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.

Moreover, CRPF director general G P Singh came forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties.

Addressing personnel at CRPF investiture ceremony coinciding with its Raising Day Monday, Singh said, "As DG of CRPF, I want to assure each one of you that whether it is an operational battalion or law-and-order unit, whatever decisions you carry out in the bona fide discharge of your duties and which are aligned with interests of the public, the force and the nation, I shall take responsibility for all those decisions and actions.

Continue to perform your duties fearlessly. Wherever responsibility or accountability needs to be taken, I will take as the director general".

World.title: 'Students deserve justice': Rahul Gandhi shares video claiming police brutality during NEET protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition

on Thursday demanded an independent Supreme Court-monitored high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police excesses against students protesting the perpetual paper leaks on July 20.

"Students deserve justice. An independent SC monitored high powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students," Rahul said in a post on X while sharing a video claiming police brutality during the protest.

The remarks came after Rahul had earlier accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of being responsible for the police's alleged excesses against protesters, including the reported firing incident.

Rahul demanded the removal of Union home minister Amit Shah and called for a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the alleged use of "lethal force" against student protesters, escalating the Opposition's attack on the government over the police crackdown.

Addressing the Lok Sabha, Rahul alleged that Shah either directly authorised the use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas against students, making him "culpable of brutalisation" of young protesters, or was unaware of the police action, which, he said, made him "incompetent."





"In either case, he has to go," Rahul said, urging Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove the senior minister from the Cabinet.

The allegations triggered strong protests from the treasury benches, with Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju demanding that Gandhi either substantiate his claims with evidence or apologise.

Rahul Gandhi also blamed RSS for what he described as the problems afflicting the education sector.

The government strongly objected to his remarks, with treasury bench members demanding that he either substantiate his allegations or apologise. They said Rahul Gandhi should not be allowed to continue his speech unless he provided evidence or expressed regret for the claims.

Union minister Jitendra Singh also said that orders for police firing are issued by a magistrate. Defending the Delhi Police, he said the force had exercised "utmost restraint" while handling the protesters' march on July 20, marking the first such defence by a senior government functionary.

World.title: Portion of Pune-Bengaluru national highway collapses near Belagavi
World.content:
A portion of the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway collapsed near Nippani on July 29. This led to panic among motorists.

The portion is part of the work of expanding the carriageway to a six-lane highway. The work has been going on for over two years now.

MLA Shashikala Jolle visited the site and expressed dissatisfaction with the quality of work. She promised to bring it to the attention of Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari. She demanded that the strip be rebuilt.

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) issued a clarification regarding the incident. Officials of the NHAI Regional Office stated that restoration work is being carried out on priority to repair the damaged embankment and resume construction on the carriageway.

Explanation by NHAI

The affected portion was an under-construction approach of a Light Vehicular Underpass (LVUP) on the Sankeshwar Bypass to the Maharashtra border section, near Nipani, on NH-48.

According to NHAI, the incident did not involve the main carriageway. The authority explained that the Pavement Quality Concrete (PQC) had not yet been laid, and the work was still at the sub-grade level, with only part of the Dry Lean Concrete (DLC) completed.

NHAI said that heavy rainfall caused water to flow through the unfinished sub-grade, resulting in the erosion of a 7–10 metre portion of the approach embankment.

The authority clarified that movement of vehicles was not affected, as motorists were already being diverted through the service road while the main carriageway was being constructed.

The clarification came after images of the collapsed side wall and eroded embankment at the construction site were shared by Belagavi resident Uday Kinjwadkar.

NHAI reiterated that the incident is confined to the under-construction approach embankment, and that there is no impact on movement of vehicles on the existing route.

World.title: T.N. government must create land banks to boost commercial real estate: experts
World.content:
While cities in Tamil Nadu are witnessing robust demand for commercial real estate, high land costs are constraining the supply of commercial spaces. To address this and sustain the momentum, the State government needs to create large land banks, speakers at the Real Estate and Urban Infrastructure Summit 2026, organised by The Hindu and held at ITC Grand Chola in the city on Thursday (July 30, 2026), said.

Discussing the topic, ‘The New Growth Triangle: Manufacturing, GCCs and Real Estate’, the speakers, however, pointed out that while there is no single solution to the land supply issue, Gujarat’s land pooling model and land leasing mechanisms could help overcome high land costs that dictate the supply of land for commercial real estate development.

Arun Prasad, Principal Architect, Arun & Associates, Coimbatore, said the State should follow the example of Gujarat, which has made land pooling a success. Mr. Prasad said that by pooling 1,000 to 2,000 acres of land from various landowners, Global Capability Centres (GCCs) have been created. The land pooling model has been a success because landowners retain ownership of their land even as development takes place, creating value for their property.

Julian Pradeep Francis, Associate Director, RMZ, wanted the State government to create large land parcels and give them on long-term lease to developers for commercial infrastructure development, which would pave the way for the city’s development. Mr. Pradeep said sustainable development has been ingrained in RMZ, which develops commercial real estate, and that it is slowly being adopted in the residential sector as well. He said that, with regard to GCCs, Pune and Gurgaon have already crossed the 100 million sq. ft. mark, while Chennai has slowed down.

Kanchana Krishnan, Commercial Head of ANAROCK, pointed out that the country has become a value creator as it has moved from business process outsourcing (BPO) centres to research and development (R&D) hubs. While Hyderabad and Bengaluru are doing well in terms of GCCs, Chennai continues to witness good supply in certain pockets. She said all the city’s extended areas are bound to witness significant commercial space development.

M. Sabareeswaran, Senior Vice President, Leasing Business Development, Casagrand Commercial, said integrated construction development, encompassing theme parks, malls and hotels, has been happening in China, and this needs to be replicated in all the cities of the State, including Tiruchi and Madurai. Mr. Sabareeswaran pointed out that Thoothukudi is emerging as a promising destination for the hospitality sector.

The talk was moderated by Soundariya Preetha, Deputy Chief of Bureau (Coimbatore), The Hindu. Ms. Preetha said Tirupur is an example of energy sustainability, where renewable energy generation far exceeds consumption and helps evacuate excess power to the State grid.

The Real Estate and Infrastructure Summit 2026 is presented by Casagrand in association with Adissia Developers. The event is supported by – Associate Partners: Navin’s and Mindspace REIT; Banking Partner: State Bank of India; Insurance Partner: United India Insurance; Academic Partner: Saveetha College of Architecture & Design; Industry Partner: CREDAI Chennai; Television Partner: Puthiya Thalaimurai; and Digital News Partner: The Federal.

World.title: Inside a Coimbatore co-working space with board games and a café
World.content:
In a quiet part of Tatabad, is a co-working space offering something different. We step into Sabol Co-Works on a busy workday as people are bent into their laptops. Opened a little over a year ago, the space, that can hold 54 desks, is the kind of place that can make a stressful day at work bearable, even fun.

“We’ve created a concept that we call WOCABO,” says Karthic Kumaran, who runs the place along with his mother Subashini Ramesh. The 26-year-old, who is also professional tennis player, explains that WO stands for work, CA for café, and BO for boardgames. “We have office spaces alongside a café and over 300 boardgames to choose from,” he explains.

The idea, says Karthic, is to show people that “working at a desk needn’t be stressful.” His father M Ramesh, who is also his mentor, explains that people can come in for a work meeting to their café and spend over an hour holding a casual meeting over a cup of coffee without the pressure of having a waiter looming over one’s shoulder.

Sabol’s office space has been done up aesthetically. Cubicles are not suffocating, grey spaces. At the ground floor for instance, there are outdoor and indoor meeting rooms with plenty of natural light. “Corporates make use of these rooms for Zoom meetings as well as interviews,” points out Karthic. The rooms can be booked on an hourly basis for ₹150, and Ramesh says that they can also be used as a podcast studio.

At present, Sabol Co-Works is being used by 15 MNCs, including start-ups, that take up the space for months together on contract. “People can choose to bring their laptops to work here for even a few hours or half-a-day,” says Karthic. There is complementary coffee and tea, not to mention printers, air-conditioning and internet. “They can also sit at our café space to work as well,” he adds.

The café, that is a little over four months old, features comfortable low benches and tables, perfect for working alongside a drink and a sandwich. There also is an outdoor seating arrangement nearby, that leads one into a room that features their boardgames collection. Even as the workaholics are consumed by work in their cubicles, Karthic picks a game for us to try at yet another meeting room that can double up a boardgaming lounge.

We play something simple to warm up, Flip 7 With a Vengeance, a card game. Karthic is a board gamer himself, and is clued in to all the trending games. “During weekends, we get plenty of serious board gamers who spend almost four hours playing as a community,” he says, adding that they also host children’s birthday parties for which he picks age-appropriate games.

“We have grandparents and grandchildren bonding over a boardgame; we’ve seen complete strangers turn friends over a game they just cannot stop playing,” he says. Their popular games include Blood on the Clocktower, Catan, Root, Merchant of The Dark Road, Brass: Birmingham, among others. “Several board gaming communities have held tournaments here,” he adds.

Karthic brings out another game called The Chameleon as the food arrives: the popular cookie milk and a paneer croissant sandwich, paired with the Thai raw papaya salad. The thoughtfully-curated menu features buns, sandwiches, and wraps, keeping in mind their customers who come for a quick meal as work plays on at the back of their mind. The cookie milk, the recipe Subashini came up with, reminds one of the summer holiday staple from the 90s: think cookies soaked in milk and whipped to a cold, smooth consistency. “This drink has become a crowd favourite,” says Subashini.

As Karthic explains the rules of the game, Ramesh recalls how when he was in his 20s, he started a similar space in RS Puram. “It was called Sabol Business Centre, and several companies, such as TCS and IFB had their offices in it,” recalls the 60-year-old. “This was around 1990, and telephone connections were in demand. We offered connections at the work desk, which was among our biggest draws,” he says. While they had to shut down as pagers and mobile phones took over the world, his son has visualised Sabol Co-Works as a place that will be in tune with the times. Why should work be confined to just one space?

For details, visit them on Instagram @wocabo_cbe, call 9344520266. Located at 65, 6th Street, Tatabad.

World.title: Ambedkar’s photo should be displayed prominently at Ripon Building: VCK Councillor
World.content:
Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) councillor G. Gopinath on Wednesday (July 29, 2026), urged the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) to restore the photograph of B.R. Ambedkar to a prominent position in the Council Hall at Ripon Buildings.

He said the the photograph of current Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and former CM M.K. Stalin were accommodated over the Mayor and Commissioner’s chairs, and the photos of Thiruvalluvar and Ambedkar were shifted to the opposite wall.

He requested that they be placed next to the photograph of Mahatma Gandhi above the Mayor’s chair. Mayor R. Priya responded that the Council Hall had limited wall space, and the GCC would examine the feasibility of his request.

World.title: Chennai Corporation councillors accuse Tamil Nadu government of denying their rights
World.content:
Councillors of the DMK-led Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) Council alleged at the Council meeting on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) that the State government was denying the elected representatives of the city’s local administration their rights.

At the meeting, Egmore DMK councillor Parithi Elamsurithi, AIADMK councillor T. Sathyanathan, and BJP councillor Uma Anandan urged Mayor R. Priya to press the Tamil Nadu government for release of ward development funds (₹60 lakh a year for each Greater Chennai Corporation councillor). They alleged that the funds had not been released even after the Model Code of Conduct was lifted after the Assembly poll.

Chennai Mayor R. Priya said there had been a delay in releasing the funds and that a request had been submitted to the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department.

Both Deputy Mayor M. Magesh Kumaar and Ms. Anandan pointed out that the urban local body elections were seven months away, and only if the funds were allocated in the next few months could they be earmarked for a project, receive administrative sanction, float tenders and issue a work order. Many councillors of the AIADMK, VCK, CPI, and CPI (M) also supported this demand during the Zero Hour.

GCC Commissioner G.S.Sameeran said the ward development funds of ₹60 lakh a year for each councillor was drawn from GCC’s capital funds.

He explained about the civic body’s ₹1,970-crore deficit apart from loans, pending bills worth ₹2,000 crore to contractors, and payment dues for NULM workers. This situation can be improved by stepping up property tax collection, and regulating underassessed properties, he added.

Taking additional loans, apart from municipal bonds, could affect the Corporation’s credit rating. A decision on releasing the ward development funds would be taken after discussions with the Mayor, he said.

Following complaints about lack of official coordination with elected representatives of Chennai Corporation, Mayor R. Priya said the councillors and ward committee chairpersons must also be invited to inauguration of projects in their respective wards. Politics and administration are different, she noted.

The remarks came after Ward 99 (Egmore) councillor Parithi Elamsuruthi of the DMK raised concerns over councillors being left out of such events.

Anna Nagar Zone Ward Committee Chairperson K.P. Jain said neither he nor the ward councillor had been invited to the inauguration of the recently renovated Bougainvillaea Park by Revenue and Disaster Management Minister K A. Sengottaiyan.

Following this, Mayor R. Priya said councillors had also not been invited to Greater Chennai Corporation polio immunisation events. She asked Commissioner G.S. Sameeran to issue zone-wise circular directing officials to coordinate with councillors and committee chairpersons.

Valasaravakkam Zone Chairperson V. Rajan alleged that GCC officials were not participating in ward committee meetings even after the meetings were scheduled at a time after consulting with the authorities.

Further, many unsafe illegal banners are being erected by the elected representatives of the State government, which needs to be inspected and curbed, the Mayor said.

World.title: Karnataka getting ready for Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s possible visit
World.content:
The Karnataka government is expecting Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to arrive in Bengaluru on August 3 for holding consultations on the Cauvery issue, although there is no official confirmation on it yet.

While Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar told presspersons in New Delhi on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) that Mr. Vijay has expressed his intention to meet him, Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister may visit Bengaluru on August 3, adding a rider that the schedule was yet to be confirmed.

Mr. Shivakumar said, “Mr. Vijay has written to the Karnataka Chief Secretary and has also spoken to me over phone. I have extended him the respect he deserves and invited him to the meeting in Bengaluru. It is our duty to receive guests visiting our State with due courtesy, and all necessary arrangements have been made to receive him.”

Visiting Cauvery basin

Mr. Shivakumar said he had requested Mr. Vijay to personally see the situation in the Cauvery basin of Karnataka that is reeling under drought. “I have also informed him that the government will make the necessary arrangements for his aerial visit to see the situation. He should witness the ground realities,” he said.

Mr. Vijay’s proposed visit comes at a time when Karnataka’s Cauvery basin is witnessing protests by farmers groups over the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s order to the State to release water to Tamil Nadu.

World.title: High prices dent gold demand in India, volume falls 6%, value rises 50% in April-June quarter: WGC
World.content:
Owing to high gold prices and excess volatility witnessed in the past months following the West Asia conflict, the overall demand for gold in India dropped 6% YoY to 131.4 tonnes in the April-June 2026 quarter from 139.7 tonnes in the year-ago period as per data released by World Gold Council (WGC).

India’s gold demand value for the quarter was ₹1,98,100 crore, up by 50% as compared to ₹132,500 crore in the year-ago period. Total Jewellery demand in India for the quarter decreased by 15% to 75.1 tonnes as compared to 88.8 tonnes a year ago.

However, the value of jewellery demand increased to ₹113,210 crore, compared to ₹84,200 crore a year ago, as per WGC. Total Bar and Coin demand increased 9% YoY to 50.3 tonnes and in value term it was 73% more at ₹75,750 crore.

As per WGC data total gold ETF demand for the quarter was at 4.2 tonnes, up 49% YoY. In value terms, gold ETF demand was ₹6,300 crore, up by 136% YoY.

Total gold recycled in India during the quarter was down 17% YoY to 19.2 tonnes. Also, total gold imports reduced by 23% YoY to 98.1 tonnes.

US$/oz average quarterly price for the quarter was $4,506.3 in comparison to $3,280.4 in the year-ago period. INR/10g average quarterly price for the quarter was ₹1,50,744.8 in comparison to ₹94,875.9 a year ago (without import duty and GST).

Sachin Jain, Regional CEO, India, World Gold Council said the highlights that consumers continue to prioritise gold even in a high-price environment.

“They are adapting their purchasing decisions to balance affordability with long-term value. This shift was particularly evident in the jewellery market. Although volumes declined to around 75 tonnes, jewellery demand in value terms grew 34% to ₹1,13,210 crores, supported by seasonal buying during festivals like Akshaya Tritiya, Gudi Padwa etc,” he said.

He said consumers are choosing lighter-weight and lower-carat jewellery, while increasingly leveraging exchange programmes to optimise their purchases.

Stating that investment demand remained encouraging, he said bar and coin demand grew 9% year-on-year to 50.3 tonnes, while Indian Gold ETFs attracted 4.2 tonnes of net inflows despite global outflows.

“These trends reinforce gold’s growing appeal not only as a traditional store of wealth but also as a strategic investment that provides stability and diversification in an increasingly uncertain economic environment,” Mr. Jain emphasised.

As per WGC’s forecast festive and wedding season in second half of this year is expected to support demand.

“While elevated prices may continue to influence buying patterns, Indian consumers have consistently demonstrated their ability to adapt,” Mr. Jain said.

“We expect gold to remain firmly embedded in household savings and investment decisions, underpinned by its enduring role as a trusted store of value and a source of financial resilience. We estimate full year demand to be in the range of 650-750 tonnes,” he added.

Globally total gold demand in the April-June 2026 quarter remained flat year-on-year (YoY) at 1,269 tonnes as the gold price eased from the record highs seen at the start of 2026.

This pushed demand for H1 2% higher YoY to an estimated 2,522 tonnes worth $380 billion.

Investment in gold ETFs, bars and coins dropped to 262 tonnes in the quarter as the lower gold price tempered the strong momentum seen earlier in the year, WGC said.

The decline was primarily driven by 45 tonnes of outflows from gold-backed ETFs in the quarter although first-half ETF demand remained modestly positive at 18 tonnes.

Bar and coin investment was relatively stable, down 3% YoY, while first-half demand was still 21% higher than at this point last year, supported by an ‘exceptional’ first quarter.

The WGC’s Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey showed that 45% of respondents intend to increase their own gold reserves over the next 12 months, highlighting gold’s enduring importance in official reserves.

Globally high prices continued to weigh on jewellery demand in the quarter, which fell 17% YoY as consumers bought less gold and shifted towards lighter products, WGC said.

World.title: American Red Cross declares second national blood crisis in history as type O positive supply drops below one day
World.content:
The American Red Cross declared a critical US blood supply shortage—only the second time in its 150-year history—after levels dropped by 25% in a single month. (File Photo/Canva)

The American Red Cross, for the second time in its history, declared a blood supply “crisis” in the United States, citing a sharp decline in donation levels.

“We’re facing a national blood crisis — only the second one in our organisation’s history. Blood donations have fallen to a four-year summer low, pushing an already strained blood supply to a critical level,” the non-profit humanitarian and disaster-relief agency said in a post on X.

It further issued an urgent appeal for blood donors to step up and help patients “counting on lifesaving blood for emergency surgeries, trauma care, cancer treatment, and other serious medical needs.”

World.title: Insurer denies accident claim over ‘hidden’ hypertension, man gets Rs 9 lakh payout
World.content:
Holding that an accident-related health insurance claim cannot be rejected on the basis of an alleged pre-existing condition unrelated to the treatment, a Punjab consumer forum has directed an insurance company to reimburse Rs 8.88 lakh with interest and pay Rs 30,000 as compensation and litigation costs to a complainant.

President Dr Harveen Bhardwaj and member Jyotsna of the Jalandhar District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission were hearing Rajinder Saini’s plea against the insurer’s rejection of reimbursement claims and cancellation of his family floater policy over the alleged concealment of his wife’s pre-existing hypertension.

“The opposite party (Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company) has failed to prove the nexus of the disease regarding which claim was lodged with the hypertension and the intentional suppression of the pre-existing disease as alleged, amounting to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The complainant, on the other hand, has paid the premium and complied with the policy conditions; thus, he cannot be deprived of the reimbursement on flimsy grounds,” the commission said on July 22.

The dispute stemmed from a March 2023 road accident in which Saini and his wife were injured. After his wife died, the insurer rejected reimbursement claims over an alleged undisclosed pre-existing condition, but the commission found no nexus between it and the accident-related treatment.

According to the complaint, Saini had purchased a Family Floater Arogya Plus health insurance policy after paying a premium of Rs 21,835. The policy, carrying a sum insured of Rs 7.5 lakh, was valid from March 26, 2022, to March 25, 2023, and covered him, his wife Pinki Saini and other family members.

On March 4, 2023, the couple met with a road accident and suffered injuries. Saini was treated at Joshi Hospital, Jalandhar, while his wife, who was critically injured, was shifted to Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, Ludhiana, before undergoing further treatment at Satyam Hospital Trauma Care Centre, Jalandhar. According to the complaint, the family spent Rs 8,88,014 on her treatment before she succumbed to the injuries on May 15, 2023.

After the treatment, Saini submitted reimbursement claims for himself and his wife. However, the insurer rejected both claims and also cancelled the policy, alleging suppression of material facts.



‘History of hypertension, stroke’

The insurer argued that medical records showed Pinki Saini allegedly had a history of hypertension before the policy was purchased and that this had not been disclosed in the proposal form.

It also claimed she had suffered a cerebrovascular accident (stroke) before obtaining the insurance policy. According to the insurer, this alleged non-disclosure entitled it to reject the claims and cancel the policy.

Saini denied intentionally concealing any medical history and contended that the claims arose solely because of the injuries suffered in the road accident. He argued that even if the insurer’s allegations regarding hypertension were accepted, the condition had no connection with the treatment for which reimbursement was sought.

No link to accident: Forum

After examining the evidence, the commission held that the insurer failed to prove that the alleged hypertension had any link to the accident injuries or the treatment for which reimbursement was claimed.



It noted that the hospital records relating to the accident did not establish that hypertension contributed to the hospitalisation. The commission also found that the insurer had not produced sufficient evidence to prove fraudulent suppression of facts. It reiterated that in accident-related claims, rejection cannot be based just on an unrelated pre-existing ailment without establishing a direct connection to the claim.

Referring to earlier consumer forum decisions, the commission observed that common lifestyle conditions cannot automatically serve as grounds for denying insurance benefits when they have no bearing on the cause of treatment.

Partly allowing the complaint, the commission directed the insurer to reimburse Rs 8,88,014 with 6 per cent annual interest from the date the claim was lodged until its realisation. It also awarded Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses, directing compliance within 45 days.

The commission, however, did not grant all his prayers, including those relating to the cancellation and renewal of the health insurance policy.



Consumer takeaway

The order highlights that health insurers cannot reject accident-related claims merely by alleging a pre-existing illness. They must prove a direct link between the condition and the treatment, and consumers can challenge arbitrary claim rejections before consumer commissions.

For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and Union territories (Punjab: 0800-22577) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.

World.title: Sobhita Dhulipala transforms into a ‘Devi’ as she closes Rahul Mishra’s ICW 2026 show
World.content:
When fashion transcends fabric and becomes storytelling, it leaves behind moments that are remembered long after the runway lights dim. At the grand finale of India Couture Week 2026 (ICW), actor Sobhita Dhulipala delivered exactly that kind of unforgettable moment as she closed Rahul Mishra’s show, not merely as a showstopper, but as the embodiment of a divine force.

The actor underwent a dramatic live transformation on the runway, gradually evolving into a ‘Devi’ as the audience watched in awe. The theatrical presentation wasn’t simply about showcasing couture; it celebrated India’s rich artistic heritage through fashion, movement and symbolism.

Sobhita Dhulipala at ICW 2026 (Photo: PR handout) Sobhita Dhulipala at ICW 2026 (Photo: PR handout)

More than a runway walk

Unlike conventional fashion finales, Sobhita’s appearance unfolded like a visual narrative. Beginning in a restrained silhouette, her look evolved on stage with sculptural elements and ceremonial styling that transformed her into a goddess-like figure.

World.title: Neeraj Chopra CWG Javelin Throw Qualification LIVE: Indian star set for his first throw
World.content:
Neeraj Chopra is waiting for his turn in the qualification round as the Indian looks to qualify for the medal round on Friday. Alongside Neeraj, India have two more athletes in Rohit Yadav and Yashvir Singh in the fray.

All three will be up against reigning Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem of Pakistan and Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage of Sri Lanka in a marquee men’s javelin clash as India seek to better last edition’s medal haul in Commonwealth Games athletics events.



A lower back injury has been troubling Chopra since September 2025 and he made a delayed start to the season at Doha Diamond League on June 19. He finished fourth with a throw of 85.69m — a modest one by his high standards.

World.title: Ranbir Kapoor responds to criticism over Lord Ram casting in Ramayana: ‘No right actor’
World.content:
After months of anticipation, the trailer of Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana: Part 1 is finally out. As expected, the ambitious adaptation has sparked mixed reactions online. While many have praised its scale and visual ambition, others have criticised several aspects of the film, with much of the debate centring on Ranbir Kapoor’s portrayal of Lord Rama. A section of social media users has argued that the actor is a misfit for the role, questioning the casting choice.

Amid the online criticism, Ranbir recently addressed the debate while promoting Ramayana at San Diego Comic-Con alongside director Nitesh Tiwari, producer Namit Malhotra and co-star Yash. Reflecting on the responsibility of portraying one of most revered deities, the actor said he believes there can never be one definitive choice to play Lord Rama. During a conversation with Review Nation, Ranbir opened up about the criticism he has faced, admitting that he initially questioned whether he was worthy of taking on the role.

“The first question that popped into my head was, am I worthy? Am I the right person and why am I being gifted this responsibility to not play Lord Rama but represent him? But very soon you understand the value, the responsibility and the noble intention of the filmmakers to present the story, which has been relevant for 4,000 years. It’s deeply ingrained in our subconscious. So I don’t think there’s a right actor to play Lord Rama.”



The actor further said that every devotee has their own image of Lord Rama, making it impossible for any one actor to satisfy everyone’s expectations. According to him, what matters most is the sincerity and faith with which the role is approached. “All the people who have watched Ramayana, they all have their own interpretation of Lord Ram. There is no fixed face to it. Many people will probably feel like I am the wrong casting. Some people will say I am the right casting. But the honest truth is that the right casting for Ram would be any actor who has the right intentions and who has belief and faith in the journey of Lord Ram.”

Yash, who plays Ravana in the film, also praised Ranbir’s performance during the same interview. Calling the role one of the most challenging an actor can undertake, he said: “It’s not easy to play Lord Ram. The way Ranbir Kapoor has done it is marvellous. He has worked incredibly hard, and when you watch Ramayana, you’ll witness a beautiful portrayal of Rama filled with intent and sacrifice.”



Social media divided over Ranbir’s casting

Ever since the trailer was unveiled, Ranbir’s casting has remained one of the biggest talking points on social media, with several users expressing reservations about him portraying Lord Rama. One user wrote, “Although I love Ranbir Kapoor and admire his work but seeing him as Shri Ram just feels too odd. Can’t picture him in that role, and even hearing him speak fluent hindi in this character feels off. Maybe they should’ve cast someone whose screen presence naturally fits the image of Shri Ram.”

Another commented, “I had doubts about Ranbir’s Hindi even before any Ramayana asset got released. He is very good for urban roles but in these roles, he feels like a miscast.”

Also Read | The women of Omkara make it the crown jewel of Vishal Bhardwaj’s Shakespeare trilogy

Playing both Lord Rama and Parshurama

Interestingly, Ramayana will see Ranbir in a double role. Apart from portraying Lord Rama, he will also essay Lord Parshurama in Nitesh Tiwari’s two-part epic. Speaking to Collider about taking on both characters, Ranbir said he relied on their distinct emotional and spiritual identities, along with differences in body language and voice, to portray them.



“Lord Vishnu had different avatars. Lord Rama was an avatar, and Lord Parshurama was an avatar before Lord Rama. Just to get the opportunity, you know, how I got to play Lord Rama, to also play Lord Parshurama was fantastic. I think as an actor, apart from body language, I think if you deeply understand the spirituality and the emotionality of the characters, I think everything starts from there. I think that’s what I did the year leading up to the shoot of Ramayana, to understand who these people and characters are, what they stand for and what their motives are.”

Ramayana is planned as a two-part epic, with the first instalment scheduled to release on Diwali 2026. The film also stars Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Sunny Deol as Hanuman.

World.title: What Chinese AI model Kimi’s success says about the next phase of US-China AI race
World.content:
In January 2025, the release of a Chinese artificial intelligence model called DeepSeek R1 drew global attention and briefly triggered market panic. It was a low-cost, quality product that was compared to ChatGPT and other top models from the United States as discussions about AI-related overspending were gaining ground.

DeepSeek also evoked curiosity and questions — just how capable is China’s AI sector? In parallel, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, accused DeepSeek of copying its technology, with a Trump administration adviser backing the claim.

A similar sequence of events seems to be playing out now. Chinese company Moonshot AI released its Kimi K3 model earlier this month, said to rival models from US-based companies OpenAI and Anthropic. It boasts features including coding, financial consulting, deep research, and video editing, and as demand surged, Moonshot AI paused sign-ups.

Alongside its rise, Anthropic has accused Moonshot AI of illicitly extracting the capabilities of its Claude model, with one US government official describing it as “an assault on every economy that prizes the entrepreneur, rewards private capital, and relies on fair and honest competition.” On Monday (July 27), China’s Commerce Ministry accused the US of “AI hegemonism” in response.

“Markets react strongly when a Chinese release challenges assumptions about permanent US technological leadership. Another sell-off is certainly possible,” said Lizzi C Lee, a Fellow on Chinese Economy at the US-based Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis. But more than just being good, the Kimi story shows that Chinese models are now becoming more ubiquitous, she said.

What Kimi K3 represents

Moonshot AI was founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, a 34-year-old entrepreneur who graduated from Beijing’s Tsinghua University and earned his PhD at Carnegie Mellon University in the US. He worked with American tech companies before returning to China.

Kimi K3 has been billed as the world’s largest “open-weight” AI system, with 2.8 trillion “parameters”. In the AI context, parameters are the settings that determine how systems respond to user prompts, based on the large amounts of data they have been trained on. Parameters are assigned “weights” or numerical values that indicate their relative significance, which guide the model’s response.



Lee said that a massive parameter count indicates large investment in compute (software and hardware used for training and running AI systems), data and engineering. But the model’s capability also depends on factors like data quality.

Poe Zhao, a China Tech Analyst and Founder of the online publication Hello China Tech, explained that “An open-weight model allows developers to download its parameters, run it locally and customise it. Open source usually implies broader disclosure, including enough code and training information to understand and modify how the model was produced.”

A worker stands at the booth for Chinese AI Startup Moonshot’s Kimi K3 during the World AI Conference in Shanghai, China on July 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Ng Han Guan) A worker stands at the booth for Chinese AI Startup Moonshot’s Kimi K3 during the World AI Conference in Shanghai, China on July 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Ng Han Guan)

Conceptually, “open-source” is not limited to AI. It simply means that the underlying code behind software and programs is publicly shared so anyone can use and modify it to create their own programs. Openness is often seen as a way to democratise technology, but has also drawn counterarguments, especially on malicious actors manipulating code and posing security risks.

The open-close debate
